I have built custom AI workflows for our exact tasks: one for product pages, one for category pages, one for buying guides, one for SEO. They produce the first draft. Your job is the judgement between the AI and the live website. You brief the workflow properly, read what comes back, check every fact against the manufacturer manual, fix what is weak, and publish it correctly. Some days that means rewriting half of what the AI produced. Some days it means catching one wrong number that would have cost us a sale. If you are a strong writer who wants to create everything from a blank page, you will find this constraining. If you are a careful person who enjoys taking a rough draft and making it correct, clear and genuinely useful to a buyer, this is a good fit. WHAT YOU GET, WHICH IS UNUSUAL FOR A VA ROLE A seat on my Claude team plan, paid by me. My custom AI workflows for every recurring task, so you are never writing prompts from scratch. Every project file we have: a full site audit, a six-month growth plan, a 118-keyword research map, and written content briefs. The manufacturer manuals, which are your source of truth. Written SOPs and checklists for every recurring task. And clear briefs, in which I name the target keyword, the page it belongs to, the internal links and the call to action. Most VA jobs hand you a vague goal and hope. This one hands you a system. Follow it precisely, and tell me where it is wrong. WHAT YOU WILL DO CONTENT AND SEO, 40% of your time. Produce category pages, product content blocks and buying guides using my workflows, then verify, edit and publish them. Write SEO titles under 60 characters and meta descriptions under 155 that actually earn a click. We currently have page-one rankings sitting at a 0.04% click rate, so fixing that is one of the highest-value things you will do. Build what a $9,000 buyer needs in order to d ---------- : specification tables, model comparisons, who this is for and who it is not for, room and doorway requirements, and honest FAQs. Add internal links from the map I give you. Track keyword positions in Google Search Console and tell me what moved. Our buyers research for weeks, so your writing has to answer real questions. Will this fit through my door. What is the difference between these two models. Why is one $8,999 and the other $26,999. Not brand storytelling. PRODUCT AND BRAND ONBOARDING, 15% of your time, starting month 2. When a supplier sends a price list and portal access, you take it from spreadsheet to live product pages. Work out what we are actually listing: models, variants, options, warranty terms and lead times. Pull the manufacturer manual and use it as the source of truth for every specification. Download the images and PDFs, rename them to our convention and compress them to WebP. Run my onboarding workflow to produce the pages and a Matrixify import CSV, then check every row before it goes near the store. Build the SKU structure correctly the first time, with unique codes, correct model prefixes and no duplicate variant sets. Flag every question the supplier still needs to answer. A brand onboarded properly takes a day. Onboarded carelessly it takes a week to fix six months later, and I know that because I am paying to fix it right now. This is also where our compliance risk is highest, because supplier marketing copy is full of health claims we cannot repeat. You are the filter. SHOPIFY CATALOGUE, 25% of your time. Fix SKUs and variants: some products have blank SKUs, some share one SKU across four variants, and some carry the wrong model code. Enforce one price per product everywhere it appears, on the product page, the collection cards, the comparison tables and the financing page. Fix product tags so items show up in the right collections and disappear from the wrong ones. Set up URL redirects and update the internal links that pointed at the old address. Run bulk edits with Matrixify or Shopify CSV. Paste HTML blocks into Shopify and test them at 375px width on a phone before you call them done. You do not need to be a developer. You need to read HTML, edit it without breaking it, and know why a wide table breaks on mobile. Claude will help you write it. Checking it is on you. KLAVIYO EMAIL MARKETING, 20% of your time. Build and edit flows: abandoned cart, browse abandonment, quote follow-up, post-purchase and review requests. Write, build and schedule campaign emails. Create and maintain segments. Edit templates, including light HTML. Report on opens, clicks and revenue after each send, in plain language. QUALITY CONTROL, 5% of your time, but it protects everything else. Every week, check that no price contradicts another anywhere on the site, and check for broken links and images. Every month, run a full price parity audit across every surface. HARD RULES, NOT NEGOTIABLE We sell wellness equipment, not medical treatment. Breaking these rules can get our ad accounts banned and create legal problems. This is the most important section in this post. RULE 1. Never publish a medical claim. Nothing that says a product treats, cures, heals or improves any condition. Never name a condition such as stroke, brain injury, PTSD, cancer, Lyme, autism, arthritis, long COVID, wound healing or inflammation. Not even if the manufacturer said it first. RULE 2. Never invent a fact. If a dimension, weight, pressure rating, certification or price is not in the manual or on the manufacturer website, write "needs verification" and flag it to me. Do not guess and do not let the AI guess. RULE 3. AI drafts, you verify. Claude will confidently produce specifications and prices that do not exist. Assume every number is wrong until you have seen it in a manual. RULE 4. Nothing publishes without the checklist. Every time, including when you are busy. The most common way people fail this role is not laziness. It is being helpful: adding a benefit the AI suggested because it makes the copy stronger. On our products that is the expensive mistake. WHAT YOU MUST ALREADY HAVE Hands-on Shopify admin experience, covering products, variants, tags, collections, metafields, redirects and SEO fields. Bulk editing with CSV or Matrixify, and the sense to spot a broken row before you import it into a live store. HTML and basic CSS, enough to read a block, change it safely and understand mobile behaviour. Klaviyo, building flows and segments from scratch rather than just pressing send. Daily use of Claude or ChatGPT, with a clear answer for how you check their output. Tidy file handling: renaming to a convention, WebP compression, folders someone else could navigate. And plain written English at a grade 7 to 9 reading level, short sentences and no filler. I will judge that last one from your application, so please write it yourself. Nice to have but not required: Google Search Console, Semrush, Merchant Center, ---------- , previous supplier catalogue onboarding from a price list rather than finished copy, or any exposure to outreach, link building and short-form video. WHY THIS ROLE COVERS SO MUCH GROUND A lot of operational marketing work is being commoditised by AI. Building a product page, drafting a campaign, cutting a short video, writing outreach: the mechanics are no longer the hard part, because good systems and good tools now do the first 80% of each one. What has not been commoditised is judgement. Knowing what is worth doing, noticing when the output is wrong, and caring whether it is accurate. That is what I am hiring for, and it is the part that transfers between channels. Five years ago this would have been four separate jobs. Today one capable person with the right systems can run all of it, and be paid better than any one of those four jobs paid on its own. That is the bet I am making, and it is why this role is built to expand rather than to specialise. WHERE THIS ROLE GOES MONTHS 1 TO 3, EXECUTION. The work described above. You learn our products, our rules and our systems. MONTHS 3 TO 9, CHANNEL SPECIALISMS. Added one at a time, never all at once, and only once the previous one runs without me. Content marketing, meaning you own the editorial calendar and produce and publish against it. Email marketing, meaning you own Klaviyo outright, including campaigns, segmentation and revenue reporting. Social media and video, meaning short-form cut from manufacturer footage, YouTube uploads and light community management. Then link building and digital PR, meaning prospecting, outreach, follow-up and tracking placements. MONTHS 9 AND BEYOND, MANAGEMENT, IF THE BUSINESS GROWS INTO IT. I will be straight with you. This depends on revenue, not on goodwill. If the plan works, the next hires are a second VA and a freelance video editor, and you would brief and review their work instead of doing all of it yourself. Marketing manager in function, whatever we end up calling it. If growth is slower than planned, this stays a strong specialist role and your pay still rises with your skill. I would rather tell you that now than imply a promotion I cannot guarantee. HOW YOU ACTUALLY PICK UP THE SKILLS Most job posts leave this vague, so here is the exact method. First, I write the guideline or SOP before you are asked to do the task. Second, we do the first one together on a call with my screen shared, so you see the reasoning and not just the steps. Third, you do the next two with me reviewing before anything publishes. Fourth, it is yours, and your job becomes telling me where the system is clumsy so we can fix it together. You get a Claude seat and I pay for any course or tool that makes you better at this. Time spent learning is part of your paid hours. It is not something you do in your own evenings. I would rather pay for a week of you getting properly good at something than have you fake it for six months. Willingness to learn a new tool every few months matters more to me than knowing everything today. I am looking for someone to stay for years. PAY AND GROWTH This starts as a paid project with a defined scope, so we both find out quickly whether it fits. If it goes well it becomes ongoing part-time, then full-time, with a review at 90 days. Pay rises as the scope grows: link building, then social and video, then channel ownership each move the rate, and I will tell you in advance what has to be true for that to happen. I pay for the tools and the training. HOW WE WORK I give you written briefs, so ask your questions before you start rather than after you finish. Send me a short end-of-day update covering what you finished, what is blocked and what is next. Three lines is enough. All work is tracked in a shared spreadsheet I provide. If my brief looks wrong, stop and tell me, because catching my mistakes is part of the job and I will say thank you. We talk on [SLACK / WHATSAPP / SKYPE] and use Loom for anything complicated. HOW TO APPLY Applications that skip these steps will not be read. I reply to everyone who follows them. This should take about ten minutes. Use AI to help if you want. I do not mind, and I would rather see how you work with it than watch you pretend you do not. STEP 1. Your subject line, or the first line of your message if there is no subject field, must read as follows. Hyperbaric VA - [your first name] - [the one duty in this post you would be weakest at] Yes, really. Look back at the five areas under WHAT YOU WILL DO and name the one you are least ready for. Nobody is strong at all five. I would rather know now than in month two, and naming it honestly counts in your favour. STEP 2. Answer these four questions briefly, in your own words. QUESTION 1. What is the most complex Shopify catalogue you have worked on, and how many products and variants did it have? QUESTION 2. Tell me about one time Claude or ChatGPT gave you information that turned out to be wrong. How did you catch it? QUESTION 3. A hyperbaric chamber weighs 88 lb, reaches 1.4 ATA and costs $8,999. Write one sentence for the product page that would help someone d ---------- whether to buy it. QUESTION 4. Which Klaviyo flows have you built from scratch, rather than just edited? STEP 3. Tell me your available hours in your local time. That is all I need to start. If we go further, I will ask for a short video and one screenshot of your own work, and then a paid test task before any interview.

description: Customer Service Representative – E-Commerce Full-Time | Remote We’re looking for a reliable, detail-oriented Customer Service Representative to support our growing e-commerce brands across Shopify, Amazon and TikTok Shop. Handle questions regarding products, orders, shipping, returns, refunds, exchanges, and replacements. Investigate customer issues and determine the appropriate resolution based on company policies. Monitor customer feedback and recurring concerns. Coordinate with the operations team when an issue requires additional investigation. Maintain a responsive and professional brand presence on the platform. Email Support Monitor shared customer service inboxes and respond within established response-time targets. Organize and prioritize incoming customer requests. Follow up on unresolved customer issues until they are fully addressed. Maintain clear and accurate communication across email threads. Identify messages requiring escalation and ensure they are routed to the appropriate team member. Reporting & Operations Maintain accurate records of customer issues, refunds, replacements, and escalations. Track recurring customer complaints and identify patterns or potential product issues. Prepare basic customer service reports and summaries when requested. Communicate important customer feedback to the operations, product, inventory, or management teams. Help improve customer service processes, templates, FAQs, and internal documentation. Identify opportunities to reduce repetitive customer inquiries through better processes and documentation. Qualifications Required Qualifications 2+ years of customer service experience, preferably supporting e-commerce businesses or online retail brands. Hands-on experience handling customer inquiries through email and/or e-commerce platforms. Strong written and verbal English communication skills. Experience handling orders, returns, refunds, replacements, cancellations, shipping issues, and product inquiries. Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to resolve customer concerns independently. Excellent attention to detail, particularly when reviewing order information, customer history, tracking details, and refund or replacement requests. Ability to manage multiple customer conversations and prioritize requests based on urgency and impact. Strong organizational and follow-up skills. Comfortable working with Shopify, Amazon Seller Central, TikTok Shop, or similar e-commerce platforms. Ability to follow company policies while using good judgment when determining the best solution for a customer. Professional and empathetic communication style, especially when handling frustrated or dissatisfied customers. Ability to work independently in a remote, fast-paced environment with minimal supervision. Comfortable learning new tools, systems, and processes quickly. Reliable internet connection and a suitable remote-work setup. Personal Attributes We're looking for someone who is: Customer-focused – genuinely wants to help customers while protecting the company's interests. Proactive – notices problems and takes action instead of waiting to be told what to do. Detail-oriented – catches small mistakes before they become bigger customer issues. Resourceful – knows how to investigate an issue and find the information needed to resolve it. Accountable – takes ownership of customer issues from start to finish. Adaptable – comfortable working across multiple platforms, brands, and processes. Calm under pressure – able to handle difficult customers professionally. A strong communicator – knows when to resolve an issue independently and when to escalate it. Why Join Us? Work directly with a founder and growing e-commerce team. Play an important role in the customer experience of our brands. Long-term opportunity with room for professional growth. Supportive and collaborative remote environment. Your ideas and initiative are valued. Opportunity to take ownership and improve systems rather than simply follow scripts. Application Questions To help us better understand your experience, please answer the following questions when you apply: Can you commit to working full-time, Monday–Friday, during our required working hours? Describe your internet speed and reliability. What backup plan do you have if your power or internet goes down during work hours? How many years of customer service experience do you have? How much of that experience involved e-commerce? Which platforms or tools have you personally used to provide customer support? Please indicate your level of hands-on experience with each: Shopify Amazon Seller Central TikTok Shop Email Gorgias Zendesk Freshdesk Help Scout Other Describe the customer service responsibilities you've personally handled. Please be specific about the types of customer issues, orders, and transactions you've managed. Have you personally handled refunds, returns, cancellations, replacements, damaged orders, missing packages, or shipping issues? Please describe your experience and the platforms you used. Tell us about a difficult or upset customer you handled. What was the situation, how did you respond, and what was the outcome? A customer sends the following email: "I've been waiting for my order for over a week and the tracking hasn't updated. This is ridiculous. I want my money back." Write the exact response you would send to the customer. Rate your hands-on experience from 1–10: Shopify Amazon Seller Central TikTok Shop Email Customer Service Google Sheets / Excel Written English Customer Complaint Resolution Give three specific examples that demonstrate your attention to detail in customer service. Tell us about a time you identified a customer or operational issue before anyone else noticed it. What did you notice, what action did you take, and what was the result? How do you prioritize your work when you have multiple customer conversations waiting across Shopify, Amazon, TikTok Shop, and email? A customer requests a refund or replacement that falls outside the company's standard policy. What would you do? How do you make sure your customer responses are personalized and helpful rather than sounding like generic templates? Have you ever helped improve a customer service process, SOP, FAQ, or response template? If yes, briefly describe what you changed and why. What are your long-term career goals, and what are you looking for in your next role? Please attach your resume and include a link to your LinkedIn profile.

You'll be the single owner: every dispute has one person accountable for it from the first alert to the final win/loss, plus the reporting that tells us where they came from. description: I'm the founder of a digital growth marketing company that helps mission-driven founders scale their businesses with more ease & less overwhelm - and I'm looking for a small team of highly-skilled Executive Assistants to help take over the marketing and management tasks that make a huge difference in the lives of the people that hire us. You've done it all from managing schedules to email & calendar management. You have a meticulous eye for detail where Prioritization and Organization are your love language -- 1+ years of experience in Sales Funnels and Shopify You're a professional who is passionate about helping changemakers simplify their lives by setting up systems that will allow them to operate their businesses with more ease and less overwhelm. You have experience with sales funnel and CRM software - 1+ years of experience advertising on platforms like Instagram, Facebook, Tik Tok, within a Marketing team consisting of Paid Acquisition, Organic Marketing, Customer Retention, & Product Marketing You're an emerging leader who has the potential to head a team in the future that will report directly to you. Having leadership experience is a MAJOR plus - Creating SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures) You’ll ensure each business function has detailed documentation for repeatable and scalable growth if it isn't already place. If you see gaps, you take the initiative to fill them and produce results without anyone knowing there was an issue (yea, all that and a bag of chips :-) - Experience working at a digital/online product/platform: You’re familiar with online courses, digital products & platforms and popular tools in the business space ranging from landing page builders and email service providers to CRMs, and course hosting platforms aren’t foreign to you (We teach tools like Shopify, Convertkit, Kajabi, Teachable, Learnworlds, Calendly, etc) ABOUT YOU: - “You down with SOP? Yeah you know me!”—You’re an advocate for SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures) to make our systems repeatable & scalable. - Your love language is processes & predictable, meteoric growth. We never question company progress towards the quarterly and yearly goals because you keep real-time metrics for all projects. - You’re aware of new software and can look at current systems and identify how to automate tasks a company has been doing manually for months. - You’re addicted to digital processes & automation in the world of social media because you love building connections in the digital space and you’ve seen how powerful it can be in business growth - You’re driven by metrics & tracking. You know that you can’t improve something unless you measure it, so you develop ways to measure performance so your company is always predictably improving. - Timeliness and deadlines are your jam. When we have a team call at 10:00am, you show up at 9:55am. When the deadline is Tuesday at 5:30pm, you have it done Monday. - You overcommunicate clearly and confidently. If you agree/disagree with something, you communicate that without hesitation or overthinking. You’re no stranger to asking why we do things a certain way to ensure we’re intentional with our resources. - You’re a leader and team player. Ego? What ego? Perks include: - Part time work hours - Work from anywhere in the world (as long as your internet signal is strong and computer is fast) - Starting Salary at $400-$500 USD a month ($4800-$6000 USD annual) - Internal certification program to enhance your professional skills in your career (I have helped clients amass at least $10M from the same digital growth marketing strategies I will require you to learn) Interested? title: Shopify Brand Operator (Full-Time , Remote , Philippines)
description: Job Overview - This is a process-driven e-commerce operator role focused on day-to-day Shopify D2C storefront execution and fulfillment operations across one or more consumer-product brands. The role is operational rather than strategic, with emphasis on structured workflows, recurring reporting, 3PL/supplier coordination, and early escalation of exceptions. What You Will Do? - Storefront Management: Maintain Shopify product listings, collections, variants, product descriptions, media assets, Metafields, and store navigation. - App & Tech Stack Maintenance: Monitor app integrations (subscriptions, upsells, reviews, inventory sync), store health, broken links, and checkout workflows. - Inventory & Fulfillment Ops: Track stock levels across warehouses/3PLs, monitor inbound supplier shipments, manage stockout risks, reorder points, and Shopify location inventory. - 3PL & Supplier Coordination: Coordinate with international suppliers, freight partners, 3PL fulfillment centers, and designers using approved templates. - Promotions & Site Updates: Setup and schedule discounts, automatic promo codes, landing pages, gift-with-purchase setups, and price adjustments. - Performance Monitoring: Track daily site revenue, conversion rate (CVR), average order value (AOV), refund/return rates, customer support tickets, and traffic trends. - Reporting & Documentation: Build clear weekly reporting inside Notion or Google Sheets. - Helpdesk & Issue Escalation: Create support cases with Shopify Support / app developers, document outcomes, and maintain task queues. - Competitor & Conversion Sourcing: Execute competitor CRO research and catalog optimization using approved tools and templates. - Flag Exceptions: Surface risks involving inventory shortages, 3PL delays, theme bugs, material supplier issues, or elevated refund trends early. What We Are Looking For? a. Required - Based in the Philippines and seeking a long-term remote role. - 2+ years of hands-on Shopify Admin & D2C E-Commerce experience. - Experience managing Shopify product catalogs, variants, collections, and order management workflows. - Familiarity with 3PL fulfillment operations, inventory tracking, and carrier shipping logistics. - Working knowledge of core D2C e-commerce metrics: CVR, AOV, ROAS, LTV, Refund Rate, and Traffic. - Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills. - Strong written English and professional supplier/partner communication. - Excellent attention to detail and ability to follow SOPs precisely. - Strong file organization, naming, documentation, and task-management habits. - Comfortable working in Notion, ClickUp, Asana, or similar tools. - Reliable internet, a suitable work computer, and dependable availability. b. Nice To Have - Experience with Shopify Theme Editors, PageFly, GemPages, or Shogun. - Experience with 3PL portals (Flexport, ShipBob, Stord, ShipMonk) or inventory management apps. - Experience managing subscription tools (Recharge, Seal) or customer service helpdesks (Gorgias, Zendesk). - Basic HTML/CSS knowledge or light Liquid troubleshooting skills.Basic image-editing, Canva, or Photoshop skills. - Experience coordinating international suppliers or freight forwarders via Alibaba/WhatsApp. c. This Role Is Not For You If... - You want to set brand strategy, select new products, or negotiate commercial terms independently. - You are uncomfortable following structured SOPs and approval rules. - You make pricing, inventory, supplier, or app subscription changes without confirming authority. - You dislike documentation, checklists, and recurring reporting. - You need frequent live supervision to complete routine work. - You plan to manage several competing full-time clients simultaneously. d. What Success Looks Like? - Shopify product pages, inventory levels, app setups, and weekly reporting are kept current without reminders. - Potential stockouts, 3PL delays, store bugs, and supplier issues are surfaced early. - Every operational task has a clean status, owner, documentation trail, and next action. - Escalations arrive with the problem, supporting data, a recommended action, and an alternative considered. - Operational consistency is maintained without making unapproved strategy changes independently. How To Apply? Please submit one application containing: - A short introduction describing your Shopify store management experience. - A list of the Shopify/ecommerce tasks you have personally owned. - The brand niches or markets you have worked in. - Your expected monthly salary in USD. Your current computer specifications. - Your internet-speed-test result. - A short Loom video, up to 3 minutes, walking through a Shopify operations workflow or 3PL/inventory process you have managed. - Two examples of Shopify-related work you can describe without sharing confidential client information. Required Qualifying Question: In 3–5 sentences, explain your exact process when you discover that a top-selling product on Shopify is at risk of going out of stock within 21 days across your 3PL warehouses. Applications that do not answer the qualifying question will not be considered.

title: Customer Service Agent | Ecommerce D2C
description: We're looking for a customer service agent who understands one thing clearly: A good reply doesn't just sound polite. It answers the real question, solves the problem before it grows, and turns a frustrated customer into one who orders again. We're a fast-growing e-commerce brand in the health and wellness space, selling products built to bring real comfort and relief to people dealing with everyday discomfort. We sell in the UK and the US, and we're scaling fast. Paid social is one of our main growth channels — which means most customers meet us through an ad, arrive with questions, and write to us before and after they buy. Support is not a cost center for us. It's one of the biggest drivers of trust, retention, and repeat revenue. We're looking for someone who can own that inbox — and who can do it using a modern, AI-driven workflow that lets us answer fast, absorb volume, and keep scaling without the quality dropping. This role is ideal for someone who understands e-commerce support, courier problems, refunds and disputes, AI-assisted workflows, and the difference between closing a ticket and keeping a customer. — WHAT YOU'LL BE HANDLING — You'll be working the inbox of a DTC brand running paid traffic, which means: — "Where is my order": stalled tracking, parcels stuck at a hub, deliveries marked complete but never received — Pre-purchase questions: people who saw the ad and want to know if it works and if we're real — Product questions: how to use it, what to expect and when, whether it's right for their situation — Sensitive cases: rare, handled carefully and escalated properly — Refunds, returns and cancellations: our guarantee, and knowing when to say yes — Disputes and chargebacks: PayPal and card cases, caught early enough to resolve instead of lose — Comments and DMs under our ads: public, and often a cold audience's first impression of us — Win-back conversations: the ones that turn a solved problem into another order — WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR — We're not looking for someone who writes beautiful, polite emails and nothing else. Anyone can do that now. AI made good prose free, which means good prose is no longer the job. We're looking for someone who works the ticket before writing it. You should: — Read the real carrier events, not the tracking link the customer already saw — Check whether this person wrote before, and what was promised last time — Notice the payment method — PayPal and card have different dispute clocks — Tell a policy abuser apart from someone genuinely upset and about to leave one star — Chase the courier yourself instead of telling the customer to keep waiting — D ---------- within your limits instead of escalating everything and slowing the queue — Close the conversation, so the same person doesn't write three more times You should be able to take a Shopify order, a tracking page that hasn't moved in five days and an angry customer, and turn it into a resolved ticket and a customer who stays. — HOW WE USE AI (AND HOW WE DON'T) — We assume you use AI. Everyone does, and we'd be concerned if you didn't. What matters is how. You should be confident in: — Drafting with it while holding one consistent tone across every reply — Building your own prompts, macros and saved replies, so the same answer isn't rewritten fifty times — Checking every fact first: AI invents shipping dates and policies, and the customer holds us to them — Knowing which tickets it never touches alone: legal threats, disputes, anyone on their third email — Spotting the answer that is technically correct and still wrong, because it missed the problem underneath — Keeping the result human: a reply that reads as generated costs more trust than a slower one would have If your workflow is pasting the customer's email into ChatGPT and sending back whatever comes out, this role isn't the right fit. — THE KIND OF PERSON WHO WILL THRIVE HERE — You'll be a strong fit if you: — Have handled real volume for an e-commerce brand, and know your daily ticket count — Know your own numbers: response time, refund rate, chargeback rate, contact rate — Are comfortable inside Shopify: orders, fulfillments, refunds, customer history — Know what macros, tags and SLAs are actually for — Chase people internally when something is stuck, without being asked twice — Write short: six clear lines beat three paragraphs — Stay calm with someone being unfair to you, and calm again the third time — Have judgment about money: a partial refund today often beats a chargeback next week — Notice patterns: thirty emails about one thing means something upstream is broken — Care whether the customer comes back, not just whether the ticket is closed We care about support that protects revenue. That doesn't mean saying no to customers. It means every reply — and every refund decision — should support the relationship, the trust, and the next order. — SKILLS & EXPERIENCE — Ideally, you have experience with: — Customer service for an e-commerce or DTC brand running paid social — Shopify: orders, refunds, fulfillments, customer history — A helpdesk: Gorgias, Zendesk, Freshdesk, Front, Intercom, or similar — Email, live chat, WhatsApp, and Instagram and Facebook ---------- and comments — Carrier tracking and claims, and dealing with couriers on missing parcels — Refunds, returns and cancellations, and the consumer rules that apply to them — PayPal and card disputes, resolved before they become chargebacks — ChatGPT, Claude, or an AI agent inside the helpdesk Bonus if you've worked with health, wellness, supplements or pain-relief brands, or with an audience that skews older. — WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING DAY TO DAY — — Answering emails inside our response time targets — Working each ticket properly: order, tracking, history and payment checked before you reply — Chasing couriers on stuck parcels, and d ---------- when to reship — Handling refunds, returns and cancellations within your limits — Catching disputes early, before they become chargebacks — Replying to comments and DMs under our ads, where a cold audience is watching — Improving macros, saved replies and prompts so the whole queue gets faster — Flagging patterns: the product page that causes tickets, the courier that keeps failing — WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU — — Competitive compensation based on experience — Performance-based bonuses tied to real numbers: response time, satisfaction, refund rate — Access to premium AI and support tools — fully covered by us — Owning the customer relationship for a brand that's scaling fast — Long-term growth with a fast-scaling D2C brand We're building a serious e-commerce brand, and we're looking for someone who knows that support is where trust is either built or lost — using both real judgment about customers and money, and the AI tools that make modern support possible at scale. If you're a customer service specialist who works the ticket AND lives in the AI workflow, we'd love to hear from you. — READY TO APPLY? — If this sounds like your kind of challenge, we'd love to hear from you. Apply here: ----------

job_title: Senior Financial Controller / Finance Manager |Multi-Store International E-Commerce | Remote
description: Senior Financial Controller / Finance Manager Multi-Store International E-Commerce | Remote We are a fast-growing international e-commerce company operating multiple Shopify stores across several countries and processing significant transaction volumes through multiple payment providers. We are looking for a highly capable Senior Financial Controller / Finance Manager to professionalize and take ownership of our finance function. This is NOT a junior bookkeeping position. We already have finance/accounting activities taking place inside the company. We need a senior finance professional who can ensure that our numbers are accurate, our controls are strong and management has reliable financial information for decision-making. Your Mission Build a finance function that the founder can trust. You will assess our current finance processes, identify weaknesses, improve controls and reporting, and oversee the people performing recurring finance work. Responsibilities * Own financial reporting and financial accuracy * Review and improve our current finance processes * Oversee bookkeeping and accounting workflows * Review reconciliations across banks and payment processors * Ensure Shopify/order data reconciles correctly with financial records * Monitor payment processor settlements and fees * Review supplier payments and COGS * Improve expense categorization and controls * Monitor refunds, chargebacks and payment-related losses * Produce reliable monthly P&L reporting * Produce consolidated and store-level management reporting * Develop cash-flow reporting and forecasting * Build budgets and forecasts * Identify unusual financial movements and discrepancies * Establish appropriate approval and financial control processes * Review the work of junior finance/accounting team members * Improve month-end closing procedures * Work with external accountants, tax advisers and other specialists where required * Help management understand profitability and financial performance * Identify opportunities for financial automation and better systems E-Commerce Complexity Experience with high-volume e-commerce is strongly preferred. Our environment may include: * Multiple Shopify stores * Multiple currencies * Multiple countries * Stripe * Shopify Payments * PayPal * Klarna and other payment methods * Refunds * Chargebacks * Supplier payments * Advertising spend * FX * Payment processor fees You should be comfortable reconciling complex transaction flows rather than only traditional invoice-based businesses. What We Are Looking For * Strong accounting/finance foundation * Significant experience in financial control, finance management or senior accounting * Excellent reconciliation skills * Strong management reporting ability * Experience creating or improving financial controls * Advanced Excel/Google Sheets skills * Experience with accounting software such as Xero or QuickBooks * High attention to detail * Strong analytical ability * Ability to investigate discrepancies independently * Ability to review and challenge the work of others * Strong written English CPA/ACCA/CIMA or comparable professional qualifications are highly valued but not automatically required if your experience is exceptional. What We Are NOT Looking For This is not suitable for someone whose experience is primarily: * Data entry * Basic bookkeeping * Accounts payable only * Virtual assistance * Producing reports without understanding the underlying numbers We need someone capable of owning and controlling a finance function, not simply processing transactions. What Success Looks Like Management can confidently answer: * How profitable are we? * Which stores are most profitable? * What is our real COGS? * Where is our cash? * What are our payment processor balances? * Are all transactions reconciled? * What are our major financial risks? * How are actual results performing against forecast? And most importantly: management can trust the answers. Application Please answer: 1. What is the largest company, measured by annual revenue or transaction volume, for which you have personally managed or controlled finance? 2. Describe the most complex reconciliation environment you have worked with. 3. Have you worked with Shopify, Stripe, PayPal or similar payment processors? Explain exactly what you were responsible for. 4. Tell us about a significant financial discrepancy or control problem you personally discovered. How did you find it and what happened? 5. Which financial reports did you personally prepare or review each month? 6. Have you managed or reviewed the work of other accountants/bookkeepers? How many? 7. Which accounting qualifications do you hold? 8. Which accounting systems are you strongest with? 9. What is your current availability and expected monthly compensation for a full-time position? Begin your application with FINANCIAL CONTROL.

title: Business Operations & Special Projects Lead E-Commerce | Founder’s Right Hand | Full-Time Remote
job_title: Business Operations & Special Projects Lead E-Commerce | Founder’s Right Hand | Full-Time Remote
description: Business Operations & Special Projects Lead E-Commerce | Founder’s Right Hand | Full-Time Remote We are a fast-growing international e-commerce company operating multiple Shopify stores across several markets, supported by a remote team of approximately 20 people across customer service, media buying, finance, product listing, operations and other functions. We are looking for an exceptionally resourceful Business Operations & Special Projects Lead to work closely with the founder. This is NOT a traditional Operations Manager role where you simply maintain existing processes and manage daily recurring tasks. We need someone who can take an unclear business problem, opportunity or idea, figure out what needs to happen, coordinate the right people and own execution until there is a measurable result. What Your Role Looks Like The founder may come to you with a problem such as: “Our customer feedback scores aren’t good enough. Find out what’s happening and improve them.” “We need to improve our finance function. Assess what is missing, find the right expertise and help implement the solution.” “We want to recruit people currently working at competitors. Build and execute a strategy.” “This department/process isn’t performing properly. Find out why.” “We want to implement a new system. Research the options and make it happen.” You should be comfortable receiving the desired outcome without receiving step-by-step instructions. Your job is to turn ambiguity into execution. Responsibilities * Own cross-functional business improvement projects from problem to result * Investigate operational problems and identify root causes * Turn founder ideas into structured projects and action plans * Coordinate projects across departments * Research solutions, tools, competitors, agencies, vendors and specialists * Find and evaluate external experts when specialized knowledge is required * Support and lead recruitment projects for important roles * Audit existing workflows, systems and SOPs * Improve accountability and follow-through across teams * Build new processes where necessary * Track deadlines, owners, KPIs and outcomes * Follow up with managers and employees to ensure agreed actions actually happen * Identify problems and opportunities proactively rather than waiting for the founder to find them * Present concise recommendations instead of forwarding problems upward * Use AI and automation intelligently to improve execution and efficiency What We Are NOT Looking For We are not looking for: * A virtual assistant who waits for instructions * Someone who needs every project explained step by step * Someone who only knows how to maintain SOPs * Someone whose main skill is updating ClickUp * Someone who forwards problems to management instead of solving them * Someone who confuses activity with results Who You Are You are: * Extremely resourceful * Highly organized * Analytical * Comfortable with ambiguity * Fast at learning unfamiliar subjects * Strong at research * Able to challenge assumptions * Comfortable holding people accountable * Able to communicate clearly with both specialists and managers * Commercially minded * Comfortable working directly with a demanding founder * Focused on measurable outcomes You do NOT need to personally be an expert in finance, Meta advertising, customer service, recruitment and technology. You DO need to know how to understand a problem, find the right information or expert, make a recommendation and drive execution. Experience Strong candidates may come from backgrounds such as: * Business Operations * Strategic Operations * Special Projects * Chief of Staff * Founder’s Associate * E-Commerce Operations * Entrepreneurship * Consulting * Startup operations E-commerce experience is strongly preferred. We care more about evidence of independent problem solving and ownership than impressive job titles. What Success Looks Like After several months, the founder should be involved in fewer operational problems and projects because you are independently taking them from idea/problem to outcome. Instead of asking the founder what to do next, you should increasingly come to the founder saying: “Here is what I found, here are the options, this is what I recommend, and this is what I need from you.” Application Please answer the following questions. Generic or AI-generated answers without specific examples will not be considered. 1. Tell us about the most ambiguous business problem you were personally responsible for solving. What was the problem, what did YOU do and what was the measurable outcome? 2. Tell us about a project where you had to coordinate several people or departments without having all the expertise yourself. 3. Imagine our customer feedback scores have suddenly deteriorated. Several teams could be responsible and nobody knows the exact cause yet. What would you do during your first 7 days? 4. Give an example of something important you discovered and improved at a previous company without your manager asking you to do it. 5. Which AI tools do you currently use professionally and how? 6. What is your current availability and expected monthly compensation for a full-time role? Please begin your application with the words SPECIAL PROJECTS so we know you carefully read the job description.

title: Shopify Expert Needed (Ongoing Work)
description: We build Shopify stores for clients on an ongoing basis and are looking for someone who can take on app installations and setups that go beyond the basics. Most apps install in a few clicks. That is not what this role is about. We need someone who can take an app, work through its documentation, and get it doing exactly what the project requires — including the configuration, the theme integration, and the troubleshooting when it does not work as expected out of the box. Examples of the kind of work involved: * Collection filtering set up with custom filters, including metafield-based ones * Rewards and loyalty programs configured and styled to match the store * Product page customisation apps — configuring options, variants and conditional logic so the right choices appear on the right products * Metafield and metaobject setups, including displaying that content on the theme where the app does not handle it automatically * Product configurators and build-your-own product setups * Bundle, upsell and subscription apps configured to a specific brief * Getting two apps to work together when they conflict * Placing app blocks and embeds correctly in the theme, and fixing them when they break the layout What we are looking for: * Someone who has installed and configured a wide range of Shopify apps, not just the common ones * Comfortable working through an app's documentation and support material to get a result, without needing to be walked through it * Able to make small theme code edits where an app requires it, and to do that safely * Able to test your own work and fix issues before handing it over * Someone who enjoys working out how to do something they have not done before The work: * Paid per task, agreed before each job * Ongoing volume — we build stores continuously * Two trial tasks as the first step, both paid per task regardless of the outcome How to apply: Include the phrase "I listen Dylan" in your message so we know you have read this listing. Give us a few examples of the more complex apps you have set up in the past, and what you configured them to do.

title: Ads Launcher / Media Buyer – Ecommerce

We specialize in building and scaling high-performing direct-response funnels through paid advertising. We’re looking for a reliable and performance-driven Ads Launcher / Media Buyer to join our team. Your main responsibility will be launching, managing, and optimizing Meta ad campaigns across multiple products and markets. If you’re highly organized, understand Meta Ads Manager, and know how to turn winning products and creatives into structured, scalable campaigns, this role could be a great fit for you. Responsibilities * Launch and manage Meta advertising campaigns across multiple stores, products, and markets * Set up campaigns, ad sets, audiences, budgets, creatives, URLs, and tracking correctly * Launch new product and creative tests following our testing structure and SOPs * Monitor campaign performance and identify winners and underperformers * Optimize campaigns based on KPIs such as CPA, ROAS, CTR, CPM, and conversion rate * Scale profitable campaigns while maintaining performance * Manage budgets and make daily optimization decisions * Keep campaign naming, tracking, and Ads Manager organization clean and consistent * Coordinate with the creative team to ensure a continuous flow of new ads and variations * Identify winning creatives and provide performance feedback to the creative team * Troubleshoot rejected ads, tracking issues, and campaign delivery problems * Maintain clear daily reporting on launches, performance, spend, and scaling decisions * Stay up to date with Meta advertising trends and ecommerce media-buying strategies Requirements * Hands-on experience with Meta Ads Manager * Previous experience launching and managing ecommerce advertising campaigns * Strong understanding of campaign structures, testing, optimization, and scaling * Comfortable analyzing metrics such as ROAS, CPA, CTR, CPM, CPC, CVR, and AOV * Able to manage multiple campaigns, products, and markets simultaneously * Extremely detail-oriented — incorrect links, budgets, creatives, or tracking can be costly * Organized and comfortable following established SOPs * Able to make decisions based on performance data rather than assumptions * Clear communicator and self-motivated team player * Reliable and comfortable working in a fast-paced remote environment * Good written and spoken English Bonus: * Experience managing high-volume ecommerce campaigns * Experience with direct-response / advertorial funnels * Experience with Funnelish, Shopify, or similar ecommerce platforms * Experience using tracking tools such as WeTracked * Experience advertising in Switzerland and/or Israel * Experience working with multiple ad accounts and international markets Compensation * Competitive pay + performance bonuses based on results * Fully remote, 48 hours/week, Monday–Saturday * Long-term opportunity with room to grow into a senior media-buying role * Fast-paced but supportive team environment * Strong creative resources and a continuous pipeline of products and ads to test How to Apply Start your message with the word MEDIA to confirm you’ve read this post. title: Shopify Copywriters for Ongoing Projects (Immediate Start!)
job_title: Shopify Copywriters for Ongoing Projects (Immediate Start!)
description: We are looking for multiple people to join our team working on ongoing Shopify projects. This role combines website copy with the back-end setup of Shopify stores. Our developers build the store design. Your job starts once the design is finished, and takes the store from there to launch-ready. On the copy side, this varies by project. On some stores you will be writing the on-theme copy from scratch to the client brief. On others our developers will have written a first pass, and your job is to review it, fix it and bring it up to standard. Either way, the finished copy on the theme is your responsibility. This is website and theme copy, not product description work. The other part of the role is the store setup itself: settings, apps, pages, markets and shipping. This is checklist-driven work. We have recorded step-by-step video training covering every part of the process, so you will know exactly what to do and how we want it done. What we need is someone who follows those steps precisely, every single time, without needing to be chased or corrected. What you will be doing: * Writing on-theme website copy to the client brief, or reviewing and fixing copy already drafted by our developers * Configuring Shopify store settings to our standard checklist * Installing and setting up apps as specified per store * Creating and uploading policy pages and other store pages * Setting up markets, shipping zones and rates What we need from you: * Excellent written English — able to write clean, natural website copy that matches a brand's voice * A sharp eye for detail — you should be able to spot a typo, a wrong product name, or a sentence that does not make sense * Practical hands-on experience inside Shopify admin, not just theory * The ability to follow written and video instructions exactly * Willingness to ask before guessing. If something is missing from the brief, we want you to ask. If it is covered in the training videos, we expect you to find it there * Reliable communication and availability for ongoing work The details: * Paid per completed store * Full video training provided before you start * Ongoing volume — we build stores continuously and want people who stay long term * Paid trial store as the first step, so you get paid for the trial regardless of the outcome How to apply: Include the phrase "I listen Dylan" in your message so we know you have read this listing. Tell us about your experience with Shopify - how long you have worked with it, and what you have handled across both the back end and the front end, outside of development itself. Settings, apps, pages, markets, shipping, theme content, copy. We want to know what you have actually done, not just that you are familiar with the platform.

title: Customer Service Manager | Ecommerce | Full Time | Remote
job_title: Customer Service Manager | Ecommerce | Full Time | Remote
description: Stillbloom LTD is looking for an experienced Customer Service Manager to take ownership of our customer support operation and lead our existing team of eight customer service representatives. Our team supports a growing skincare brand and receives approximately 250 customer enquiries per day, primarily through email and messaging, covering orders, deliveries, product questions, subscriptions, cancellations and refunds. We’re looking for someone who can assess and improve the performance of the existing team, hire strong people when needed, train them properly, set clear expectations and make sure those expectations are met. You should be comfortable giving direct feedback, addressing underperformance and making difficult people decisions fairly and professionally. You will have responsibility for hiring, probation and dismissal decisions within agreed company policies and budgets, alongside the day-to-day performance of the team. In this role, you will: -Manage team capacity and recruitment. Assess the existing team’s workload, skills and coverage before recommending staffing changes. Recruit candidates when needed, run interviews and practical assessments, select new hires, and manage onboarding and probation. Maintain enough capacity to cover demand, weekends and planned absences. -Lead, coach and hold people accountable. Set clear responsibilities and performance expectations. Run regular one-to-ones, review individual results, recognise strong work and address missed standards promptly. -Manage underperformance and dismissals. Identify whether problems come from skills, processes, workload or individual performance. Give clear feedback and appropriate support, document improvement plans, and make and carry out dismissal or contract termination decisions when necessary, following the agreed company process. -Own the daily support operation. Monitor incoming enquiries, allocate workloads, manage shifts and prevent backlogs. Ensure urgent requests reach the right person and customer issues are followed through to resolution. -Maintain excellent service quality. Review a sample of each agent’s conversations, check the accuracy and tone of replies, and coach the team using specific examples. Ensure order changes, refunds and subscription requests are handled correctly. -Handle complex cases. Take ownership of escalated complaints and difficult customer situations. Work with fulfilment, operations and other team members to resolve the underlying problem, and help in the inbox when needed. -Improve systems and processes. Keep procedures, reply templates and training materials current. Improve helpdesk workflows, reporting and appropriate automation so the team can work accurately and efficiently. -Report results and act on them. Maintain a clear weekly scorecard covering response times, backlog, resolution quality, agent productivity and customer satisfaction. Track recurring refund and cancellation reasons, recommend improvements and follow through on agreed actions. Success in this role means customers receive timely, helpful answers; the team knows what is expected; performance issues are addressed early; and company leadership has a clear view of results and priorities. During your first month, you will review the eight agents’ workloads and service quality, assess shift coverage and workflows, establish a performance baseline, and present a prioritised improvement plan. You’ll be a strong fit if you have: -At least three years of experience managing a customer support team, ideally within ecommerce or a direct-to-consumer brand. Experience leading a remote team of a similar size is strongly preferred. -Personal experience recruiting, onboarding, coaching and managing the performance of remote agents, including handling dismissals or contract terminations. -Clear examples of improving team performance, supported by measurable results. -Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate calmly, clearly and confidently with customers and colleagues. -Strong experience with Zendesk or a similar helpdesk, including reporting, reply templates, ticket routing and quality reviews. -Experience handling ecommerce orders, refunds and subscriptions. Familiarity with WooCommerce or Shopify is an advantage. -The ability to interpret reports, investigate problems and turn findings into practical changes. -Strong organisation, sound judgement and the discipline to follow through without needing regular reminders. -Your own reliable computer, high-speed internet and a quiet workspace suitable for video calls. The working arrangement is: -Full time, 40 hours per week, working remotely from the Philippines. -An agreed schedule within our support window of 4am–11pm London time, with weekday and weekend shifts as required. These are coverage hours across the team; your own schedule will be 40 hours per week. -Responsibility for organising reliable coverage across the team and maintaining regular overlap with company leadership. -Salary of $1,800–$2,500 USD per month, depending on experience and demonstrated management ability. Please include your expected monthly rate in USD when applying. This is an opportunity to take real ownership of an important part of a growing business. You’ll work closely with company leadership, have the opportunity to improve how the department operates, and help your team develop and succeed. Stillbloom LTD is a UK-based digital marketing and ecommerce company. We build and grow brands through online marketing, including our skincare brand. We value initiative, clear communication and doing what we say we’ll do. We also enjoy celebrating our wins and having a laugh along the way. To apply, please send your CV and brief answers to the following: 1 What customer support teams have you managed? Include the type of business, number of direct reports and approximate daily enquiry volume. 2 How many agents have you personally hired, and how did you assess whether they would be successful? 3 Describe a measurable improvement you made to a support team. What was the starting position, what did you change, and what was the result? 4 Give an example of how you handled an underperforming agent, including a dismissal or contract termination you managed. What steps did you take and why? 5 Which helpdesk and ecommerce platforms have you used, and what reporting or workflows have you personally set up? 6 What is your expected monthly rate in USD, earliest start date and availability within the stated working hours? Please use the subject line “CS Manager — [Your Name]”. We’re particularly interested in specific examples of what you personally owned and achieved. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an interview and a short paid practical assessment. We look forward to hearing from you.

title: Shopify Product & E-commerce Manager — $4/Hour
description: **PLEASE READ THIS BEFORE APPLYING** This position is **$4/hour**, but this is **NOT a simple data-entry or product-uploading job.** We are looking for someone who is genuinely interested in this position and wants to take ownership of the work. If you are only applying because you are looking for any available VA job, **please do not apply.** If you are genuinely interested, please understand that our hiring process will be **serious and thorough**. We will interview candidates extensively and ask detailed questions about Shopify, e-commerce, AI, product research, pricing, competitors, and how you think. **We will only hire someone after a proper interview and evaluation.** We are looking for someone who wants to stay with us long-term and potentially take on significantly more responsibility as they prove themselves. ### IMPORTANT — APPLICATION We also ask that you **do not apply for a higher amount than the $4/hour rate listed for this position.** If you apply for a higher rate, we will take that as an indication that you may not be genuinely interested in the position as advertised. If you are comfortable starting at **$4/hour** and believe you can prove your value through your work, we are happy to discuss increases in the future based on performance and responsibility. --- # About the Position We are looking for a **Shopify Product & E-commerce Manager** to help manage and maintain our Shopify product catalog and feed. This role involves much more than uploading products. You will be responsible for looking at: * Supplier quotations and costs * Our product catalog * Competitor products * Competitor pricing * Our own sales * Product listings * Product images * Product titles and descriptions * AI-generated product information * Opportunities to improve conversion rates You need to be someone who can **look at the data and think**, rather than simply follow instructions. --- # Your Main Responsibilities ### 1. Shopify Product Management * Manage and maintain Shopify products. * Add and update products. * Check product titles, descriptions, variants, pricing, images, and other information. * Find and correct mistakes in product listings. * Keep our product feed organized and accurate. * Review products before they are published. ### 2. Supplier Pricing You will regularly review supplier quotations and costs. You will need to identify things such as: * Supplier prices increasing or decreasing * Products where our margins have changed * Products that need their selling price updated * Products where our pricing is no longer competitive You should be comfortable working with spreadsheets and comparing large amounts of product data. ### 3. Competitor Research A major part of the job will be researching competitors. For products we sell, you may need to check: * What competitors are charging * How they present their products * What product images they use * How they write their titles * How they structure their descriptions * What offers they are using * How our listing compares to theirs You should be able to look at a competitor and identify: **"What are they doing better than us, and what can we change?"** ### 4. Pricing Management You will help us keep our prices competitive. Pricing decisions may take into account: * Supplier cost * Competitor pricing * Our margins * Sales volume * Product performance * Market conditions You will need to regularly monitor these things and bring potential pricing changes to our attention. ### 5. You should be able to identify: * Products that are selling well * Products that aren't selling * Products suddenly getting more sales * Products where sales have dropped * Products that may need a price change * Products that may need listing or image improvements We want someone who can look at sales data and **notice opportunities and problems.** --- # AI & Claude — VERY IMPORTANT **AI experience is a major requirement for this position.** We use AI heavily in our e-commerce operations. For example, we may use **Claude** to import a large number of products into our Shopify store and generate product information. Your job will then be to review and manage that process. You may need to: * Fill in product information in Google Sheets. * Review AI-generated product information. * Correct mistakes made by AI. * Improve product titles. * Improve product descriptions. * Check AI-generated information against supplier information. * Identify incorrect assumptions made by AI. * Make sure products are properly prepared before publishing. * Help improve the AI workflow over time. We want someone who can say: **"Claude got this wrong. You will be expected to look at competitor listings and identify opportunities to improve ours. This can include: * Reviewing product images * Comparing our images with competitors * Finding better product images * Recommending image changes * Improving titles * Improving descriptions * Improving the overall presentation of products The goal isn't simply: **"The product has been uploaded."** The goal is: **"This is a good product listing that has a strong chance of converting."** --- # What We Are Looking For ### Required: * Good Shopify experience * Strong Google Sheets skills * Good attention to detail * Good English * Comfortable researching products online * Comfortable researching competitors * Comfortable working with pricing data * Comfortable working with AI * Experience with Claude is highly preferred * Able to work independently * Able to handle a large number of products * Able to identify mistakes without needing everything explained ### Strongly Preferred: * Dropshipping experience * E-commerce experience * Experience managing large Shopify catalogs * Experience with product feeds * Google Shopping experience * Competitor research experience * Product pricing experience * AI automation experience * Experience working with Claude * Experience with bulk product imports --- # The Type of Person We Want We want someone who is **proactive.** For example, if you notice: > "The supplier increased the cost of this product." You should notice it. If you notice: > "Our competitor is selling the same product for less." You should notice it. If you notice: > "This product is selling well, but our images are much worse than the competitor." You should notice it. If you notice: > "Claude made the same mistake across 50 products." You should notice it and help fix the underlying problem. We don't want someone who waits for instructions for every single task. We want someone who can **think like an e-commerce operator.** --- # Salary **$4/hour** This is a **full-time, long-term position**. For the right person, there is room for increased pay and responsibility over time based on performance. We care much more about finding the **right person** than finding the cheapest person. --- # Hiring Process Please understand that this will **not be an easy interview process.** Because this position involves pricing, product management, AI, competitor research, and e-commerce decisions, we will interview candidates thoroughly. We may ask you practical questions and give you scenarios to see how you think. We are looking for someone who can actually perform the job, not someone who simply has "Shopify VA" written on their resume. **If you are serious about this position, take your application seriously.** --- # How To Apply Start your application with: **SHOPIFY + AI** Then answer ALL of the following: 1. How many years of Shopify experience do you have? 2. How many Shopify stores have you worked on? 3. Approximately how many products have you managed? 4. Have you used Claude? Give us one example of how you improved a product listing or helped increase conversions. 11. What do you think is more important when managing product pricing: competitor price, supplier cost, margin, or sales performance? Explain your answer. 12. What is your expected hourly rate? **Please note that the starting rate for this position is $4/hour.** **Please do not send a generic application.** Applications that do not follow the instructions above will be ignored. We are specifically looking for someone who is genuinely interested in **Shopify, e-commerce, AI, product management, competitor research, and optimization**. If that's you, we would like to hear from you.

Feedback is not intended as personal criticism; it is a necessary part of improving both your performance and the business as a whole. You should be willing to: * Accept constructive feedback without taking it personally. * Learn from mistakes. * Adapt when processes change. * Ask questions when something is unclear. * Take suggestions seriously and implement them. * Share your own ideas when you see opportunities for improvement. We want team members who are not afraid to say "I think we could do this better" and who are willing to work with us to find a better solution. Our goal is to continuously optimize the company, improve our systems, and become more efficient as we grow. ## Attention to Detail Is Extremely Important Small mistakes can create large problems in eCommerce. For example: * Sending duplicate responses. * Giving a customer incorrect information. * Responding to the wrong conversation. * Missing important supplier updates. * Forgetting to follow up on an outstanding issue. * Providing an answer that does not match our SOPs. We therefore need someone who works carefully, checks their work, and takes responsibility for their tasks. ## What We Provide You will receive: * Detailed SOPs and training materials. * Training and guidance during your onboarding. * Direct support from our existing team. * A clear structure and defined processes. * The opportunity to learn multiple areas of an international eCommerce business. * Long-term opportunities for increased responsibility. * Opportunities for salary increases based on performance and company growth. Because we are growing quickly, new positions and responsibilities will continue to become available. Someone who performs exceptionally well in this role could eventually move into areas such as Operations Management, Customer Support Management, Supply Chain Management, Team Management, or other roles within the business. ## Trial Period & Compensation The position begins with a two-week paid trial period at $4/hour. During these two weeks, we will evaluate: * Quality of work * Reliability * Communication * Attention to detail * Learning speed * Initiative * Ability to follow SOPs * Ability to receive and implement feedback * Overall attitude and team fit After successfully completing the two-week trial period, the position will transition to full-time at $5/hour, with a high chance of an increase after consistently good performance. As the company grows and your responsibilities and performance increase, there will be opportunities for additional responsibilities and future salary increases. ## Who We Are Looking For We are not looking for someone who simply wants to clock in, complete a checklist, and clock out. We are looking for someone who sees an opportunity to become an important part of a young and ambitious company. If you are ambitious, reliable, willing to learn, open to feedback, and excited by the idea of growing together with a company that is expanding internationally, this could be a very good long-term opportunity for you. ## Application Instructions Please include the following in your application: 1. title: E-commerce & Social Media Virtual Assistant
description: What this job is Miçanga Swim is a small, growing swimwear brand in Los Angeles. Our founder designs everything, shoots all our content, runs our pop-ups, and manages production in Brazil. She has more good ideas than time to execute them. That's where you come in. This is an execution role. You'll take a clear list of tasks and get them done consistently, week after week, without needing to be chased. If you're someone who likes checking things off and keeping a system running smoothly, you'll do well here. You don't need to invent the plan. You need to run it. What you'll actually do Shopify store (about half your time) Our store needs real work and we know exactly what it needs: • Write and optimize product listings with SEO (titles, descriptions, tags, alt text) • Build out size charts across every product • Standardize product images so the store looks consistent • Install and configure apps: size chart app, FAQ page, store locator, email popup, shoppable Instagram feed, appointment booking • Build out an FAQ page and a landing page • Keep collections organized and seasonal • Make sure every product is listed, complete, and live • Process orders and update tracking • Flag anything broken or off-brand Social media (about a third of your time) Our founder shoots great content. She goes viral regularly. The problem is consistency, and that's what you'll fix. • Post 3 Instagram feed posts per week from content she provides • Post 4 Instagram stories per week • Post 3 TikToks per week • Write captions in our brand voice • Respond to DMs and comments on both platforms • Light editing and cutting of clips she sends you • Build simple graphics in Canva when we need them (sale announcements, size guides, story templates) • Keep a running content calendar so we always know what's going out • Join a short planning call every Sunday Customer service and organization (the rest) • Answer customer emails: sizing, shipping, returns, product questions • Keep an organized file system for photos, videos, and product assets • Name and sort content so we can actually find things later • Keep a shared task list current and flag what needs the founder's decision • Short weekly check-in on what got done and what's next What we need from you Required: • Real hands-on Shopify experience. You've managed a store, not just seen one. • Comfortable installing and configuring Shopify apps • Solid written English. You'll be writing captions and talking to customers as our brand. • Canva skills at a working level • Experience scheduling and posting to Instagram and TikTok • Organized. You keep files named and systems tidy without being told. • Reliable. You do what you said you'd do, and you say something when you can't. • Steady internet and clear communication Helpful but not required: • Fashion, swimwear, or lifestyle brand experience • Basic photo or video editing (Lightroom, CapCut, or similar) • Klaviyo or email marketing experience • Product photography editing and retouching • Experience with a small brand where you wore a lot of hats A normal week • Optimize 5-8 product listings with SEO and size charts • Install or configure an app we've asked for • Post 3 IG feed posts, 4 stories, 3 TikToks • Write the captions for all of it • Answer 20-30 customer emails and DMs • Make 2-3 Canva graphics • Organize the week's new photos and video into the right folders • Sunday planning call and a short Friday update on what shipped First 30 days • Every product listing has SEO, a complete description, and a size chart • The core apps are installed and working • Social is posting on schedule without the founder having to think about it • Customer emails answered within 24 hours • A file system exists and is being used First 90 days • Store is fully built out: FAQ, landing page, store locator, popup, IG feed • Social has been consistent for three months straight • You own customer service end to end • The founder no longer thinks about posting, listings, or inbox About Miçanga Swim Miçanga Swim is an independent swimwear and activewear brand born between Los Angeles and Rio de Janeiro. We're inspired by the confidence, color, and effortless sexiness of Brazilian beach culture, combined with influences from founder Alena Slapak's Brazilian and Indian experiences. Every piece is designed in small batches and produced in Brazil. Authentic Brazilian cuts with playful details, beading, and embroidery. Community is the heart of what we do. We pop up almost every weekend at flea markets, vintage stores, and local events around Silver Lake and Echo Park, and we've built a loyal following across Los Angeles and San Diego through pop-ups, pool parties, wellness events, and customization experiences. We recently opened our first showroom in Downtown LA. Most of our sales have come from meeting people in person. Our next chapter is bringing that same energy online, and that's the job you'd be helping with. At its core Miçanga is about great bikinis, self-expression, and building a community people actually want to be part of. Why this role exists Our founder does design, production, photography, pop-ups, and travels to Brazil to manage manufacturing. The online side keeps getting pushed to whenever she has a spare hour, which means it moves slowly. We want someone to own it so it stops depending on her. If you do this well, you'll see the store grow and you'll have had a direct hand in it. How to apply Send us: 1 A short note about why this role interests you 2 Links to two or three Shopify stores you've worked on, and what you did on them 3 An example of social media you've managed 4 Your rate, your weekly availability, and your time zone 5 One thing you'd change about our site after looking at ---------- That last one matters most. We want to see how you think.

title: Compliance Manager For Magnali

Requirements * Excellent written and spoken English * Strong research, documentation, and analytical skills * Exceptional attention to detail * Ability to interpret regulations and turn them into clear action steps * Experience in compliance, legal operations, quality assurance, risk management, or regulatory affairs * Ability to work independently and take ownership of projects * Comfortable working in a fast-moving international e-commerce environment * Strong skills with Google Docs, Google Sheets, project-management tools, and online research ## Preferred Experience Experience in one or more of the following areas is highly preferred: * Dietary supplements, health, wellness, cosmetics, or longevity products * FTC and FDA marketing requirements * E-commerce and Shopify * Meta, Google, or TikTok advertising policies * Subscription and automatic-renewal compliance * Payment processors, chargebacks, and consumer disputes * Product labeling and substantiation of health claims * U.S. consumer-protection regulations A legal degree is helpful but **not required**. Practical experience, strong judgment, and attention to detail are more important. ## What We Offer * Long-term, stable remote position * Competitive salary based on experience * Opportunity to grow into a senior compliance or operations role * Direct collaboration with the founder and management team * Meaningful responsibility within a rapidly growing international company * Performance-based compensation increases ## How to Apply Please include the following in your application: 1.
