title: E-commerce Operations & Customer Support Specialist
description: About us We are an Australian online retailer of commercial kitchen equipment, We carry around 49 brands and more than 2,000 products on Shopify — cooking equipment, refrigeration, warewashing, benching and fit-out gear — and sell to restaurants, cafes, hotels, caterers and kitchen fit-out contractors across Australia. We run from a Sydney head office and showroom, with partner warehouses in Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide and Perth. Our promise to customers is simple: the widest range at a guaranteed lowest price, backed by real local support. We are a small, fast-moving team. You will work directly with the business owner, not through layers of management. The role You will be the operational backbone of the store: the person who makes sure every order moves from checkout to delivery cleanly, that every customer gets a fast, clear answer, and that the Shopify catalogue stays accurate. This is not a call-centre or scripted-chat role. Commercial customers ask real questions about specifications, freight, lead times and warranty, and they expect competent written answers. You will learn our products, our suppliers and our freight process, and become the person the owner trusts to run the day-to-day. About 60% of the work is logistics and order operations, 30% is customer and sales support, and 10% is Shopify catalogue and admin. What you will do Order and logistics operations Process daily Shopify orders: confirm stock with our warehouses and suppliers, raise purchase orders, and book freight. Coordinate deliveries of large, heavy commercial equipment: tailgate and forklift requirements, delivery windows, site access, and regional consignments. Track every open shipment and proactively update customers before they have to ask. Handle delivery exceptions: delays, damaged freight, missed deliveries, re-deliveries and returns. Own each case through to resolution. Keep supplier lead times and stock positions up to date so the sales team quotes accurately. Maintain a clean order pipeline: no order sits without a status, a next action and an owner. Customer and sales support Answer customer emails and web enquiries within agreed response times, in clear, professional Australian business English. Respond to pre-sale questions on products, specifications, compatibility, lead times and freight costs, using supplier spec sheets and our product pages as your source of truth. Prepare quotes for multi-item and trade orders and follow up on open quotes. Coordinate warranty and after-sales claims between the customer and the manufacturer's service network. Escalate pricing decisions, disputes and anything you are not sure about to the owner, with a clear summary and a recommended action. Shopify catalogue and admin Update product data: pricing, stock status, lead-time notes, specifications and images, working from supplier information. Spot and fix catalogue errors (wrong specs, missing images, broken variants) as you find them. Keep the shared inbox, order notes and internal trackers tidy so anyone can pick up where you left off. Produce a short daily end-of-day report: orders processed, shipments booked, open issues and what needs the owner's decision. What we need from you Must-haves 2+ years in e-commerce operations, order fulfilment, logistics coordination or customer support for an online store. Hands-on Shopify admin experience: orders, fulfilment, products, variants and inventory. Not just theory. Excellent written English. You will write to Australian business customers every day and your emails must be clear, warm and correct the first time. Confident, direct communicator who asks questions early rather than guessing. Fast learner who is comfortable with technical products. You do not need to know commercial kitchens today, but you must be able to read a spec sheet and explain it plainly. Highly organised. You track many open items at once and nothing gets dropped. Able to work Sydney business hours from a quiet home office with a reliable computer, stable internet (25 Mbps+) and a backup connection or power plan. Nice-to-haves Experience with Australian freight: booking through carriers or freight forwarders, understanding tailgate delivery, pallets and regional surcharges. Experience selling or supporting B2B, trade or high-ticket products (equipment, machinery, furniture, appliances). Familiarity with Google Workspace, Slack, ClickUp and shared inbox workflows. Basic Xero or invoicing experience. Experience communicating with Chinese or overseas suppliers on stock and lead times. Working arrangements Full-time, 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday on Sydney time. Australian public holidays are observed. Remote from home in the Philippines. You supply your own computer and internet; we cover work software. Paid twice monthly via Wise or a payroll platform. 13th-month pay included. Paid leave after a 3-month probation period. Long-term role. We are hiring someone to grow with the business, not to fill a short project. Regular pay reviews tied to performance and responsibility. How to apply Reply with the following. Applications that skip any item will not be considered. Your CV and your OnlineJobs.ph profile link, including your English and DISC test results. A screenshot of the Shopify orders screen from a store you have actually managed, with the store name blurred out. Your expected monthly salary and earliest start date. Written answers to these three questions: Q1. A customer's freight is now five days late and the carrier has no update. Write the email you would send to the customer. Q2. A customer asks whether a 900mm-wide gas cooktop will work in their kitchen. What questions do you ask before you answer, and where do you find the answer? Q3. Describe a time you handled many open orders or tickets at once. How did you keep track and what did you do when something went wrong? Start your application with the word BENCHTOP so we know you read the full post.

title: Shopify Store Builder and Creative Strategist
job_title: Shopify Store Builder and Creative Strategist
description: About the role: We run a portfolio of direct-to-consumer Shopify brands. We build new stores, test products, and scale the winners with paid ads on Meta. Your primary job is building Shopify stores. When we have a store in the queue, that's what you're working on, and we expect them built fast and built well. Between builds — and there will be real stretches between them — you shift to our second priority: static creative. Ad images that run on Meta, and on-site graphics that make our product pages look like real brands instead of dropshipping stores. On the creative side, we want an owner, not a pair of hands. We'll give you the product, the market research, the customer angles, and examples of what's worked before. From there we expect you to do your own research into what's currently winning in the category, decide what's worth testing, and hand back finished creatives. If you need a detailed spec for every asset, this isn't the right role. If you already spend time in the Meta Ad Library because you find it interesting, keep reading. So: a builder first, a designer second, and someone who can switch between the two without losing a day to context switching. What you'll do: Shopify store building (primary): Build and launch new stores from a theme: home page, product pages, collection pages, policy pages, and the full navigation. Install and configure apps (bundles, cart drawer, upsells, reviews, email) following our documented setup. Set up product listings: variants, pricing, images, descriptions, SEO fields, and inventory settings. Make sure every page looks correct on mobile first, then desktop. Most of our traffic is mobile. Clone and adapt proven page layouts across new stores instead of reinventing each one. Speed comes from reuse. Maintain live stores: fix broken sections, spacing problems, slow-loading images, misaligned buttons. Keep our build process documented so each store goes faster than the last. Static creative (between builds): Design ad creatives for Meta in 1:1, 4:5, and 9:16 using our brand templates and safe-zone guidelines. Research what's working right now in our categories: competitor ads, adjacent niches, ad libraries, TikTok and Instagram creative trends. Keep an organized swipe file we can all use. Bring us new static concepts with a one-line rationale for each — new angles, new hooks, new formats. Iterate on winners: when an ad performs, produce the variations that extend its life (new hook, new headline, new background, same winning structure). Create on-site graphics: comparison charts, benefit icon rows, "how it works" strips, guarantee badges, review and testimonial cards, bundle graphics, size and spec charts. Retouch and clean up supplier product photos — remove backgrounds, fix lighting, composite products into lifestyle scenes. Organize every asset in our shared Drive with a consistent naming convention so we can trace which creative won. Requirements: Must have: 2+ years building Shopify stores. You know the theme editor cold and have shipped stores end to end, not just edited someone else's. You're fast. Tell us honestly how long a full store build takes you from empty theme to launch-ready. 2+ years designing static ads for ecommerce — direct response, not brand or social content. You understand that an ad's job is to stop the scroll and sell, and your work shows it. You can look at an ad and explain why it works: the angle, the hook, the visual hierarchy, the offer. We will ask you to do this in the interview. A working habit of researching creative on your own — ad libraries, competitor tracking, saving what you see. Fluent in Canva and at least one of Photoshop, Figma, or Illustrator. You already use AI tools daily — Claude, ChatGPT, or equivalent — and you're good at it. We use AI throughout our operation: product research, ad copy, page copy, image generation and editing, troubleshooting Shopify issues, and speeding up repetitive work. We expect you to reach for these tools on your own, not wait to be told. Be ready to tell us specifically how you use them and where they save you time. Solid written English. You'll be pitching creative ideas in writing, not just receiving instructions. Reliable internet and a computer that can handle design work without crashing. Genuinely self-directed. You plan your own week and report progress without being chased. Nice to have: Basic HTML/CSS for small theme tweaks. Experience with page builders (GemPages, PageFly, Replo, Shogun). Familiarity with conversion apps: bundle widgets, cart drawers, post-purchase upsells, review apps. Experience running or managing Meta ads yourself, even at small scale. Copywriting for ads — headlines, hooks, overlay text. AI image generation and editing for creative work (Midjourney, Flux, Nano Banana, Photoshop generative fill, or similar). Basic video editing or motion (a plus, not required — we have a separate editor). Tools you'll use: Shopify, Canva, Photoshop or Figma, Claude and ChatGPT, AI image tools, Meta Ad Library, Google Drive, Google Sheets, Slack or WhatsApp, Loom, and a handful of Shopify apps we'll train you on. What it's like working with us: We give you the product, the research, and the goal — then get out of your way. Fast feedback and no ambiguity about what "done" means. We're direct. If something isn't working we'll tell you plainly, and we expect the same back. If you think one of our ideas is weak, say so. Reliable pay, on schedule, every time. Long-term role. If you're good, your scope and rate grow — we'd rather raise one strong person than cycle through five cheap ones. How to apply: Applications that don't follow these steps will not be read. 1. Put "BEESWAX" as the first word of your application so we know you read this. 2. Send a portfolio link with at least 3 Shopify stores you built (live URLs) and at least 5 static ads you designed for ecommerce brands. Tell us specifically what you did on each. Answer these questions: 1. How long does a full store build take you, from empty theme to ready to launch? Walk us through your process briefly. 2. Go to the Meta Ad Library, pick any direct-to-consumer product you find interesting, and find one static ad you think is performing well. Send us the screenshot and 3–4 sentences on why you think it works. 3. Where do you look for creative inspiration and competitor research? Name the actual sources you use. 4. Which AI tools do you use in your day-to-day work, and give us one concrete example of a task you've made faster with them. Generic answers ("I use ChatGPT for content") tell us nothing. 5.Which are you stronger at — store building or creative? Be honest. Tell us your hours in PHT, and your monthly rate for full-time work. Shortlisted candidates get a small paid test project: build one product page from a reference, and — given a product and our market research — come back with three ad angles you'd test plus two finished statics. We pay for it whether or not we hire you.

title: Appointment Setter for US Vacation Rental Company (Phone and Text, Must Sound Great on the Phone)
job_title: Appointment Setter for US Vacation Rental Company (Phone and Text, Must Sound Great on the Phone)
description: JOB TITLE Appointment Setter for US Vacation Rental Company (Phone and Text, Must Sound Great on the Phone) SALARY Open, based on experience. Tell us your number. HOURS Full time, 40 hours per week, and this has to be your only job. Most of those hours are at your computer. We set your core schedule together and the start and end times can move. Read this part before you apply. Owner leads come in at all hours. If one lands at nine at night and you are still awake, we want a text or a quick call from you inside a few minutes. Most of those calls run three or four minutes. Automations cover the hours you are asleep. We stay flexible on your schedule. In return we hold you to the calls getting made. TYPE Full time, long term ABOUT US Getaway and Stay manages more than 40 vacation rental homes across Wisconsin, Tennessee, North Carolina, Alabama and Wyoming. Property owners find us through Facebook ads, our website and Airbnb. We have run a remote team for years. Five of our people work remotely right now. We found every one of them ourselves, we hired them ourselves, and we trained them ourselves. Nobody here is new to working with a VA, and nobody here is new to talking about pay. Ask us whatever you want about the role or the money. THE JOB We get about 25 new owner leads a month and we are too slow to call them. That is the problem you solve. A lead comes in. You call and you text within minutes. Your only goal is to book that owner onto the calendar with Becky or Tom. You do not sell. You do not quote fees. You get the appointment. If they do not answer, you keep going. Our standard is one call and one text, twice a day, for fourteen days. That is up to 28 touches before a lead gets closed out. Most people quit after three. We do not. Every call and text gets logged in GoHighLevel with a short note. We will train you on it. YOUR DAY About half your day is calling, texting and logging. The other half is studying. You will learn our markets, our fees, what makes a good rental property and how owners talk about their problems. We hand you the material. We expect you to use it. WHAT WE NEED You sound great on the phone. Warm, awake, confident. A US property owner should not have to work to understand you. You have sold something over the phone before. Appointment setting, inside sales, outbound, collections, any of it counts. You take a no without losing your energy. You write text messages that sound like a person, not a template. Reliable internet and a quiet place to work. You can work US Central business hours. NICE TO HAVE GoHighLevel, HubSpot or a similar CRM. Real estate, vacation rental or hospitality background. Anything else you are already good at that we could use. SEO, CRM buildouts, reporting, ad management. WHERE THIS GOES This starts as a calling and texting role. It does not have to stay one. Once appointments are steady there is room in CRM management, website SEO, reporting and market research. We will train you. If you already have a strength, we will use it. PAY Hourly or monthly, your choice, plus a bonus for every appointment that gets held. Rates depend on experience. Tell us what you want and why you are worth it. HOW TO APPLY Do not reply here with a resume. We only read applications that come through this form: ---------- It takes about ten minutes and it includes a short video you record on your phone. Applications without the video do not get reviewed. The first question asks for a word. The word is BAILEYS.

title: Marketing & Growth Manager
description: Own the marketing. Generate qualified customers. Share in the results. Company: Anderson Heating, Air & Insulation Location: Remote, Philippines Compensation: $15–$20 USD per hour, based on demonstrated experience, plus substantial performance bonus opportunities Schedule: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time, including a scheduled one-hour meal break. Approximately 40 working hours per week. Opportunity: Full-time, long-term role working directly with company leadership About the opportunity Anderson Heating, Air & Insulation is an established home-services company based in Calhoun, Georgia. We are looking for an experienced, hands-on marketing professional to take ownership of our marketing, strengthen our online presence, and generate more qualified customers. Our priority is more HVAC repair calls, replacement opportunities, and commercial repair and maintenance customers in Calhoun and our surrounding service area. We are looking for someone who can turn marketing into measurable business, not just traffic, impressions, or reports. You will have direct access to leadership, support from our existing team, and room to recommend and implement improvements. We want someone who can investigate, prioritize, execute, and follow through without needing a daily task list. What you will own Google Ads and qualified lead generation Manage and improve our Google Ads campaigns, targeting, messaging, landing pages, and conversion tracking. Focus on attracting customers who need our services within our approved service area. Identify other promising marketing channels, recommend focused tests, and evaluate whether the results justify the spending. Our website and customer conversion Take ownership of the website’s marketing performance, including service pages, landing pages, content, and the paths visitors use to contact us. Make improvements directly where you have the skills and coordinate technical help when necessary. You do not need to personally code everything, but you must make sure approved improvements get completed and work correctly. Google Business Profile, local SEO, and AI-search visibility Improve how Anderson appears in local search and AI-assisted search experiences. We want someone with strong SEO fundamentals who stays current with how search is changing and can apply useful new approaches without relying on hype or unsupported ranking promises. Accurate business information across the web Audit and improve our Google Business Profile, Yelp, Better Business Bureau profile, business directories, and other relevant mentions of Anderson. Identify outdated branding, incorrect business information, duplicate listings, missing services, and confusing descriptions. Correct what we control, pursue corrections on third-party platforms, and track unresolved issues. Lead tracking and the office handoff Establish reliable tracking from the original marketing source through qualified inquiry, booked appointment, completed work, and collected revenue. Our office handles customer calls, appointment booking, and sales follow-up. You will work with them to establish a dependable handoff, monitor outcomes, and help resolve problems when opportunities are missed. Your responsibility does not end when a lead is delivered. Reporting, prioritization, and follow-through Explain what is working, what is not, and what should happen next. Work with leadership and bookkeeping to understand acquisition costs and the profitability of the work being generated. Document important processes and take responsibility for maintaining the improvements you implement. Who we are looking for You should have demonstrated experience generating customers for local service businesses. HVAC experience is valuable, but relevant results in plumbing, electrical, roofing, or similar services are also welcome. We are looking for: Hands-on marketing ability: Relevant experience with Google Ads, local SEO, Google Business Profile, website improvements, and lead tracking. Practical AI skills: The ability to use AI effectively for research, audits, analysis, content, and workflow improvements while checking its output and taking responsibility for decisions. Independent ownership: The ability to identify opportunities, set priorities, implement approved changes, and follow through without constant direction. Strong communication and business judgment: The ability to work with employees, explain results clearly, manage approved resources, and recognize when specialist support is needed. You do not need to be an expert in every marketing channel or know every system we use on day one. Experience with Housecall Pro, customer reactivation, call tracking, and marketing automation is helpful. Building complicated AI systems is not the primary purpose of this role. Using the right tools and judgment to generate profitable growth is. A degree is not required. Your demonstrated work and results matter more than your previous title or certificates. You will be part of our team This is a dedicated position within Anderson, not an outside advisory assignment. You will use our company phone and communication systems and work with leadership, office staff, and relevant field employees. You will also have access to our existing virtual assistant for agreed supporting work, such as research, listing updates, and data cleanup. You remain responsible for the strategy, instructions, quality, and results. We will provide appropriate access to company information and systems, including Housecall Pro and QuickBooks where relevant to your responsibilities. We are willing to fund useful software, approved marketing tests, and specialist support when there is a sound business case. We will agree on priorities, budgets, and approval boundaries, then expect you to manage execution. All work must use company-owned accounts where appropriate, protect customer information, and leave Anderson with accessible records and documentation. How success will be measured We will evaluate qualified inquiries, booked appointments, resulting business, acquisition costs, and contribution to profitable growth. Traffic, rankings, clicks, and impressions are useful indicators, but they are not the final objective. During your first 90 days, we will expect you to learn the business, establish a baseline, address priority online-presence problems, implement tracking, and launch or improve a focused set of marketing initiatives. We will agree on realistic targets based on our starting position, budget, and service capacity. Compensation and bonuses The base rate is $15–$20 USD per hour, depending on relevant experience and demonstrated ability. We are prepared to pay at the upper end for the right person. In addition, there will be substantial performance bonus opportunities tied to measurable new or recovered profitable business you help create. The bonus structure will be agreed in writing before you start, including how results are measured, how contributions are credited, and when bonuses are paid. We want this to become a rewarding, well-paid, long-term position. Strong performance should create meaningful opportunities to earn more. Schedule and working expectations You must be consistently available Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time, with the scheduled meal break. Availability must follow U.S. Eastern Time throughout the year, including its seasonal clock changes. This is an overnight schedule in the Philippines. You will participate in relevant meetings, remain reachable through our company communication systems, and record working hours using company-approved timekeeping software. Reliable internet, a suitable computer, and a professional environment for calls and meetings are required. How to apply Please submit your résumé or professional profile, desired hourly rate, earliest availability, and confirmation that you can consistently work the stated schedule. Include one strong example of results you personally helped produce for a local service business. Briefly explain the business, your specific responsibilities, the marketing channels and approximate budget, and what improved. Distinguish verified bookings or revenue from estimates and general lead counts. You may share redacted examples. Do not disclose another company’s confidential information. Shortlisted applicants may be invited to walk through their work and complete a small, paid practical assessment. We are not asking for a full unpaid marketing audit. We are looking for someone who wants to become a trusted member of our team, take ownership of marketing, and help Anderson grow through measurable results.

description: We're ScaleSage — UK-based AI automation and client acquisition specialists, one venture inside The Machine Collective. Our platform is nearly built: Python/FastAPI back end, Next.js front end on Vercel, Postgres on Supabase, Stripe, cold email through the Instantly and Apollo APIs, a conversational diagnostic funnel, a partner commission engine, CI-gated deployments to a Mac Mini production box behind Cloudflare Tunnels, and a growing set of AI agents. You'll take the platform over from the current developer during a structured handover, finish it to a proven standard, and then build what comes next — a client platform, a content production product, and a search and AI visibility product — all scoped and all yours to own. Here's the honest situation. A lot has been built. From now on nothing is called done until it's demonstrated working, estimates are real and kept, and every hour is accounted for. If that sounds like pressure, this isn't your role. If it sounds like how good engineering should work anyway, keep reading. HOW THIS WORKS We start on a monthly retainer at ~20 hours a week, on a fixed weekly pattern you propose and we agree, with at least three hours of daily overlap with Bangkok and Manila working hours. Nothing here is promised. Everything is earned. The path is written into the contract: part-time to prove the fit, expanded part-time as you deliver, full-time when the business and your delivery earn it, and then technical lead across the group's ventures. Full-time follows delivery, not time served. What we hire for, in order: finishing what you start; proving it works before you call it done; clear, precise written and spoken English, because nothing can get lost in translation here; being extremely organised; and an eye for detail, for design, and for what premium quality actually is. Our clients pay for premium and can tell the difference. WHAT YOU'LL INHERIT FastAPI services on Docker Compose on a Mac Mini behind Cloudflare Tunnels and Tailscale; Postgres on Supabase with Alembic migrations and row-level security; GitHub Actions CI gating deploys; Instantly, Apollo, Hunter, Google Places and Companies House APIs; Stripe with webhooks; HeyGen and ElevenLabs for generated video and voice; an e-signature flow; scheduled jobs; LLM agents with per-run cost tracking; Slack alerting. All of it real, all of it in production today. WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY DO The 30-day trial starts on day one and runs alongside the outgoing developer for as long as he's there, overlapping for the remainder of his notice period so you inherit the platform safely before he's gone. Own the platform end to end. Nothing is called done below proven, with evidence: Daily written EOD: completed, active, blocked, next — with hours Four status words for all work — architected, coded, live, proven One live demonstration call a week, working things shown on screen, plus short recorded walkthroughs Blockers raised the same day they appear Time tracking through an agreed tool Any other client work disclosed in writing before it starts Post-trial. You own the platform and scope and build what's next: a client platform, a content production product, and a search and AI visibility product. Not a phased roadmap — you're shipping what the business needs as it needs it. A candidate who takes clean ownership of the platform and closes out the handover meets the bar. One who backs every claim with a proven demo is doing this role well. One who also spots what's inefficient or under-specified and improves the plan is exceptional. MUST HAVE Python and FastAPI in production Postgres and Supabase, schema design and migrations, background jobs and schedulers, webhooks Next.js and React on Vercel, Tailwind, responsive layouts that look right on a phone, CSS animation and motion, and the ability to take a Figma or visual reference and build it to the pixel Stripe subscriptions and one-off payments, REST API integration with third-party SaaS Email sending and deliverability Docker, CI pipelines, Linux, Cloudflare Tunnels, backups and restore, secrets handled properly LLM APIs, prompt and agent design, evaluation of outputs Automated tests, QA on real devices, security and data-protection basics Documentation good enough that someone else could take over Excellent written and spoken English — you'll write daily EODs and speak on a weekly demo call, and English is tested live on the screening call Self-managing: able to take a brief and ship without hand-holding Reliable internet, a quiet workspace If you're strong in most of these and honest about the rest, apply. NICE TO HAVE Experience taking over an existing, undocumented codebase and making it safe to change Background in an agency or client-services environment where "done" has to be provable to someone else Exposure to content production tooling or SEO/AI-search-visibility work Working knowledge of UK GDPR and PECR as they apply to cold email: suppression, unsubscribe handling, eligibility Active GitHub with public commits in the last 90 days Entrepreneurial mindset — you've tried to build something yourself You don't need to know everything already. But you need to be the kind of person who can learn a new tool fast, build with it, and document what you did so the rest of the team can use it. HOW TO APPLY Send: A short recorded video, under three minutes, on why this role and how you'd approach the first week. Answers to the seven questions below, directly in your application. Applications without them are not read. Give real examples — generic answers are exactly what this is screening against: Describe a system you built end to end and are proud of: the stack, what it does, what's live today, and what you'd do differently. Have you taken over someone else's system? Give an example: what you were handed, what was missing, and how you got to the point of being able to change it safely. Give an example of a deadline you missed. When did you tell the client, what did you say, and what changed afterwards? Describe something you shipped that later turned out not to work in production. How was it found, and what did you change so it wouldn't happen again? What is your current client load in hours per week, and what fixed windows could you give this role, in Bangkok time? Send a link to something you've built where the front end is yours, and tell us one thing about it you'd fix if you had an hour. You'll have Claude Code and Codex. Tell us how you use them and how you know what they produce is right. If your answer to question 4 is "that has never happened to me," this isn't the role for you. In return: real freedom in how and when you work, a direct line to the founder, a documented system, and a company that wants you to grow into leading it. Process Written screen → 30-minute call → short technical test → two client references → contract with a 30-day trial. State your monthly retainer for 20 hours a week and your full-time rate.

title: Direct Response Video Editor (VSLs + AI Cartoon Videos and other AI style ads + Short form videos)
job_title: Direct Response Video Editor (VSLs + AI Cartoon Videos and other AI style ads + Short form videos)
description: DTC / dropshipping brand doing ~$80k/month in revenue Role: Video Editor / AI Video Producer Type: Read this part first We are not looking for someone to "make our videos look nice." We are looking for someone who understands that a video's job is to hold attention and make people buy — and who can build that video end to end, including sourcing or generating every frame of footage inside it. If you need a folder of assets handed to you before you can start editing, this role isn't for you. If you can take a script and a product and come back with a finished, conversion-ready asset, keep reading. Who we are We're a direct response DTC brand currently doing around $200k/month, almost entirely on the back of paid media and creative. Creative is our growth lever. Not the site, not the offer tweaks, not the email flows — the video. That means the editor seat is one of the highest-leverage roles in the company. When a video wins here, it wins loudly and you'll see it in the numbers within days. We're scaling, and we want to stop stitching together freelancers per project. We want one highly skilled person who becomes part of the team, learns our angles and our customer inside out, and gets sharper with every batch we ship. How this role starts (please read carefully) This does not begin as a full-time position, and that's deliberate. We start every editor on a lighter workload — a smaller number of videos per week — for the first stretch. Not because we're testing whether you can hold a job, but because we want to see how you fit: how you take feedback, how you handle a script we hand you, how you communicate when something's unclear, and whether the work holds up once the novelty wears off. It also gives you time to learn our customer, our angles, and what a "winning" video looks like in our account specifically. From there it scales. As the fit proves out and your creatives start performing, the volume goes up, the pay goes up, and the arrangement moves toward a secure, permanent full-time seat — with a defined monthly retainer rather than per-project work. To be clear about what we're offering: Phase 1 — Fit: Lower volume, paid per project or at a smaller retainer. Heavy feedback from us. We're both figuring out if this works. Phase 2 — Ramp: Volume increases, you take on the VSLs and the AI cartoon projects with less hand-holding, pay increases accordingly. Phase 3 — In-house: Full-time, secure retainer, you own the creative pipeline and have real input on direction. Room to grow into a creative lead as we bring on more editors. We're not looking for someone to fill a gap for three months. We're looking for the person who's still here in two years running our creative. The slow start is how we get there without either of us wasting the other's time. If you need immediate full-time income from day one, this probably isn't the right fit right now — and that's fine, just be upfront about it. What you'll actually be making 1. Long-form VSLs (Video Sales Letters) The core of the role. 2–7+ minute sales videos built off scripts we provide. You'll be responsible for: Pacing the entire video so retention doesn't collapse — pattern interrupts, cuts, zooms, motion, sound design, text emphasis, visual proof Sourcing your own b-roll. Stock libraries, licensed footage, UGC-style clips, screen recordings, archival, whatever the script calls for. You find it. You don't ask us to send it. In some cases we will also provide clips and we have a bunch of softwares that you can use to make this process easier aswell. Generating AI video to fill the gaps stock can't cover — visualizing mechanisms, metaphors, before/after states, scenarios that don't exist as footage. Building the visual language for a section, not just laying clips over a voiceover Kinetic text, callouts, subtitles, on-screen proof elements, testimonial treatments Sound design and music that carries emotional beats without burying the VO 2. AI cartoon / animated videos (short form AND long form) We're producing a growing volume of fully AI-generated animated content — story-driven ads, explainer content, character-led narratives. You'll take a script and: Build a consistent character and world (this is the hard part — character consistency across dozens of shots is a real skill and we'll be testing for it) Generate the shots yourself using AI image + video tools Handle lip sync, voiceover, and audio Cut it into a video that actually flows as a story rather than a slideshow of AI clips Deliver in both short form (15–60s, vertical) and long form formats 3. Short form paid ads Hook-first ads for Meta / TikTok. High volume, fast iteration. Multiple hook variants of the same body. You'll be cutting these constantly, and you'll be expected to have opinions about which hooks are worth testing. What we need you to be good at Non-negotiable: Editing that converts, not just editing that looks good. You understand hooks, retention curves, pattern interrupts, why the first 3 seconds d ---------- everything, and how to build toward a CTA. If you've never thought about a video in terms of watch time or CPA, you're not ready for this seat. Sourcing your own footage. Independently. You know where to find good b-roll, Generating AI video yourself. Not "willing to learn" — actually doing it now. You know how to prompt, how to iterate when a generation is wrong, how to maintain consistency, and how to upscale and clean up output so it doesn't look like AI slop. Strong technical craft — clean cuts, deliberate pacing, proper audio levels, colour that matches across mixed sources, subtitles that don't look like an afterthought. Speed. We ship a lot. Quality at volume is the whole game. Ownership. You get a script and a brief and come back with a finished asset. You flag problems early. You don't go quiet for four days. Tools — you should be fluent in most of these or their equivalents: Editing: Premiere Pro, After Effects, DaVinci Resolve, or CapCut. AI video: Higgsfield, Veo, Kling, Runway, Sora, Hailuo, Seedance — or whatever you've found works better AI image: Midjourney, Flux, Nano Banana, Ideogram Voice: ElevenLabs or similar Upscaling / cleanup: Topaz, Magnific Bonus: Descript, Adobe Podcast, motion graphics templating, basic scripting/automation for batching Removing text from video: Vmake Nice to have: You've written or restructured direct response scripts before You've worked on offers in health and wellnes niche You can take a competitor's winning ad, break down why it works, and build a better version You track what's new in AI video weekly because you find it genuinely interesting Who this is NOT for Editors who only work from supplied assets People who see AI tools as a threat or a gimmick "Cinematic" editors who make beautiful videos that don't sell Anyone who needs to be chased for updates Agencies or people who'll pass the work to a junior. We want the person doing the work. What you get A real seat on a growing team. We start light on purpose, but the destination is a secure full-time role — and if it works, we build our creative operation around you. Direct feedback loop on your work. You'll see spend, retention data, and CPA on the creatives you cut. Most editors never get this — it's the fastest way to get genuinely good. Budget for tools and subscriptions. We're not going to bottleneck you over a $50/mo AI credit plan. Performance bonuses when your creative becomes a winner. Room to grow into a creative lead role as we scale and bring on more editors under you. Fast decisions. Small team. No layers of approval. How to apply Please follow this exactly — it's the first filter. Send your portfolio. We want to see, specifically: At least one long-form VSL or long-form sales video you cut At least one AI-generated video you produced yourself (cartoon/animated preferred) Short form paid ads if you have them For 2–3 of those videos, tell us in one or two lines each: what the goal was, what you did to hold attention, and any performance numbers you're allowed to share (spend, ROAS, retention, CTR — whatever you have). Tell us your AI stack. Which tools you use for what, and one problem you've solved with them that most people get wrong. Your rate and your realistic capacity — how many long-form videos and how many short form ads per week. Turnaround time on a typical 10-minute VSL, assuming script and VO are provided. Confirm you're okay with the ramp-up structure — starting at lower volume and building toward full-time. One line is enough.

Your Adobe Photoshop experience and the other design tools you use. 7. Confirmation that you can work Monday to Saturday from 1:00 PM to 10:00 PM Philippine time. 8. title: Residential Construction Estimator
description: We are a small construction company (a team of 5 people) based in Western Southland, New Zealand. We complete new residential builds, renovations, rural pole sheds, re-roofing, cladding and other residential and rural projects throughout Southland and Fiordland. We are looking for someone to join the team, that is able to accurately price jobs using architectural plans and complete back-costing reports on existing jobs. About the Role We are looking for a someone to: * Price residential and rural construction projects. * Prepare detailed material take-offs. * Develop labour allowances. * Create construction programmes. * Prepare material-ordering schedules. Engagement and Payment * Approved work will be paid weekly through Wise or PayPal. * The role will begin with a paid test project. * Initial 90-day trial. Systems and Access Singh Building will provide: * A company Google account. * Access to Gmail, Google Drive, Google Docs and Google Sheets. * Access to Wunderbuild, which is our estimating software. The successful applicant must complete the required Wunderbuild training before starting a live estimate. Training time will be paid. All Singh Building work must be completed and stored using the company accounts provided. Required Experience Applicants must have a background in quantity surveying, construction estimating, architecture, engineering, project management or practical construction. You must be able to: * Read architectural and engineering drawings. * Complete detailed quantity take-offs. * Prepare labour and material cost build-ups. * Create practical construction programmes. * Use spreadsheets confidently. * Explain assumptions and ask clear questions. * Communicate clearly in written and spoken English. * Use Wunderbuild, Buildxact or similar estimating software. New Zealand or Australian estimating experience is preferred, but we are willing to train someone with strong construction knowledge and the right attitude. New Zealand Construction Knowledge The successful applicant must become familiar with the New Zealand Building Code and relevant Southland District Council consent guidance. You are not expected to approve Building Code compliance. However, you must understand the New Zealand construction environment well enough to identify requirements or missing information that could affect the estimate, take-off or programme. If something is unclear, it must be raised with Singh Building rather than assumed. Key Responsibilities Review Project Information Before beginning an estimate: * Review the drawings, specifications, engineering information and site details. * Confirm the document dates and drawing revisions. * Identify missing or conflicting information. * Prepare a clear list of questions and assumptions. * Agree on the required deliverables and completion date. Prepare Estimates Prepare detailed estimates in Wunderbuild covering all relevant project costs, including: * Materials and wastage. * Labour by construction stage. * Subcontractors. * Plant, equipment and scaffolding. * Freight, travel and accommodation where applicable. * Site establishment and project overheads. * Prime-cost items, provisional sums and approved mark-ups. Supplier and subcontractor prices must show their source and date. Any figure that is not based on a confirmed price must be clearly identified as an allowance. Complete Material Take-Offs Prepare accurate, traceable take-offs for the materials required to complete each project. Take-offs must: * Use metric measurements. * Identify the relevant drawing and revision. * Separate different products, sizes and specifications. * Show wastage and provisional quantities. * Be checked before submission. * Be detailed enough for Singh Building to obtain supplier prices and order materials. Take-offs may cover concrete, reinforcing, framing, structural timber, roofing, cladding, insulation, linings, flooring, windows, doors, fixings, trim, decking, rural shed materials and other project-specific items. Prepare Labour Allowances * Break labour into practical construction stages. * Use Singh Building’s approved labour rates and productivity assumptions. * Identify the number and type of workers allowed for. * Account for site access, travel, setup and weather where relevant. * Highlight labour-intensive stages and areas of uncertainty. Create Construction Programmes Prepare a practical construction programme for each project, including: * Construction stages and realistic durations. * Dependencies between builders, subcontractors and suppliers. * Council inspections. * Material lead times and ordering dates. * Customer selections and decision deadlines. * Work that can occur at the same time. * Likely delays, clashes or risks. The programme must reflect how the project will actually be built and must not rely only on generic software durations. Where ongoing scheduling is included in the agreed project scope, you will update the programme using information from the site team and clearly identify any changes or risks to key dates. Prepare Material-Ordering Information Provide material-ordering information showing: * Product or specification. * Size and quantity. * Wastage allowed. * Required-on-site date. * Construction stage. * Supplier or price source. * Lead time. * Drawing reference. * Outstanding decisions. The estimator will prepare ordering information but must not place orders without Singh Building’s approval. Final Deliverables Each completed project estimate must include (all done within Wunderbuild): * Detailed estimate. * Quantity take-off. * Labour build-up. * Supplier and subcontractor pricing. * Construction programme. * Material-ordering schedule. * Assumptions and exclusions. * Prime-cost items and provisional sums. * Identified risks and outstanding questions. * Drawing revision, estimate version and date. * Supporting calculations and source files. We're hiring an experienced SEO outreach / link builder to source and acquire communities for us. If you've negotiated guest post or link placements, you've done this — we just need you comfortable doing it on bigger deals. Reddit experience is a plus, not a requirement. The platform mechanics are quick to learn for someone who already knows SEO. WHO YOU PROBABLY ARE • An experienced link builder, SEO outreach specialist, guest post / blogger outreach VA, or digital PR outreach person with real past work you can point to • Fluent in Ahrefs (or Semrush) — prospecting, traffic analysis, keyword and niche evaluation • Comfortable with high-volume cold outreach AND with negotiating a price with a site owner • You understand niches, search intent, and what makes traffic actually valuable • Organized, self-directed, runs your own pipeline • Clear written English • Bonus: affiliate marketing experience, or you've bought/sold websites or domains COMPENSATION Competitive base + a bonus on every acquisition you close. Strong closers earn well here. TO APPLY, ANSWER THESE 1. Describe your link building / outreach experience — what kinds of sites did you prospect, what tools did you use, and roughly what volume of outreach and placements did you handle? 2. You're evaluating a site or community in Ahrefs. Beyond the raw traffic number, what specifically tells you the niche is genuinely valuable and worth paying for versus something that just looks big? Your desired rate and weekly availability.

title: Klaviyo Email Marketing Specialist — Shopify Jewelry Brand (Account Rebuild + Flows)
job_title: Klaviyo Email Marketing Specialist — Shopify Jewelry Brand (Account Rebuild + Flows)
description: ## JOB TYPE Part-time (20 hrs/week) — with the option to move to full-time based on performance **About us** Nolters Gold is a US-based e-commerce brand selling 10K and 14K solid gold jewelry. We've been in business for four years and sell through Shopify ( ---------- ), Etsy, and eBay. We are a small, fast-moving remote team, and we already work with several Philippines-based specialists. **What this role is** This is not a "send a newsletter every week" role. Our Klaviyo account has been dormant since 2024, and we need someone to rebuild it properly from the ground up and then run it. Phase 1 is a rebuild project (roughly 4–6 weeks). Phase 2 is ongoing management of the channel. We are hiring one person for both. **Phase 1 — Account rebuild** - Audit the existing Klaviyo account: old flows, forms, lists, and segments. Recommend what to keep, fix, or delete. - Re-enable and verify the Shopify integration, confirm order history and Placed Order events are syncing correctly. - Clean and segment the contact list. A portion of our contacts were manually imported from Etsy and have no purchase events attached — these need to be identified and handled separately. - Verify and repair sending infrastructure: dedicated sending domain, DKIM, SPF, and DMARC. - Plan and execute a re-engagement and warm-up sequence so we can start sending to a two-year-dormant list without damaging our domain reputation. This is the single most important part of the job. - Build our core flow suite: welcome series, abandoned cart, abandoned checkout, browse abandonment, post-purchase, and win-back. Abandoned cart is our first priority. - Build on-site signup forms and a popup that matches our brand. **Phase 2 — Ongoing management** - Plan and send a monthly campaign calendar (promotions, new product launches, seasonal). - Write email copy and build emails in Klaviyo's editor using our product photography. - Maintain segmentation and suppression lists; monitor list health. - A/B test subject lines, send times, and offers. - Report monthly on flow revenue, campaign revenue, open/click/conversion rates, deliverability, and list growth. --- ## REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE - Minimum 2 years of hands-on Klaviyo experience with Shopify e-commerce brands. This is a hard requirement — please do not apply if your experience is mainly Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, or general VA work. - Proven experience with email deliverability: sending domain setup, DKIM/SPF/DMARC, sender reputation repair, and list warming. - Experience reviving or cleaning up a neglected or dormant email list. - Strong written English. You will be writing customer-facing copy for a US audience. - Comfortable building emails that look good on mobile, working from existing brand photography. - Able to read Klaviyo analytics and explain what the numbers mean in plain language. - Reliable and self-directed. We will give you clear goals, not step-by-step instructions. **Nice to have** - Klaviyo certifications (Product, Deliverability, or Marketing Automation) - Experience with jewelry, luxury, or other high-average-order-value products - SMS marketing experience in Klaviyo - Basic HTML/CSS for email --- ## WORK ARRANGEMENT - Fully remote - Flexible hours, but you must have at least 3 hours of daily overlap with Pacific Time (Los Angeles) business hours - Hours are tracked with TimeDoctor - Paid twice monthly via Wise, on approximately the 1st and the 16th - We will ask you to complete a W-8BEN form for US tax compliance --- ## HOW TO APPLY Applications that skip any of these steps will not be reviewed. 1. Put **GOLD-KLAVIYO** at the start of your application subject line. 2. Answer these three questions directly in your application: - Our Klaviyo list has not been emailed since 2024. Walk us through exactly how you would start sending to it again without damaging our sender reputation. Be specific about sequence and segmentation. - Some of our contacts were manually copied from Etsy orders into Klaviyo, so they have no Placed Order event and unclear marketing consent. How would you handle them? - What was the flow revenue percentage (flow revenue as a share of total store revenue) on the last Klaviyo account you managed, and how long did it take you to get there? 3. Attach one screenshot of a Klaviyo dashboard or flow report from an account you personally built or managed. Blur the client name if you need to. Shortlisted applicants will be given a short paid test task before we make an offer.

title: Meta Ads Specialist + Social Media Manager (Part-Time)
job_title: Meta Ads Specialist + Social Media Manager (Part-Time)
description: About EE Media Productions We are a Canadian video production and social media agency based in Winnipeg, Manitoba. We produce content and run social media for clients in real estate, health and wellness, hospitality, and professional services. You will be working directly with the owner on real client accounts, not on practice work. About the Role This role is two things at once, and you need to be strong at both. 1. Meta Ads. You will set up, run, and optimize Facebook and Instagram ad campaigns for our clients and for EE Media. 2. Social Media Management. You will plan, create, schedule, and publish content, and manage the community around it. If you can do social media but have never built a real campaign in Ads Manager, this is not the role. If you can run ads but cannot produce good-looking content, it is also not the role. We need both. This is not a beginner position. We need someone who can work independently, think on their feet, solve problems on their own, and consistently deliver polished work with minimal supervision. If you require constant instructions, frequent follow-ups, or step-by-step guidance for every task, this role will not be a good fit. Meta Ads Requirements (the part we screen hardest on) You must be able to do all of the following without hand-holding: * Build a campaign from scratch in Ads Manager. Boosting posts from the Page is not the same thing and does not count * Choose the right objective, conversion location, and performance goal for a given business outcome * Set up and troubleshoot the pixel, standard events, and custom conversions * Know what Special Ad Categories are and when they apply. Several of our clients are in real estate, so Housing comes up often * Build and manage audiences, budgets, and schedules * Read the results and know what to change, what to leave alone, and when it is too early to judge * Write ad copy that stays inside Meta's advertising policies Social Media Management Responsibilities * Develop and implement social media strategies and monthly content calendars * Create, schedule, and publish posts across agreed platforms * Manage scheduling and publishing through SocialBee * Create graphics and simple video edits for social content * Monitor and respond to comments, messages, and mentions, and engage the online community * Track and analyze performance metrics and provide regular reports * Stay updated on social media trends and apply strategies to grow reach and engagement * Organize project files and maintain efficient workflows * Meet deadlines consistently and communicate proactively Must-Have Skills * Fluent in English, both written and spoken * Proven Meta Ads experience, as described above * Very familiar with Meta Business Suite and Business Manager * Familiar with SocialBee * Good graphic design skills (Canva, Photoshop, or similar) * Knows some video editing (CapCut, Premiere Pro, or similar) * Strong understanding of social media content and current trends Working Hours * 10 to 20 hours per week, flexible within Philippine business hours * You must be reachable on WhatsApp within 15 to 30 minutes during your working hours * One short written update at the end of each of your working days, so it is waiting for us when Winnipeg wakes up * Occasional calls will be scheduled with advance notice to find a time that works for both sides Personality Traits We Value * Resourceful and proactive * Strong problem-solving skills * Detail-oriented * Fast learner * Reliable and accountable * Able to work with little to no supervision * Takes initiative instead of waiting for instructions Bonus Points * Newsletter and email marketing experience (Mailchimp) * Copywriting or caption-writing experience * WordPress and basic SEO * Experience with real estate or premium brand content * Experience reporting on paid ad results and analytics Rate CAD $8 per hour Hiring Process 1. We review applications that followed the instructions below 2. Shortlisted applicants complete a short PAID test task, about one hour, paid at the hourly rate 3. A short call 4. Start Application Instructions To apply, please do all of the following: * Start your message with the phrase "EE Creative" so we know you read this post to the end * Include a link to your portfolio (graphic design and social media samples, plus any Meta Ads results or case studies you can share) * Describe one Meta Ads campaign you managed in two or three sentences. Tell us the objective you chose, the conversion location, what the cost per result was, and what you changed to improve it * Record a short 30 to 45 second video introducing yourself and send it to our WhatsApp: [YOUR NUMBER HERE] APPLICANTS WHO DO NOT FOLLOW THE INSTRUCTIONS ABOVE WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED

title: Video Editor/ Social Media Manager
description: Video Editor & Social Media Manager — Part-Time Starting Pay: $5 USD/hour Hours: Part-Time to Start Opportunity: Potential to Become Full-Time Work: Remote Industry: Real Estate — Florida 🚨 We Are Looking for a FAST, Organized, and Reliable Person We are looking for a Video Editor & Social Media Manager who is creative, fast, organized, and extremely good at time management. This is not a position for someone who needs constant reminders or takes several days to complete simple tasks. We have a consistent daily content schedule, and we need someone who can work efficiently, meet deadlines, follow instructions, and keep content moving every day. We want someone who can become an important part of our marketing team. As you learn our business and demonstrate that you can consistently produce quality work, meet deadlines, and take ownership of your responsibilities, there may be opportunities for: More hours Additional responsibilities Increased pay based on performance and responsibilities Full-time employment Long-term growth within the company 📩 How to Apply Please include the following in your application: A short introduction about yourself Your previous experience with video editing and social media A link to your portfolio or examples of your best work 2–3 examples of short-form videos/Reels you have edited Examples of graphics, carousels, or social media posts you have created The software you normally use for video editing and graphic design Your desired hourly rate Your current weekly availability Your internet speed Your computer specifications Bonus Send us 2–3 social media accounts or brands whose content style you like and briefly explain why you like their content. 🎯 Who Will Succeed in This Position? The person who succeeds in this role will be: FAST. ORGANIZED. CREATIVE. DEPENDABLE. DETAIL-ORIENTED. GOOD WITH DEADLINES. ABLE TO FOLLOW DIRECTIONS. ABLE TO WORK INDEPENDENTLY. We don't expect perfection, but we do expect effort, accountability, communication, and consistency. If you are creative, move quickly, manage your time well, take pride in your work, and want the opportunity to grow with a company, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Full Stack / DevOps Contractor - SaaS Platform (Licensed Cannabis Dispensaries) - Long Term, Start ASAP
job_title: Full Stack / DevOps Contractor - SaaS Platform (Licensed Cannabis Dispensaries) - Long Term, Start ASAP
description: About us: We are ClearCore, a SaaS platform built for licensed cannabis dispensaries. Our software gives dispensaries a full point of sale system, order management, inventory tracking, staff management, compliance tools, and a member loyalty program, all in one place. We are a startup approaching launch and building our team as we go. About the role: We are looking for someone to join our team long term as a QA tester who can grow into full stack and DevOps work. Experience with cannabis compliance or METRC is a big plus and will stand out, but not required to apply. Quick note on METRC for anyone new to the industry: METRC stands for Marijuana Enforcement Tracking Reporting Compliance. It is the seed to sale tracking system that most states require licensed cannabis businesses to use. It tracks cannabis products from the moment they are grown all the way through to the final sale, so the state can confirm everything is accounted for and compliant. You can learn more at metrc.com. Our platform integrates with METRC, and that integration is part of what you would eventually help us build and improve. What this role looks like starting out: You will spend your first couple weeks learning our product by testing it. Our platform has three dashboards, Admin, Shops, and Members. Your job is to click through each one daily, find bugs, and log them into our shared Notion doc. We review what you find and make code changes daily on our time zone so we can move fast together. This role should only take a couple hours a day to start, Monday through Friday. No expectation of weekend work. We want you to actually learn how the product should work before moving into anything technical. Once you know the front end well, you will get access to our GitHub. From there you can start reading the codebase and helping us improve the backend, including our METRC integration and other APIs. If you also have front end UI skills, there is room to help improve the UI across all three dashboards and our two marketing websites as well. Pay structure: Starting rate is $5 per hour, paid semi monthly on the 15th and the last day of the month, which is the 30th or 31st depending on the month. This is a long term role from the start, not a short term project. As you grow with us and take on more, especially backend and METRC work, pay will increase based on your contribution. What we are looking for: Someone reliable who shows up daily Monday through Friday and communicates clearly Comfortable testing software and writing clear bug reports Willing to learn cannabis industry compliance and METRC over time Interested in a long term role, we hire with the intent of growing together Some background in QA, full stack development, or DevOps is helpful but we care more about attitude and consistency Front end UI skills are a bonus We want someone who is willing to learn this industry and grow with us through launch and beyond. If this sounds like you, apply and tell us a little about your experience with software testing, full stack or DevOps work, and whether you have any exposure to cannabis or METRC.

title: Experienced Credit Repair Specialist – FCRA/CFPB
description: ## Experienced Credit Repair Specialist Needed We are looking for an experienced **Credit Repair Specialist / Credit Dispute Specialist** who understands U.S. consumer credit laws and can independently review credit reports, identify inaccurate or questionable negative items, prepare customized disputes, and properly document all activity inside **Credit Repair Cloud**. ### REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE You must be familiar with: * FCRA — Fair Credit Reporting Act * FACTA — Fair and Accurate Credit Transactions Act * FDCPA — Fair Debt Collection Practices Act * CFPB complaint procedures * FTC Identity Theft procedures * HIPAA as it relates to applicable medical debt/privacy situations * Credit bureau dispute procedures * Creditor and collection agency disputes * Identity theft blocking procedures * Consumer reporting agency freezes ### CREDIT REPAIR CLOUD EXPERIENCE REQUIRED You must have experience using **Credit Repair Cloud** as a credit repair CRM. You should know how to: * Add and manage clients * Import/analyze credit reports * Track negative tradelines * Track dispute rounds * Update client progress * Update CRM at the 15-day, 30-day, and 45-day stages * Track dispute letters that have been sent * Record bureau responses * Track deletions and account updates * Record creditor and collection agency responses * Create and manage follow-up actions * Keep detailed client notes * Maintain organized client files and documentation * Track the complete dispute history for each client ### CREDIT REPORT EXPERIENCE You must know how to analyze credit reports from platforms such as: * Experian * Equifax * TransUnion * MyFICO * SmartCredit * IdentityIQ * PrivacyGuard * Credit Karma * Identity Guard * Other credit monitoring platforms You should be able to identify and analyze: * Collections * Charge-offs * Late payments * Repossessions * Closed derogatory accounts * Inaccurate balances * Duplicate accounts * Incorrect account statuses * Incorrect dates * Payment history inconsistencies * Accounts reporting differently between bureaus * Unauthorized hard inquiries * Potential identity theft accounts * Other inaccurate or unverifiable information ### RESPONSIBILITIES The selected specialist will be responsible for: * Reviewing all three credit bureaus * Identifying negative tradelines * Identifying inconsistencies between Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion * Developing an appropriate dispute strategy for each client * Creating customized dispute letters for Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion * Creating customized letters for original creditors * Creating customized letters for collection agencies and debt buyers * Preparing follow-up disputes when necessary * Updating **Credit Repair Cloud** throughout the dispute process * Updating client files approximately every 15, 30, and 45 days * Keeping detailed records of disputes, responses, deletions, updates, and next actions * Reviewing bureau investigation results * Reviewing creditor and collector responses * Escalating legitimate unresolved reporting issues when appropriate ### FREEZE EXPERIENCE You should know how to properly submit and manage security freezes or freeze requests with: * Equifax * Experian * TransUnion * LexisNexis * Innovis * ARS * CoreLogic * SageStream You should understand when a freeze is appropriate and when it is not. ### CFPB / FTC EXPERIENCE You must understand how to: * Prepare and submit legitimate CFPB complaints * Include supporting documentation * Create a clear timeline of the dispute * Determine when CFPB escalation is appropriate * Properly use FTC IdentityTheft.gov procedures for legitimate identity theft cases * Prepare supporting documentation for legitimate identity theft disputes **We will not use false identity theft claims or fraudulent dispute tactics.** ### IMPORTANT We are NOT looking for someone who simply sends the same generic dispute template to every client. We want someone who understands the complete process: **Analyze → Identify inaccuracies/inconsistencies → Determine the correct dispute strategy → Create customized disputes → Track everything in Credit Repair Cloud → Review responses → Follow up → Escalate when justified** Attention to detail and organization are extremely important. ### TO APPLY Please answer ALL of the following: 1. How many years have you worked in credit repair? 2. Approximately how many client credit files have you handled? 3. How many years of experience do you have using **Credit Repair Cloud**? 4. What tasks have you personally performed inside Credit Repair Cloud? 5. Which credit monitoring platforms are you experienced with? 6. Explain the difference between an FCRA dispute and an FDCPA dispute. 7. When would you dispute directly with a creditor or furnisher instead of only disputing with the credit bureaus? 8. What would you look for when the same account is reporting differently between Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion? 9. Have you prepared CFPB complaints before? Explain your experience. 10. Have you handled legitimate identity theft disputes involving FTC Identity Theft Reports? 11. Are you experienced with LexisNexis, Innovis, CoreLogic, SageStream, and ARS freezes? 12. What is your process after receiving a bureau investigation result? 13. What information do you normally track inside Credit Repair Cloud during a 30–45 day dispute cycle? 14. How do you determine whether to send another dispute, dispute with the furnisher, or escalate the issue? Please start your onlinejobs.ph proposal with the words: **“CREDIT REPAIR CLOUD”** If you do not include those words, your application may not be reviewed. We are looking for someone dependable, detail-oriented, and experienced who can potentially work with us **long term as our client volume grows**.

title: Chief of Staff / Executive Operations Manager — Real Estate & Short-Term Rentals
job_title: Chief of Staff / Executive Operations Manager — Real Estate & Short-Term Rentals
description: READ THIS FIRST I am looking for someone who can eventually become my right hand across the entire business. This is NOT an Executive Assistant position. I don’t need someone to manage my calendar, take notes, remind me about tasks, or wait for instructions. I need an absolute execution monster who can take the hundreds of moving pieces in my business, organize them, drive people to completion, solve problems independently, and dramatically reduce how much I personally have to manage. My businesses involve: * 20+ short-term rentals * Property management * Large renovation and construction projects * Real estate acquisitions * Direct-to-seller marketing * Contractors and maintenance teams * Cleaners and vendors * Claims and damage recovery * Financing and lenders * New property launches * Large acreage/development projects * VAs and remote employees * AI/automation implementation There are constantly dozens of projects and hundreds of follow-ups happening simultaneously. Your job is to make sure nothing gets dropped. ⸻ YOUR JOB IS TO CREATE LEVERAGE FOR ME If I tell you: “Get me three HVAC quotes for this property, figure out why the septic contractor hasn’t responded, make sure the lender has the revised scope, get an answer from the excavator, find out why this Airbnb claim hasn’t been paid, and make sure the new listing launches Friday.” I should not need to ask about those things again. You figure out: Who needs contacted → what information is missing → who owns it → what the deadline is → what needs followed up on → what can be solved without me → and what actually requires my decision. Then you drive everything forward. I DON’T WANT PROBLEMS BROUGHT TO ME Whenever possible, I want: Problem → research → options → your recommendation → decision needed from me. Not: “What do you want me to do?” ⸻ What You Will Own You will eventually oversee and coordinate execution across the business. That includes: * Maintaining the master company/project priority list * Turning my ideas and conversations into actionable projects * Assigning responsibilities and deadlines * Following up relentlessly until tasks are completed * Holding employees and contractors accountable * Coordinating VAs and department leads * Tracking construction and renovation projects * Tracking property launches * Coordinating lenders, contractors, vendors and service providers * Making sure important emails/messages receive responses * Researching problems before bringing them to me * Obtaining quotes and comparing options * Preparing decisions for me * Running weekly accountability meetings * Tracking KPIs across departments * Identifying bottlenecks * Improving SOPs and company systems * Working with our AI/automation person to eliminate unnecessary manual work * Catching problems before I notice them * Making sure something I mentioned three weeks ago doesn’t disappear because I stopped talking about it Eventually, you should understand my businesses well enough to know what I am going to ask before I ask it. ⸻ THIS POSITION WILL NOT BE EASY I move quickly. I have a lot happening simultaneously. Priorities can change. I ask a lot of questions. I generate new ideas constantly. I expect people to follow through. And I have very little patience for repeatedly asking about something that should already have been handled. If you need an extremely structured corporate environment where someone gives you five tasks every morning, this position will be miserable for you. But if you love taking chaos and turning it into execution, you may absolutely thrive here. ⸻ I NEED SOMEONE BETTER ORGANIZED THAN I AM You should be the person saying: “You mentioned this two weeks ago. Here’s where it stands.” “We’re waiting on these three people. I’ve already followed up twice.” “This contractor’s quote doesn’t make sense. I got two alternatives.” “This project will miss its deadline unless we make this decision today.” “You don’t need to handle this. I already solved it.” That’s the level I’m looking for. ⸻ THE GOAL Eventually, I want the organizational structure to look something like: Owner/CEO → Chief of Staff → Department Leads / Specialists / VAs I don’t want to personally manage eight different employees and constantly check whether things happened. You make sure they happen. That means you must be comfortable holding other people accountable—even people with specialized expertise you don’t personally have. ⸻ DO NOT APPLY IF: * You are primarily an Executive Assistant * You need detailed instructions for every task * You are afraid to make decisions * You avoid uncomfortable follow-ups * You aren’t comfortable holding people accountable * You regularly forget things * You wait several days before following up * You think updating a task-management system = getting something accomplished * You send problems upward without first trying to solve them * You become overwhelmed when 20 things happen simultaneously I would rather not fill this position than hire an average person. ⸻ PROVE YOU’RE THE PERSON Generic applications will be ignored. Answer ALL of these: 1. What is the most complicated business/operation you’ve personally helped run? How many employees, projects, customers, or locations were involved? 2. Tell me about an executive/founder you supported who had too many things happening simultaneously. How did you create order? 3. Give me an example where your boss gave you a vague objective instead of instructions. What did you do? 4. Tell me about something important that would have been forgotten or missed if you hadn’t caught it. 5. Give me an example where you had to hold an employee, contractor, or vendor accountable when they weren’t performing. 6. Your boss gives you 30 unrelated tasks in one conversation. Walk me through exactly what happens afterward. 7. You need an answer from a contractor today. You’ve called twice, texted, and emailed with no response. What do you do? 8. Three employees tell you their tasks are delayed because they’re waiting on other people. What do you do? 9. Tell me about a decision you made without asking your boss first. Why did you feel comfortable making it? 10. What information would you want from me during your first 30 days so you could eventually begin anticipating what I need? 11. What systems have you personally used to manage complex projects, teams, SOPs, communication, and accountability? 12. What experience do you have with real estate, construction, property management, Airbnb/STRs, hospitality, or investing? MOST IMPORTANT QUESTION: 13. Assume I disappear for 7 days and barely respond to you. What specifically would you do to make sure the business continues moving forward without me? ⸻ VIDEO REQUIRED Send a 3–5 minute video. Tell me about the most chaotic operation, company, executive, or project you’ve ever managed. Explain: What was happening → why it was difficult → what YOU took ownership of → systems you created → problems you solved → measurable result. Don’t tell me you’re organized. Show me evidence that you’ve operated at this level. ⸻ Compensation I am willing to pay well above typical OnlineJobs.ph compensation for an exceptional person. I’m not looking for cheap labor. I’m looking for leverage. If hiring you gives me back significant hours every week, makes the rest of my team perform better, prevents expensive mistakes, and allows the company to grow without everything flowing through me, you will be extremely valuable to me. There is substantial room for increased compensation and responsibility for someone who becomes indispensable. If you’re the kind of person who sees 100 moving pieces and immediately wants to take control of them, I want to hear from you.
