title: Senior Construction Project Manager — Residential / STR Renovations
job_title: Senior Construction Project Manager — Residential / STR Renovations
description: READ THIS BEFORE APPLYING This will probably be the hardest position in my company to replace me in. I am an extremely hands-on owner and a licensed General Contractor. I have personally managed hundreds of thousands of dollars in renovations, major residential projects, and complicated STR builds. I am involved in scopes, pricing, contractor selection, materials, design decisions, problem solving, scheduling, and quality control. I currently plan to continue managing my own construction projects. I am posting this because there is a chance that an exceptional construction project manager exists who can actually manage these projects better than I can. If that’s you, I want to meet you. If you need me to tell you what to do every day, do not apply. If your idea of project management is updating a spreadsheet and asking contractors for updates, do not apply. If you cannot look at a construction problem, understand what’s happening, challenge a contractor, compare solutions, negotiate pricing, and drive the project forward without me, do not apply. The Standard I don’t need an assistant for construction. I need someone capable of replacing me as the person driving the project. You should eventually know: What is happening → what should be happening → what’s behind schedule → who’s responsible → what decision needs made → what it should cost → and what happens next. Ideally, you tell me what needs to happen—not the other way around. Our Projects These aren’t cookie-cutter apartment turns. Projects can include: * Large luxury STR renovations * 5,000–10,000+ sq. ft. homes * Indoor pools and pool rooms * HVAC and mechanical systems * Plumbing and electrical * Septic systems * Foundations and structural work * Roofing and exterior projects * Flooring, cabinetry and finish carpentry * Excavation, grading, roads and drainage * Landscaping and large acreage properties * Amenity construction * New cabins and larger ground-up developments * Furnishing and final STR launch * Multiple contractors working simultaneously You don’t have to personally be an expert tradesperson in every category. But you need enough construction knowledge to know when someone is feeding you bullshit. What You Would Own You would eventually be responsible for: * Creating detailed scopes of work * Breaking projects into phases and critical paths * Soliciting and comparing multiple bids * Finding and vetting contractors * Negotiating labor and material pricing * Reviewing estimates for missing scope and inflated pricing * Building project budgets * Tracking actual vs. budget * Scheduling trades in the correct sequence * Ordering and tracking materials * Preventing material shortages from delaying jobs * Coordinating contractors remotely * Reviewing daily job-site photos/videos * Maintaining punch lists * Verifying work before payments are released * Tracking change orders * Catching mistakes before they become expensive * Following up relentlessly * Keeping contractors accountable to schedules * Escalating only decisions that actually require ownership * Giving me a concise dashboard of every project’s budget, schedule, problems and next actions I Am Extremely Involved Understand this before applying: You are not walking into a company where the owner doesn’t understand construction. I will question your recommendations. I will question bids. I will notice things. I will ask why. And if I can manage the project faster, cheaper, or better myself, there is no reason for this position to exist. That isn’t meant to intimidate the right person. The right person should read that and see an opportunity. The Person I’m Looking For I want someone who is: Relentless. Organized. Construction-smart. Financially sharp. Extremely proactive. Difficult to bullshit. Excellent with contractors. Excellent at negotiation. Obsessed with follow-through. You need to think like an owner, not an employee. Saving $20,000 through better bidding matters. Catching a $30,000 mistake before construction matters. Getting a property launched four weeks earlier matters. Finding a better contractor matters. Sending me a beautiful spreadsheet while a project runs three months late does not matter. PROVE YOU’RE BETTER THAN ME Do not send me a generic application. Answer every question below: 1. What is the largest construction/renovation project you’ve personally managed? Give me the budget, square footage, timeline and scope. 2. How many projects have you managed simultaneously? 3. Give me an example where you caught a contractor’s mistake before it became an expensive problem. What would it have cost if you hadn’t caught it? 4. Give me an example where you negotiated a contractor/vendor price down. Original price, final price, and how you did it. 5. Tell me about a project that was behind schedule. What specifically did you do to recover the schedule? 6. A contractor gives you a $70,000 bid that just says “HVAC replacement — labor and materials.” What do you do next? 7. Two contractors bid the same project at $42,000 and $71,000. Walk me through exactly how you determine which bid is actually better. 8. A contractor tells you something unexpected will cost another $18,000. What do you require before approving the change order? 9. How would you remotely verify that work is actually completed correctly before releasing payment? 10. What construction software/project-management systems have you used? 11. What construction trades do you understand well enough to challenge a contractor’s scope or recommendation? 12. Tell me about your worst construction mistake. What did you miss, how much did it cost, and what system did you implement so it never happened again? FINAL TEST Send me a 3–5 minute video. Don’t spend the video telling me you’re hardworking. Pick one complicated project you personally managed and show me: Scope → budget → schedule → contractor management → major problems → your decisions → final result. If possible, show actual redacted schedules, budgets, scopes, bids, progress photos, or project-management systems. Compensation I am willing to pay well above typical OnlineJobs.ph compensation for the right person. But this isn’t a position I’m desperate to fill. If I don’t find someone exceptional, I will continue doing it myself. The person I hire needs to create enough value through better pricing, tighter schedules, fewer mistakes, better contractor management, and less of my time that hiring them becomes an obvious decision. If you think you can manage my construction projects better than I can, prove it.

title: NinjaTrader / NinjaScript Developer | Automated Futures Systems & Product Strategy
job_title: NinjaTrader / NinjaScript Developer | Automated Futures Systems & Product Strategy
description: KJD Capital is looking for an experienced NinjaTrader 8 / NinjaScript Developer to design, build, test, deploy, and maintain automated futures trading systems. We are not looking for someone who simply writes indicators or converts basic rules into code. We want a developer who understands futures markets, systematic trading, live execution, risk management, performance validation, and the commercial side of building a high-value automated trading product. A major objective of this role is to help us develop systems that can progress from research and backtesting into forward testing and live trading, with performance documented through credible live brokerage records. The ideal candidate can also work with management on product strategy—helping determine which systems, features, risk configurations, and performance characteristics make the product compelling for a high-ticket automated trading offer. Main Responsibilities NinjaTrader Strategy Development Develop automated futures trading strategies in NinjaTrader 8 Write clean and maintainable NinjaScript / C# Convert trading concepts and detailed specifications into functioning automated systems Develop new strategies from the ground up Modify and improve existing strategies Build custom indicators and supporting tools Develop sophisticated entry and exit logic Build stop-loss and profit-target management Create trailing-stop and break-even functionality Implement time-of-day and session filters Build position-sizing and contract-sizing logic Create daily profit/loss limits and account-level risk controls Develop multi-timeframe and multi-data-series strategies where necessary Troubleshoot execution and order-management issues Live Trading & Performance Validation This is an important part of the position. We want someone who understands that a profitable backtest alone is not enough. You should be able to help take a strategy through: Concept → Development → Backtest → Optimization → Robustness Testing → Forward Testing → Simulation → Live Deployment → Performance Monitoring Responsibilities may include: Conduct realistic backtests Account for commissions and slippage Avoid unrealistic fills or backtesting assumptions Identify potential overfitting Perform out-of-sample testing Perform walk-forward or similar robustness testing Forward-test systems before live deployment Analyze live execution versus historical results Troubleshoot discrepancies between backtest and live performance Monitor slippage and order execution Improve system stability and reliability Help establish appropriate risk parameters for live accounts Maintain accurate strategy versions and performance records Our objective is to develop strategies capable of establishing credible, verifiable live track records, rather than relying solely on hypothetical backtests. The developer should understand the importance of maintaining appropriate documentation and broker-generated performance records and never fabricating or overstating live results. Futures Trading Knowledge Strong futures knowledge is highly preferred. You should understand: NQ / MNQ ES / MES GC / MGC CL Futures contracts Tick size and tick value Contract sizing Position sizing Long and short trades Market, limit, stop, and stop-limit orders Slippage Commissions P&L Win rate Profit factor Average winner / average loser Risk-to-reward Maximum drawdown Trailing drawdown Sharpe and other performance metrics Equity curves Daily loss limits Prop firm risk requirements Live brokerage trading You should be able to look beyond total net profit and determine whether a strategy has a realistic and commercially viable risk profile. NinjaTrader Expertise Strong experience with NinjaTrader 8 is required. You should be comfortable working with: NinjaScript C# NinjaTrader Editor Strategy Analyzer Market Replay Playback Historical and real-time data OnBarUpdate() OnOrderUpdate() OnExecutionUpdate() BarsInProgress Multiple data series Calculate modes Tick Replay Session templates Trading hours Strategy states Managed order handling Unmanaged order handling where appropriate Live account execution Simulation accounts Brokerage connections You should understand the differences between historical processing, backtesting, playback, simulation, and live execution. Strategy Research & Optimization We want someone who can contribute intellectually to strategy development rather than simply waiting to receive exact coding instructions. You should be able to: Evaluate trading ideas Identify weaknesses in strategy logic Suggest improvements Analyze performance distributions Analyze drawdown characteristics Determine whether an optimization is likely overfit Test multiple market conditions Evaluate performance across different periods Help determine appropriate risk configurations Develop different strategy presets when appropriate Help determine which configurations should be deployed to live accounts Experience with quantitative research, systematic trading, statistical analysis, Python, or data analysis is a major advantage. Product & High-Ticket Offer Strategy This developer will also work with management on the commercial strategy behind the automated trading systems. You will not necessarily be responsible for closing sales, but we want someone who understands how the technical product contributes to a premium offer. You may help us: Determine which strategy configurations should become customer-facing products Develop different risk profiles and system presets Identify the most meaningful performance statistics to present to prospects Explain the technical differentiators of the system Help our sales team understand how the strategies operate Prepare technical information for product demonstrations Help create clear explanations of strategy logic without exposing proprietary intellectual property Identify features that could increase the value of the product Help determine how the product should be positioned for serious futures traders Assist management with the technical side of a high-ticket automated trading offer The goal is to create a product where the software, live performance history, risk controls, documentation, onboarding experience, and sales presentation all support the value of the offering. Marketing and sales materials must accurately distinguish live results, simulated results, and hypothetical/backtested performance. Prop Firm & Live Brokerage Knowledge Experience with both environments is highly preferred. You should understand the differences between: Prop Firm Trading Funded accounts Evaluation accounts Trailing drawdown Daily loss limits Consistency requirements Contract limits and: Live Brokerage Trading Real capital Brokerage connections Commissions Slippage Order routing Live fills Account-level risk management Experience with NinjaTrader Brokerage and Tradovate is a major plus. AI & Codex Experience Experience using OpenAI Codex or similar AI-assisted development tools is highly preferred. We want a developer who knows how to use modern AI development tools to: Accelerate development Debug NinjaScript Refactor code Build internal tools Analyze logs Create testing utilities Develop reporting tools Work with APIs and integrations Automate repetitive development processes AI should accelerate your work—not replace your understanding of C#, NinjaTrader, or trading-system architecture. Requirements The ideal candidate has: Strong NinjaTrader 8 experience Strong NinjaScript experience Strong C# development skills Previous automated strategy development experience Understanding of futures markets Understanding of algorithmic/systematic trading Experience with backtesting and forward testing Experience deploying strategies in live or realistic trading environments Strong understanding of risk management Strong debugging skills Ability to analyze trading statistics Ability to document work clearly Excellent communication Ability to work directly with management Ability to think strategically rather than simply complete coding tickets High attention to detail Ability to protect proprietary source code and trading logic Major Plus Previous strategies with documented live deployment experience Quantitative research experience Python SQL APIs Git/GitHub OpenAI Codex Tradovate Brokerage APIs Prop firm experience Trading-system licensing or protection experience Software product development experience Who We're Looking For We want someone who can do more than say: "The backtest looks profitable." We want someone who can ask: Is the strategy robust? Is it overfit? What happens after commissions and slippage? Does it behave correctly in live execution? What is the realistic drawdown? How should position sizing change based on account size? Can this system establish a credible live performance history? What would make this system valuable enough to become a premium commercial product? That is the level of developer we are looking for. When Applying, Please Answer How many years have you worked with NinjaTrader 8 and NinjaScript? Please describe automated futures strategies you have previously developed. Have any strategies you developed been deployed to live brokerage accounts? Have you worked with systems that have established documented live performance histories? What futures markets have you developed systems for? Explain how you prevent overfitting when developing a trading strategy. How do you account for commissions and slippage in testing? Explain the difference between a backtest, forward test, simulation, and live performance. How would you investigate a strategy that performs well historically but poorly live? What NinjaTrader order-management methods do you normally use? Have you built multi-timeframe or multi-instrument NinjaTrader strategies? What experience do you have with NinjaTrader Brokerage or Tradovate? Have you developed systems specifically for prop firms? What experience do you have with Python, APIs, GitHub, or Codex? Please provide examples of previous NinjaTrader work or code samples you are legally permitted to share. Please describe one automated system you helped take from initial concept through live deployment. How would you evaluate whether a trading system is strong enough to become a premium/high-ticket commercial product? We are looking for a long-term developer who can help KJD Capital build serious automated futures products—not simply complete one-off NinjaScript projects.

title: Executive Assistant to Owner | Construction Company | Operations + AI + GHL
job_title: Executive Assistant to Owner | Construction Company | Operations + AI + GHL
description: Executive Assistant to Owner | Construction Company | Operations + AI + GHL **Full-Time | Remote | Long-Term | U.S. Company We are looking for an exceptional Executive Assistant to work directly with the owner of a growing U.S.-based construction and landscape company. This is **not a traditional Virtual Assistant position**. We are not looking for someone who waits for a list of tasks, completes them, and waits for the next instruction. We are looking for someone who can become the owner's right hand: organize chaos, close open loops, follow up relentlessly, turn ideas into action, improve systems, and eventually help lead other specialized VAs. The goal of this position is simple: **Take work off the owner's plate and make sure important things actually get finished.** As trust and capability grow, this role has the potential to develop from Executive Assistant into an operations and VA leadership position. About the Company We are a growing U.S. construction and landscape design-build company. We are actively building a more systemized company where responsibilities, workflows, SOPs, dashboards, automation, and accountability replace owner dependency. We are currently building Version 1 of our operating system and intend to reach Version 3 within approximately one year. You will play an important role in helping us get there. Who We Need Non-Negotiable **1. Excellent spoken and written English** You will communicate directly with the owner, employees, applicants, vendors, subcontractors, leads, and customers. You must be confident communicating by email, chat, video, and phone. **2. Extremely organized** You naturally create order out of messy information. You track commitments, deadlines, delegated tasks, follow-ups, documents, meetings, and priorities without allowing things to disappear. **3. Resourceful** When you encounter something you do not know, your first instinct should be to investigate, research, use AI, review available documentation, and attempt to solve it. We value intelligent questions, but we do not want someone who immediately pushes every problem back to the owner. **4. Extreme accountability** You take ownership of outcomes. If you make a mistake, you acknowledge it, correct it, and improve the system so it is less likely to happen again. As your responsibilities grow, you must also be comfortable holding other team members accountable to clearly defined expectations. **5. Consistency** We value consistent, focused execution more than occasional bursts of excellent work. We need someone dependable every day. **6. Comfortable working directly with a high-expectation owner** The owner moves quickly, generates many ideas, delegates heavily, and expects direct communication and follow-through. Part of your job will be turning that information into organized priorities and completed actions. **7. Strong follow-through and project management** You do not consider something complete because an email was sent. You follow the task until the outcome is actually achieved. **8. Positive, solutions-oriented mindset** We want someone who communicates problems clearly without creating drama, excuses, or unnecessary negativity. Identify the problem. Recommend a solution. Execute. **9. Strong AI fluency** You should already be comfortable using tools such as: * ChatGPT * Claude * AI research tools * AI-assisted writing and analysis We want someone who uses AI as leverage, not someone who simply copies and pastes AI output. **10. Leadership mindset** There is significant growth potential in this role. We see progression happening in three stages: **Stage 1: Execution** Master delegated responsibilities, ask intelligent questions, document what you learn, and execute consistently. **Stage 2: Systems** Understand how our company operates and help us improve workflows, SOPs, dashboards, automation, and our overall operating system. **Stage 3: Leadership** Help recruit, onboard, manage, and hold accountable specialized VAs. We eventually expect to employ approximately 5-10 specialized VAs across different functions. The person who proves they can lead those people creates significant additional value to the company and significant financial growth potential for themselves. Bonus Points We will be especially interested if you naturally: * Identify company bottlenecks * Document processes * Build SOPs * Recommend automation * Determine what should be delegated * Help identify the correct role needed * Recruit people to own those responsibilities * Build systems that reduce reliance on the owner We want someone who eventually sees a recurring problem and thinks: **"How do we make sure this never needs the owner's attention again?"** ## Helpful Experience, But Not Required You do NOT need experience with every platform below. Ability to learn quickly matters more than checking every software box. Experience with any of the following is helpful: * Google Workspace * Google Drive * GoHighLevel * QuickBooks Online * ClickUp * Project management software * CRM systems * Construction software * Construction, landscaping, home services, or trades businesses What You May Eventually Own Responsibilities will be handed off progressively rather than all at once. Potential responsibilities include: Executive Support * Manage inbox and calendar * Maintain the owner's master priority list * Turn voice notes, conversations, and brain dumps into organized action items * Schedule meetings and appointments * Prepare the owner for meetings * Track delegated work until completion * Follow up on commitments and deadlines Operations * Build and maintain SOPs * Organize Google Drive * Maintain company documentation * Update dashboards and trackers * Coordinate projects and internal follow-ups * Help improve company workflows * Identify recurring bottlenecks * Help build our operating system Communication * Follow up with employees * Follow up with vendors * Follow up with subcontractors * Follow up with applicants * Manage website inquiries * Help manage Facebook messages * Handle inbound business calls * Make outbound calls when needed CRM + Lead Administration * Help administer GoHighLevel * Monitor incoming leads * Coordinate customer follow-up * Maintain CRM organization * Make sure leads do not fall through the cracks Recruiting * Help recruit employees and VAs * Screen applicants * Coordinate interviews * Maintain applicant pipelines * Help onboard future team members Administrative Support * Basic QuickBooks Online coordination * Research purchases * Research vendors * Research software * Gather information needed for decisions AI + Systems * Use ChatGPT and Claude for: * SOP development * Research * Drafting * Analysis * Process documentation * Meeting preparation * Summaries * Workflow improvements Marketing Administration * Google Business Profile management * Basic social media coordination * Review and reputation follow-up * Coordinate marketing-related administrative work This role will evolve considerably as trust is earned. Work Expectations This is a **full-time, long-term position**. Because you will communicate with a U.S.-based company and eventually handle inbound communication, you must be comfortable working substantial overlap with **U.S. Eastern Time business hours**. We are looking for someone who wants to build a career with one growing company, not simply add another temporary client. What Success Looks Like Within your first few months: * The owner has fewer open loops to remember * Important follow-ups happen without reminders * Delegated tasks are tracked until completion * Information becomes easier to find * Meetings are better prepared * Company systems become more documented * Administrative work increasingly moves away from the owner * Problems come to the owner with proposed solutions * You become someone the owner can confidently hand responsibilities to Long-term: **Owner → EA → specialized team** Instead of the owner coordinating everyone individually, you increasingly help organize execution and surface only the decisions or exceptions that actually require the owner. This is a full-time position and work hours are tracked using time-tracking software, including activity tracking and periodic screenshots. This is used for accountability and time verification, not constant micromanagement. Performance is primarily evaluated based on execution, reliability, communication, and results. How to Apply **The first word of your application must be: SUPERB47** Applications that do not follow this instruction will not be considered. Please answer all six questions: **1. Why are you a better fit for an Executive Assistant position than a traditional Virtual Assistant position?** **2. Tell us about one situation where you noticed a problem and solved it without waiting for your boss to tell you exactly what to do.** Be specific about: * The problem * What you did * The result **3. What AI tools do you personally use each week, and what do you actually use them for?** **4. What CRM, project management, accounting, or business software have you used?** Clearly explain your experience level with each. **5. Record a 2-minute Loom video introducing yourself.** Tell us: * Who you are * Your most relevant experience * Why this position interests you * Why you believe you would be good at it Include the Loom link in your application. **6. What monthly salary are you seeking for a full-time position?** Also include: * Your current employment status * Your availability to start * Whether you can work U.S. Eastern Time business hours Please do not submit a generic AI-generated cover letter. Short, specific, thoughtful answers are far more valuable to us. We are looking for someone who wants responsibility, growth, and the opportunity to become an important part of building a company.

title: People & Culture Operations Specialist

Candidates who have administered another HRIS may also be considered if they have strong relevant experience and can quickly adapt to new systems. Payroll Coordination -Support payroll administration for employees in the United States and United Kingdom by: -Preparing and reviewing employee updates that affect payroll. -Coordinating new employee additions and terminations with payroll. -Processing salary increases, promotions, bonuses, and other compensation updates. -Checking that leave and employee status changes are properly reflected in payroll. -Reviewing payroll information for accuracy before processing. -Maintaining supporting documentation and securing required internal approvals. -Investigating discrepancies and coordinating necessary corrections. -Keeping records of payroll changes and their effective dates. -Working with Finance, payroll providers, and the Head of People & Culture when required. Previous experience supporting U.S. and/or UK payroll administration is strongly preferred. -Leave & Time-Off Support -Handle the administrative coordination of employee leaves of absence. -Keep leave-related records, documentation, correspondence, and dates accurate within the HRIS. -Support maternity, parental, medical, and other applicable leave processes. -Ensure required approvals and documentation are collected and properly maintained. -Monitor key leave dates and follow up on outstanding requirements. -Administer company time-off policies through BambooHR. -Respond to routine employee questions concerning leave and time-off procedures. -Escalate complex leave, legal, or employee-relations concerns to the Head of People & Culture. -Apply leave and time-off procedures consistently according to company policies. Recruitment Coordination Provide administrative support across the hiring process, including: -Arranging interviews across different time zones. -Coordinating candidate availability with hiring teams. -Keeping candidate information and recruitment activities updated in the ATS. -Managing candidate communications during the recruitment process. -Coordinating interview schedules and following up with interviewers. -Preparing offer documentation and assisting with the candidate-to-employee transition. -Coordinating pre-employment and onboarding requirements. -Maintaining recruitment trackers and monitoring candidate progress. -Supporting the Head of People & Culture and hiring managers with additional recruitment-related activities. Training & Compliance -Manage administrative activities within the company’s employee training platform. -Assign required training to employees. -Monitor completion of mandatory and role-specific training. -Follow up on incomplete training requirements. -Maintain training records and completion reports. -Assist with implementing new policies, procedures, and required employee acknowledgements. -Maintain documentation related to policy acknowledgements and other required records. -Support compliance monitoring and reporting activities. -People & Culture Support The People & Culture inbox will be an important part of your day-to-day responsibilities. You will: -Monitor incoming employee and manager requests. -Ensure questions and requests receive timely responses. -Handle routine HR and policy-related inquiries when appropriate. -Direct matters to the appropriate People & Culture team member or internal stakeholder. -Monitor open requests until they are fully resolved. -Follow up with employees, managers, or stakeholders when additional information or action is needed. -Recognize urgent, sensitive, or complex matters and escalate them promptly. -Help provide employees with a professional, responsive, and supportive People & Culture experience. HR Policies & Compliance -Become familiar with the company’s employee handbook, HR policies, and internal procedures. -Support the consistent application of established HR policies. -Maintain and update HR templates, documentation, procedures, and employee-facing materials. -Assist with policy rollouts and employee acknowledgement activities. -Keep current policy and procedure records organized. -Prior exposure to U.S. and UK employment practices and employment law is preferred. -Identify matters that require escalation rather than attempting to independently resolve complex legal or employee-relations issues. Process Improvement & HR Organization A key focus of this position is helping create a more organized, efficient, consistent, and scalable People & Culture operation. You will be expected to: -Evaluate current HR processes and identify areas where efficiency and accuracy can be improved. -Create and maintain SOPs, checklists, templates, trackers, and other process documentation. -Establish repeatable approaches for recurring People & Culture activities. -Identify manual tasks that can be simplified, standardized, or automated. -Help clarify ownership and deadlines for recurring HR activities. -Keep electronic employee and departmental records well organized. -Make HR information easy to find, understand, and hand over when necessary. -Monitor outstanding actions and ensure they are followed through to completion. -Assist the Head of People & Culture with ad hoc projects, reporting, audits, and other operational initiatives. What We’re Looking For Must-Have Qualifications: -At least 2 years of professional experience in Human Resources, People Operations, HR Operations, or a related HR function. -Strong English communication skills, with the ability to clearly communicate HR decisions and information. -Demonstrated ability to independently manage HR administrative activities such as employee records, documentation, trackers, onboarding/offboarding, training or learning-management platforms, and recurring HR processes. -Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Word, including spreadsheets, employee data, reports, trackers, and HR documentation. -Hands-on experience with an HRIS and Applicant Tracking System (ATS) or employee management system. description: About the role I own a financial services firm in the US serving small businesses. I need valuations and industry research for specific companies, one engagement at a time. You don't need "valuation analyst" in your job title — you need to have done the work. Solid grasp of valuation methodology: DCF, market multiples, SDE vs. EBITDA, normalization adjustments, discount rates You understand why multiples differ by industry and can explain it in plain language Strong Excel or Google Sheets. You build models, not fill in templates. Comfortable with research databases. I provide subscription access — you need to know how to use these tools and where their data has gaps. Able to work down to county and metro level, not just national averages Extremely organized. Assumptions documented, sources cited, nothing hand-waved. Written and spoken English strong enough for live calls and clean written deliverables Available for calls during a set overlap window with US Central Time Nice to have CPA, CFA, or progress toward either Big 4 or mid-tier audit background US market experience, especially Texas Small business valuations, not just large-cap Hands-on with BizBuySell, DealStats, IBISWorld, PitchBook, or similar Industry research or market sizing experience How you'll communicate with me I'm busy and I d ---------- fast. Your reporting should be: Short. Bullets, not paragraphs. Lead with the conclusion. Visual where it helps. A table or chart beats a wall of text. Decision-oriented. Give me the number, the range, and what drives it. Channels: Teams is primary. iMessage or WhatsApp for urgent items. Video calls with camera on are required — you'll walk me through your findings and defend your assumptions live, not just send a file. Access and security Read-only access to whatever financial records an engagement requires, plus a dedicated inbox for project materials — not my personal accounts. No shared logins. Research platform access is provided under my subscription and is for my engagements only. Client information is confidential; you'll sign an NDA before the first project. How to apply Read this carefully. Applications that skip a step get deleted without a reply. Start your message with the word MULTIPLE on its own first line. Attach one piece of analytical work you produced — a valuation, a financial model, a market research report, or a comparable company analysis. Redact company names and anything confidential. Your own work only, not a template or a class project. Write a summary of that file's conclusion as if you were sending it to me. Maximum 100 words, bullets only. Record a video under 2 minutes, camera on: your name, your background, and a walkthrough of the file — specifically, how you arrived at your key assumption and why you're confident in it. In one or two sentences: name an industry you've analyzed and where you found the multiple or benchmark data for it. Tell me your rate — per project or per hour — and what text app you use.

title: Head Chef & Production Captain
description: The Head Chef & Production Captain is the primary team leader responsible for theday-to-day execution of TGS production operations. The role is responsible for leading the production team, executing approved production plans, maintaining product consistency, enforcing production standards, training production personnel, coordinating with the Sanitation Officer and Quality Control Officer, and ensuring that all production activities are completed safely, efficiently, accurately, and according to TGS standards. The Head Chef & Production Captain serves as the hands-on leader of the production floor and acts as the bridge between management and the production stewards. The position is expected to lead by example, maintain discipline and accountability within the production team, identify operational issues, and promptly escalate concerns to the Management. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES These are some of the tasks but are not limited to: 1. Production Leadership & Daily Operations Lead and supervise the production team during daily operations. Execute the approved daily and weekly production plan. Assign tasks and responsibilities to production team members based on production requirements and manpower availability. Monitor progress throughout the production cycle. Ensure production targets are achieved within the required timeline. Ensure all production activities follow approved recipes, specifications, and SOPs Monitor workflow and identify bottlenecks, delays, or manpower issues. Take immediate corrective action within the scope of authority and escalate major concerns to the Management. Ensure the production area remains organized and operational throughout the shift. Lead by example in work ethic, discipline, cleanliness, and adherence to company standards. 2. Production Team Leadership Serve as the immediate team leader of the Production Team. Conduct daily task delegation and production briefings. Train new production personnel on approved production procedures. Coach team members on proper techniques, productivity, quality, and workplace discipline. Monitor attendance, punctuality, productivity, and work performance of production personnel. Identify training needs and recommend additional training or corrective action when necessary. Promote teamwork, accountability, respect, and professionalism within the production team. Report significant performance or disciplinary concerns to the Management. 3. Production Standards & Recipe Compliance Ensure all products are prepared according to approved TGS recipes and specifications. Ensure proper measurement and handling of ingredients. Maintain consistency in product weight, appearance, texture, taste, and overall quality. Prevent unauthorized changes to recipes, formulations, or production methods. Immediately report any proposed recipe or process changes to the Management for proper approval. Ensure only the latest approved recipes and production instructions are used by the production team. 4. Quality Control Coordination The Head Chef is responsible for production-level quality monitoring, while the Quality Control Officer maintains the designated quality control function. The Head Chef shall: Conduct routine checks throughout production to identify obvious quality issues. Ensure production personnel follow approved product specifications. Coordinate with the Quality Control Officer during inspections and QA 5. Sanitation & Food Safety Coordination 6. Training & Development 7. Research & Development (R&D) 8. Inventory & Material Coordination 9. Production & Inventory Assistant Supervision 10. Incentive Report & Production Documentation 11. Production Reporting 12. Equipment & Production Area 13. Confidentiality & Recipe Protection QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS Bachelor’s Degree in Culinary Arts, Food Technology, Hospitality Management, Food Science, or a related field is preferred. A Culinary Arts diploma/certificate with substantial relevant industry experience may be considered in lieu of a bachelor’s degree. At least 3–5 years of hands-on experience in professional kitchen, bakery, pastry, commissary, central kitchen, or food production operations. At least 1–2 years of experience in a supervisory or team-lead capacity, preferably managing a production or kitchen team. Strong hands-on knowledge of food preparation, production processes, recipes, portion control, food costing, and product consistency. Demonstrated experience in production planning, task delegation, workflow management, and meeting daily/weekly production targets. Knowledge of food safety, sanitation, HACCP principles, GMP, and proper food handling procedures. Experience coordinating with Quality Control, Sanitation, Inventory, and other production support functions. Ability to train, coach, and supervise production personnel effectively. Strong understanding of recipe compliance, standard operating procedures (SOPs), batch production, measurements, and quality standards. Experience with inventory and raw-material coordination, including monitoring usage, availability, and wastage. Experience in product development/R&D, recipe testing, product improvement, or production trials is an advantage. Ability to work in a fast-paced production environment and manage multiple priorities. Willingness to be hands-on in production activities and lead the team by example. Strong communication skills and the ability to coordinate effectively with Management and cross-functional teams. Proficiency in basic Microsoft Office/Google Workspace or other tools used for production reporting and documentation.

title: Video Editor
description: VIDEO EDITOR (Remote, Full-Time) - Be Part of AEF’s Pioneer Editing Team Dear Future Team Member, This isn’t just another editing job. This is your chance to be part of something special: a heart-driven team that powers cinematic wedding films and premium corporate productions for clients across Asia. We’re AdvantEdge Films (AEF) — a Singapore-based creative studio behind the brand Memory Makers. >> Why Memory Makers? Because our work goes beyond cutting clips. But we’re just getting started — and we want you to be part of shaping what’s next. As we grow, we’re opening 1–2 seats for talented editors to join our pioneer team. >> Get in early. But if you want your edits to move people… to make couples cry happy tears… to see your work truly matter and to know you’re part of something bigger — then you’ll fit right in. It’s about finally having the stability, recognition and growth path that so many freelancers dream about — but rarely find. Your family will see that what you’re doing is a real career, not just a side hustle. >> Here’s what you can look forward to when you join us: • A Clear Career Path — No more endless freelancing without direction. You’ll grow step by step: Trainee >> Junior Editor >> Senior Editor >> Lead Editor. Your hard work will actually lead somewhere. • Stable Monthly Salary (pegged to market rates) — Paid on time, every month. No chasing clients, no dry months. And as you grow, so does your pay. • Pioneer Team Advantage — Get in early and grow with us. As we expand, you’ll be first in line for leadership opportunities. • Onboarding & Training That Sets You Up To Win — Clear SOPs, style guides and real feedback — no guessing games, no being left alone. You’ll always know how to succeed here. • Premium Portfolio You’ll Be Proud Of — Work on cinematic wedding films and corporate projects that showcase your craft — projects you’ll be proud to say, “I edited this.” • Performance Bonuses & Growth Perks — Whether it’s a brand-new laptop, sponsored overseas travel (Company Retreats), or courses to sharpen your skills, we reward commitment and excellence. >> How Life is Gonna Look Like For you Joining AEF means stepping into a role where you can do what you love — without the chaos and uncertainty that freelancers often face. Here’s how your day-to-day will actually look like: Work From Anywhere (100% Remote) - No commuting, no traffic, no wasted hours. You’ll have the freedom to work from the comfort of your home (or anywhere with a good connection). Whether that’s your family home, a quiet café, or even during a brownout with your backup plan — you stay in control of your day. A Stable Rhythm, Clear Expectations - You’ll work Mon–Fri, 10:00 AM to 6:30 PM (SGT). But we’re not here to micromanage or track your every move. What matters most is that key deliverables are done on task, on time, on target, and to the required standards. Weekends are yours for family, rest, or passion projects. Stay Connected, Never Isolated - Even though we’re remote, you’ll never feel like you’re working alone. With quick daily stand-ups and weekly reviews (Mon, Wed, Fri), you’ll always have support, feedback, and a team that’s got your back. A Team That Values You - You’ll work with creatives who genuinely care about quality and storytelling — and about each other. Every edit you deliver contributes directly to making couples cry happy tears, or helping businesses shine. Clarity + Growth Built In - Your projects will come with clear briefs, SOPs and feedback loops. That means less confusion, fewer revisions and more space for you to focus on doing what you do best — creating edits that move people. In short: Your days will feel structured, purposeful and supported. You’ll edit amazing stories, grow your skills, and still have time for yourself and your loved ones. >> What You’ll Actually Do Craft Wedding Highlight Reels - Take the most emotional moments of a wedding day and weave them into a cinematic highlight that brings couples to happy tears and rewatch for years to come. Bring Corporate & Event Stories to Life - Edit impactful films that help brands connect with their audiences — from events to marketing videos. Follow Clear SOPs, Add Your Creative Touch - Use AEF’s editing frameworks and style guides as your foundation — while bringing in your storytelling instincts to make each video feel alive. Grow Through Feedback Loops - You’ll collaborate with our Singapore Team using Slack, WhatsApp and GDrive. Master the Full Editing Flow - From raw >> first cut >> fine cut>> final cut, you’ll manage projects end to end, sharpening not just your skills but your confidence as an editor. >> How Your Career Growth is Gonna Look Like This isn’t a dead-end editing gig. We want you to grow with us. • 0 - 3 months (Probation): Trainee Think of this as your warm-up stage. You’ll learn our style, workflows and editing frameworks while working on real projects. By the end, you’ll already have a feel for what it means to edit stories the AEF way — consistent, on-brief and emotionally powerful. • 1-2 Years: Junior Editor Now you can hold your own fort. You’ll deliver quality edits with fewer revisions, adapt confidently to our brand styles, and start building a premium portfolio of wedding highlights and corporate projects you’ll be proud to showcase. • 3-4 Years: Senior Editor This is where you level up. You’ll take on more complex projects with your own cinematic touch, handle edits with minimal supervision, and even begin guiding newer editors. Your work won’t just meet expectations — it’ll inspire. • 5 Years & Beyond: Lead Editor (Pioneer Team Track) As part of the founding team, this is the fast track. You’ll set standards, refine SOPs, mentor juniors, and lead large or high-profile projects. You’ll have a direct hand in shaping AEF’s editing division as we grow. Join now, and you won’t just be another editor — You’ll be among our founding editors, with the fastest path to leadership and long-term impact. And years from now, you’ll look back with pride knowing you weren’t just freelancing gig to gig — you were part of the original pioneer team, building a career your family can celebrate. >> Compensation & Stability We offer competitive pay pegged to the Philippine market rate for full-time video editors, and will assess fairly based on your portfolio and experience. No more chasing invoices, no dry months, no waiting games. Stable monthly income. Paid on time, every time. title: marketing manager (CPG)
description: A profitable, growing US-based specialty tea CPG brand (~15% YoY, 130K+ lifetime orders, warehouses in the US, Canada, UK, and EU) selling primarily through Shopify and TikTok Shop, built on authentic sourcing, education, and a founder-creator with millions of followers who is, today, the company's entire marketing engine. The brand ships frequent new product lines (two launches in the next four months alone) and runs a quarterly subscription program (~2,000 members) that is the growth core. The founder built the entire business on organic content and the company has never run paid ads. Marketing today is a set of good ideas with no owner: email, loyalty, referrals, collabs, community, contests. Your job is to become that owner, and to build the machine around the founder's audience instead of depending on it. One thing to know before you apply: nothing customer-facing here is AI-generated. All creative is real and hand-made. That is the brand's identity, not a policy. See "How this company uses AI" below; it will d ---------- whether this role is for you. The role You own marketing end to end. This is a content-led brand: high-quality entertainment and infotainment IS the acquisition engine, and everything you do in paid, email, and lifecycle has to interact coherently with the organic machine, not run beside it. You understand how paid and organic feed each other and you manage brand awareness as one system. The mandate runs in a deliberate order. First, find the leaks and build the scoreboard: subscription drop-off, paused members, one-time buyers, and the KPI system to see it all. Second, stand up paid media and get the email and lifecycle machine performing. Third, once the fundamentals run, expand into organic collaboration: creator collabs, bigger content plays, deeper integration with the founder's production. The wrong hire walks in asking for a big ad budget. The right hire walks in asking where the money is leaking and what the data says. You are a player-coach, weighted toward player early. You personally run media strategy and media buying (today's AI-powered buying tools make this a one-person job at this scale) until the marketing arm grows enough to justify dedicated hands, at which point you help define that hire. The email specialist reports to you and executes email and lifecycle operations under your direction. You'll also coordinate with the rest of the small team around marketing: a Shopify/ecommerce operations person and the founder's YouTube account manager. On creative: you are close to a creative director who never creates. The founder is the creator. He likes performing, he WANTS to make ads, and he already has some in production. Your job is to make that enthusiasm strategic and intentional: understand the brand's edges and preferences deeply enough to direct email, paid media, and collab work cohesively without ever violating the ethos, and to tell him exactly what the data says he should make next. He will make you one great ad at a time, not fifteen mediocre ones. This is not a strategy-deck job. You make tactical judgment calls on messaging, audiences, offers, and budget the same day they come up, and you push initiatives to done. The unofficial title is "the person who makes marketing ideas stop dying in the parking lot." What you'll do Find the leaks and build the scoreboard Diagnose subscription drop-off: who leaves, when (the drop after box two and three is the known weak point), and why Quantify how much meat is on the bone: lapsed members, paused subscriptions, one-time buyers who never subscribed, email list segments that never converted Think in the levers that multiply the business: LTV, AOV, CAC, churn, and net-new customers. When the data to see a lever doesn't exist, you fix the measurement system so it does Run the win-back loop for paused and lapsed members, working with the internal AI survey systems that surface why people pause Run paid media yourself Launch paid ads from zero (Meta first, TikTok second) with an intro test budget, personally owning media strategy and buying with modern AI-powered tools Approach ads from first principles: early paid is a learning instrument. Breaking even early on is a perfectly good outcome; the bar is don't bleed money while collecting the data that verifies hunches and shapes the growth plan, then refine and iterate from there Run the full range deliberately: put cash behind organic content that's already working, test odd angles, and run boring direct-response ads. You have to be comfortable with both the weird and the boring Build the creative testing plan around the founder's content and the ads he has in production; brief him on what to make next based on what the data says Own holiday-season ad buying (Oct through Feb is the season) Earn the budget: scale spend only as unit economics prove out, and be the person telling the founder when NOT to spend Own email, lifecycle, and loyalty Set strategy for and manage the email specialist, who executes email and lifecycle operations under your direction Evolve loyalty into a VIP program and fold the referral program into its tiers Multiply LTV and AOV: bundles, premium tiers, subscription upgrades, win-backs Expand the organic machine (stage two, after the fundamentals run) Lead creator collab strategy, including YouTube collaborations: you set the strategy and direct it, with outreach and legwork resources added as the workload materializes Surface-manage the content production workflow (the founder has a YouTube account manager) enough to keep it moving and connected to the rest of marketing Deepen the paid-organic loop as both sides mature Run the machine Build the marketing calendar and own cross-channel coordination across Shopify and TikTok Shop: a constant new-product launch cadence (next two launches already scheduled for mid-September and November) and the holiday season Direct the founder's creative production: batched, specific asks with clear briefs, on his rhythm Run the AI marketing stack for analytics and orchestration, and teach: make sure the whole team understands what the numbers say and why Be our eyes and ears on the marketing org: as channels prove out, you define the next roles the team needs and help us scope them Who survives here The founder runs this company as a creator and an artist. He will not work 70-hour weeks, he will not sit in frequent syncs, and he does not want to be managed hard. There are standing weekly team calls and brand-alignment checks; beyond that, you get batched, well-prepared asks and a lot of autonomy. The person who thrives: a first-principles thinker who asks "what are the alternatives" and comes at problems from angles, cares deeply about brand ethos and being genuine, and is flexible and adaptable when the picture changes. Low ego, systems-builder, gets energy from ownership rather than access, treats the founder as a scarce production resource and designs the work around that constraint. A sense of humor is close to required: the brand runs on it. The person who fails: needs frequent alignment meetings, wants to "workshop the vision" repeatedly, bulldozes the founder's constraints in the name of growth, or is too proud to run boring ads. How this company uses AI The company runs a deliberate split: aggressive AI adoption in operations, a hard wall around anything creative or customer-facing. This role sits exactly on that line and has to hold it. The wall (creative side) - Nothing customer-facing is AI-generated. No AI images ever, no AI-written copy shipped as-is. This is brand identity, not a preference: the entire premise of the brand is that everything is real. Real sourcing trips, real photos, real people. - The standard is cultural, not just a rule. Real example: product photos came back with dust on them right before a launch, the founder was unreachable, and the team spent hours manually retouching the dust out rather than AI-recreating the images, because they knew that is what he would want. That instinct is the hiring bar. - AI-assisted drafting is tolerated only when the shipped output is written by hand or aggressively reviewed by hand. AI passing as human is the sin. A previous team member put an obviously AI-generated image into an internal test email; it never shipped and it was still treated as a serious culture violation. The embrace (operations side) - The company builds internal AI agents aggressively: live inventory and logistics answers for the CS team, a demand-prediction model for new products, and a customer survey loop that maps the customer journey. - The founder's stated goal is a middle road: full transparency with the team about how AI is used, so nobody feels they are training their replacement, and AI kept as far from the creative side as possible. What this means for you - You manage the AI marketing setup: agent-driven ad analytics and orchestration (think "this ad is overperforming in one region, redivert budget"), AI-powered media buying, research, segmentation, reporting, workflow. Analytics and orchestration, yes. Generating ads, images, or copy that ships, no. - You are also the translator: part of the job is making sure everyone on the team understands what the AI spend analytics say and why, in plain language. - The founder believes AI slop is destroying trust in faceless content and low-tier influencer marketing, and that this brand's realness becomes MORE valuable as that happens. He has watched an agency lose his business by sending an unchecked AI-generated proposal. Pitching AI-generated creator content or mass AI outreach in your interview ends the interview. What you've done before - 6+ years across multiple marketing channels with your own hands: paid social, email/retention, loyalty or referral programs, influencer or community marketing - Hands-on media strategy and media buying: you have personally planned, bought, and optimized paid media, not just supervised an agency doing it - Food and beverage CPG experience is required: you have marketed a consumable product people buy repeatedly, and you understand replenishment cycles, taste-driven loyalty, and launch cadence - Subscription experience is required: you have managed a subscription service and its retention economics, not just one-time - - DTC - DTC ecommerce experience; Shopify fluency expected, TikTok Shop experience a strong plus - Startup or small-team environments: you have been the whole marketing department before, comfortable with scrappiness and wearing every hat, not corporate structure and big budgets - You understand content-led brands: experience running or working inside media/content production is a real asset, because here the content IS the marketing - Ran frequent product launches end to end as the project manager, not just the channel owner; this brand ships new lines constantly and the calendar never stops - Managed at least a small team or agency relationships; comfortable being the strategy layer for an executor - Worked directly with a founder or creative director and can tell us how you adapted to them - Comfortable managing AI agents and tools in your workflow; clear-eyed about where AI belongs and where it does not - You should genuinely enjoy the product. Tea, tea culture, or Chinese culture as a real personal interest is close to a requirement here: this team lives the product, and it shows in the work. Comedic sensibility is a plus, since the founder's content runs on humor

title: Part-Time GoHighLevel (GHL) Newsletter Production Assistant

Build and maintain approved email campaign funnels/sequences in GHL from supplied strategy, workflow logic, copy, audience rules, and tracking requirements. Build/edit the HTML email and ensure correct desktop/mobile rendering. Apply the approved email template and branding. Insert and test supplied links, buttons, CTAs, images, and destination URLs. Apply supplied UTM/tracking parameters correctly. Configure supplied GHL tracked links, click tracking, and campaign actions exactly as instructed. Verify that tracked buttons/links/actions record correctly before send. Use only the audience/Smart List/segment instructions provided. Check desktop and mobile presentation. Prepare test sends and clearly identify PASS/FAIL issues. Prepare campaigns for scheduling only after required checks pass. Never initiate a live newsletter send without explicit authorization. Record campaign URLs, test results, status, and final campaign information in our existing tracking system. After live campaigns, retrieve and record campaign statistics. Campaign statistics include recipients; delivered; hard and soft bounces; spam complaints; unsubscribes; unique opens; unique clicks; click-through rate; top clicked links/buttons/actions; replies where available; sample requests; quote requests; orders; coupon usage; attributable revenue where available. Ability to confirm that tracking is actually recording correctly. Experience retrieving and reporting GHL email campaign statistics. Strong attention to detail. Experience checking responsive email formatting. Good written English. Ability to follow supplied source material and campaign instructions exactly rather than redesigning or rewriting them. Reliable communication and ability to work independently. This role does NOT own newsletter strategy; copywriting; audience policy; CRM/GHL architecture; unsubscribe architecture; automation strategy/design; final send authorization. The assistant may implement approved tracking/actions, but does not invent campaign automation or audience logic. Paid Test — Maximum 90 Minutes Shortlisted candidates will complete a paid test using a supplied newsletter package. The test will evaluate: accurate GHL/HTML build; correct subject, preheader, body, links, buttons, CTA, and formatting; desktop/mobile presentation; link and destination testing; correct supplied UTM/tracking setup; correct tracked-link/button/action configuration; ability to explain how they verify that those actions are recording correctly; ability to locate and retrieve campaign delivery, bounce, unsubscribe, click, top-link/action, and available conversion statistics; test-send QA and clear identification of problems; total time used. To apply, please include: How long have you worked directly in GoHighLevel? What GHL email/newsletter work have you personally done? Have you built or edited HTML emails directly in GHL? What experience do you have with tracked links, UTMs, click tracking, and GHL actions? What email campaign statistics have you personally retrieved and reported? Please describe one campaign you built, tested, tracked, and reported yourself. Are you comfortable starting at 3–5 hours/week? Your requested hourly rate. Put GHL NEWSLETTER at the beginning of your application subject.

description: Most people d ---------- whether to watch a YouTube video in just a few seconds. The channel is new, and I'm building it full-time from the ground up. I handle the thumbnail strategy and concept for every video myself. description: Join Solve Outsource and Help Build the Foundation for Client Success! How would you handle a situation where rental income has been misallocated between two properties? Tell me about a time when you found inconsistencies in property-related financial data. What steps did you take? ???? Tenant Accounts & Rent Management A tenant claims they already paid rent, but there’s no record in the system. How do you investigate and resolve this? How do you track and follow up on delinquent accounts without damaging the tenant relationship? What process do you follow to ensure tenant payment entries are accurate and timely? ???? Vendor & Expense Management If two invoices come in for the same service but with different amounts, how would you determine which one to process? What steps do you take to ensure recurring expenses don’t exceed the approved budget? Have you ever caught an error or overcharge from a vendor? How did you handle it? ???? Reporting & Cash Flow Management How do you make sure your monthly reports are both accurate and ready on time, especially when you are managing multiple deadlines? If you identify a cash flow shortfall for a property, what immediate actions would you take before escalating it to the Finance Manager? What steps do you take to ensure accuracy in budget vs. actual reporting? ???? Compliance & Documentation How do you make sure financial activities comply with lease agreements and company policies? If an auditor asks for supporting documentation and you discover missing records, what would be your approach? Tell me about a time you had to handle sensitive or confidential financial information. How did you protect it? ???? Coordination & Escalation A property manager pushes you to approve an expense that doesn’t follow policy. What would you do? How do you balance communication between landlords, tenants, and internal teams when dealing with financial disputes? Tell me about a time you escalated a financial issue to leadership. What was the outcome? ???? Tools & Technical Skills Walk me through how you would set up a spreadsheet in Excel to track rent payments for 50+ tenants. How do you avoid errors when multiple tea ---------- mbers are updating the same QuickBooks or Excel file? Have you ever suggested or implemented a change to improve financial workflows? What was the impact? ???? Problem-Solving & Judgment Imagine you discover that monthly reconciliations were skipped for two months. How would you catch up and ensure no errors were missed? You’re under pressure to close books, but you notice a suspicious transaction. Do you escalate immediately or finish closing first? Why? What’s the biggest financial mistake you’ve ever made, and how did you correct it? ???? Commitment & Fit This role requires handling multiple properties/accounts at once. How do you manage time and prioritize when everything feels urgent? How do you stay calm and accurate when deadlines overlap and you’re under pressure? What motivates you more: accuracy, deadlines, or recognition? Why? Some of it is documented better than the rest. The standard from here is simple: nothing is called done until it's demonstrated working, estimates are real and kept, and every hour is accounted for. If that sounds like pressure, this isn't your role. If it sounds like how good engineering should work anyway, keep reading. What I hire for, in order: finishing what you start; proving it works before you call it done; clear, precise written and spoken English, because nothing can get lost in translation here; being extremely organised; and an eye for detail, for design, and for what premium quality actually is. Our clients pay for premium and can tell the difference. ## What you'll inherit Python/FastAPI services on Docker Compose on a Mac Mini production box behind Cloudflare Tunnels and Tailscale. Next.js front end on Vercel. Postgres on Supabase with Alembic migrations and row-level security. GitHub Actions CI gating deploys. Stripe with webhooks. Cold email through the Instantly and Apollo APIs, plus Hunter, Google Places and Companies House. A conversational diagnostic funnel and a partner commission engine. HeyGen and ElevenLabs for generated video and voice. An e-signature flow, scheduled jobs, LLM agents with per-run cost tracking, and Slack alerting. All of it real. All of it in production today. ## What you'll actually do The 30-day trial starts on day one and runs alongside the outgoing developer for the rest of his notice period, so you inherit the platform safely before he's gone. In the trial: - Take the handover repo by repo and service by service until you can change any of it safely, documenting what you find as you go. - Close out what's in flight with evidence: outbound email, payments, the diagnostic funnel, partner tooling. - Prove it. For every piece you touch, a short recorded walkthrough showing it working, not a message saying it does. A candidate who takes clean ownership of the platform and closes out the handover meets the bar. One who backs every claim with a proven demo is doing this role well. One who also spots what's inefficient or under-specified and improves the plan is exceptional. After the trial you own the platform and its scope. Next on ScaleSage: a client platform, a content production product, and a search and AI visibility product. All scoped, all yours to build. Beyond ScaleSage, the rest of TMC as it needs you: the Belly Full Seasonings brand site and e-commerce, Legacy Curriculum education app builds, AI video, voice and persona production, the internal content factory that serves our own brands, dashboards and tools, and client systems as ScaleSage grows. This is not a phased roadmap. You're a TMC team member shipping what the business needs. Variety is the deal. ## How we work - A daily written end-of-day report: completed, active, blocked, next, with hours. - Four status words for all work: architected, coded, live, proven. Only the last one counts as done. - One live demonstration call a week, working things shown on screen, plus short recorded walkthroughs. - Blockers raised the same day they appear. - Time tracked through an agreed tool. - Any other client work disclosed in writing before it starts. - Written and async by default. You propose your fixed weekly windows and we agree them, with at least three hours a day of overlap with Bangkok and Manila working hours. ## The path Nothing here is promised. Everything is earned. The path is written into the contract: part-time to prove the fit, expanded part-time as you deliver, full-time when the business and your delivery earn it, then technical lead across the group's ventures, hiring the people beneath you. Full-time follows delivery, not time served. Bonuses are paid for execution: when you ship a big build, solve a complex problem, or hit a real milestone. Pay rises are earned through consistency, reliability and loyalty over time. The money, straight: $600 a month for a fixed 20 hours a week to start, through the trial and into the part-time retainer. I'm a founder, not a corporation. I pay what I can afford now and grow it as the business grows, and the ladder above is how that happens. I won't sell you a dream. I'll tell you the ceiling is high for the right person. ## What you get - Real freedom in how and when you work, inside the windows we agree. - A direct line to the founder. Decisions in hours, not weeks. No red tape. - Claude Code and Codex provided as your daily tools. - Ownership. No product manager sitting between you and the work. - Variety across ventures instead of one narrow codebase. - Paid monthly in arrears, on time, every time, by Wise or crypto (USDT or USDC on the network of your choice). - Trips to Thailand for in-person workshops, expenses covered. - A company that wants you to grow into leading its technology. ## Must have - Python and FastAPI in production - Postgres and Supabase: schema design and migrations, background jobs and schedulers, webhooks - Next.js and React on Vercel, Tailwind, responsive layouts that look right on a phone, CSS animation and motion, and the ability to take a Figma or visual reference and build it to the pixel - Stripe subscriptions and one-off payments, REST integration with third-party SaaS - Email sending and deliverability - Docker, CI pipelines, Linux, Cloudflare Tunnels, backups and restore, secrets handled properly - LLM APIs, prompt and agent design, evaluation of outputs - AI-native: you use Claude Code, Cursor or similar every day, and you can tell when they're wrong - Automated tests, QA on real devices, security and data-protection basics - Documentation good enough that someone else could take over - Excellent written and spoken English. You'll write daily reports and speak on a weekly demo call. English is tested live on the screening call. - Self-managing: able to take a brief and ship without hand-holding - Reliable internet and a quiet workspace If you're strong in most of these and honest about the rest, apply. ## Nice to have - Experience taking over an existing, under-documented codebase and making it safe to change - Background in a client-services environment where "done" has to be provable to someone else - Content production tooling, or SEO and AI-search-visibility work - Working knowledge of UK GDPR and PECR as they apply to cold email: suppression, unsubscribe handling, eligibility - AI voice agents (Vapi, Retell, ElevenLabs) and AI image and video tools (Runway, Flux, HeyGen, Higgsfield) - RAG and vector databases (pgvector or similar) - An active GitHub with public commits in the last 90 days - An entrepreneurial mindset: you've tried to build something yourself - Willingness to travel to Thailand, and openness to relocating long-term if the fit is right You don't need to know everything already. But you need to be the kind of person who can learn a new tool fast, build with it, and document what you did so the rest of the team can use it. ## How to apply Start your message with the word PROVEN, so I know you read this properly. Then send: 1. A recorded video, under three minutes: why this role, and how you'd approach the first week. No script needed. I want to see how you think and hear how you speak. 2. Answers to these seven questions, written directly in your application. Real examples only. Generic answers are exactly what this is screening against. 1. Send a link to something you've built where the front end is yours, and tell me one thing about it you'd fix if you had an hour. 7. You'll have Claude Code and Codex. Confirmation you can start at the $600 retainer for 20 hours a week, or your number with the reason. Plus your full-time rate and your earliest start date. 5. One thing you'd push back on or improve in this brief. It shows me you think, not just execute. 6. One question for me about the role, the company, or me. If your answer to question four is "that has never happened to me", this isn't the role for you. If you used AI to help write your application, say which tool. I respect AI use. I don't respect pretending. Applications missing any of the above are not read. ## Process Written screen, then a 30-minute video call where English is tested live and you screen-share one production system you built, then a short technical test, then two client references, then a contract with a 30-day trial. We're hiring now. The trial starts as soon as the right person is found, while the current developer is still here to hand over. J W-Blake Founder, The Machine Collective

title: Vendor sourcing specialist (USA)
description: Vendor Sourcing Specialist (USA) Task: Beverage Co-Packer Outreach & Research Summary I’m launching a premium sparkling functional beverage (clean caffeine + L-theanine + electrolytes, 12oz can) and need someone to call/contact a list of beverage manufacturers and co-packers, ask a defined set of questions, and log the answers in a shared tracker. Some companies have already been contacted by email — this role is about getting the missing information by phone (or follow-up email if a call isn’t possible), plus doing first-touch outreach to a second list of manufacturers we haven’t contacted yet. This is not a sales or persuasion role. You’re gathering factual information: capabilities, pricing, minimums, samples, and compliance documentation. Structure: Paid Trial, Then Full Job Phase 1 (trial, paid separately): Call the 5 priority companies flagged below, get complete answers, log them in the tracker in the format specified. I’ll review the quality before assigning the rest. Phase 2 (if trial goes well): Full remaining list — both follow-up calls and new outreach. Priority 5 for Phase 1 These are the highest-leverage first calls — a mix of fastest-path-to-sample and one-stop shops that could shortcut needing separate formulation + canning partners: 1. LTBB (Lucky To Be Beverage) — has ready, market-tested stock formulas; fastest path to an actual sample, no formulation wait. 2. MacroCap Labs — vertically integrated (formulation + canning + fulfillment in one facility); could solve the “nobody wants to formulate” problem in a single vendor. 3. Big Brands — turnkey formulation + co-packing specifically for functional/adaptogen beverages; another one-stop candidate. 4. BevZero — full turnkey concept-to-product, 30+ years in the category; broad, established option. 5. Chapter Foods — not a manufacturer, a matchmaking/consulting service. Worth calling early since a good conversation here could surface better-fit co-packers than cold-emailing the rest of the list one by one. What You’re Calling About A premium sparkling clean-energy + hydration beverage. Manufacturer-facing context, if asked: 12 oz aluminum can ~40–60mg caffeine (prefer clean/natural source like green tea), L-theanine, electrolytes Zero/very low added sugar, low calorie Exploring both private-label (their existing stock formula) and semi-custom routes Two flavors/SKUs planned for initial launch Early-stage: want a first sample round before committing to volume Once Stephanie identifies the company, the first ask on that call is to get the specific contact’s name and direct phone number, same as every other entry. Information to Get on Every Call 1. Private label or custom only? Do they have existing stock formulas we can taste/sample, or is everything custom-built? 2. MOQ — per SKU, in cans/cases, for both stock and custom (if different) 3. Pricing — indicative per-can cost at initial volume and at scale; any setup/tooling fees 4. Samples — can they send samples, cost (if any), and turnaround time 5. Lead time — production and reorder lead times 6. Formula ownership/exclusivity terms — do we own the formula, or is it licensed/shared 7. Compliance documents (get copies or confirmation these exist): GFSI audit certificate (SQF Level 2/3, BRCGS, or FSSC 22000) FDA facility registration number Product-specific HACCP plan Most recent third-party food safety audit report (e.g. Silliker, Eurofins, NSF) 8. Warehousing / direct-to-distributor capability — can they ship direct to distributors or do we need our own 3PL How to Log Results Update the shared tracker (MVM Manufacturer Tracker) after every call — don’t batch it. (To be provided) For each company, fill in: - Status/Latest Action (date + what was discussed) - MOQ - Pricing/Financial Notes - Capability/Fit Analysis (your read on whether they’re a real fit) - The four compliance columns (mark received/confirmed/not available) I*f a call goes to voicemail or gets no answer, log the attempt and try again — don’t mark it “no response” after one try. Notes Be upfront that this is an early-stage brand exploring options, not placing an order yet — don’t overpromise volume. If a company says they don’t do private label or the MOQ is clearly incompatible (e.g. 100,000+ units for a first pilot), don’t spend time pushing — log it as disqualified and move on. Questions during the trial phase: reach out before guessing.
