Our Ideal Candidate We are looking for someone who is: * Naturally conversational and personable * An excellent listener * Curious rather than pushy * Comfortable asking questions * Confident speaking with business owners and decision-makers * Comfortable making outbound calls * Resilient when people say no * Highly coachable * Organized and consistent * Comfortable working independently * Able to follow a defined process without sounding robotic Experience **Required:** * Previous B2B appointment-setting, outbound sales, or business development experience * Strong spoken English * Experience communicating with US-based prospects strongly preferred * Reliable internet and professional home-office setup * Ability to work during US business hours **Strongly preferred:** * Experience selling to or setting appointments with schools, childcare organizations, education companies, or other organizations in the education sector * Experience speaking with owners, directors, administrators, or other decision-makers * Experience selling services, SaaS, technology, marketing, or other consultative solutions * Experience with GoHighLevel or another CRM * Experience using a sales dialer or outbound calling platform * Demonstrated appointment-setting results Education-sector experience is a strong advantage but not required. We would rather hire an excellent B2B communicator who is highly coachable than someone with education experience who is not a strong conversational salesperson. What Success Looks Like This pilot is about determining whether outbound appointment setting can become a viable acquisition channel for Enroll & Shine. We will evaluate: * Quality conversations * Number of decision-makers reached * Qualified appointments booked * Appointment show rate * Quality of appointments * Prospect feedback * Consistency of follow-up * Overall results relative to the time and cost of the pilot **Success is not simply making a high number of calls. We care about the quality and outcome of the activity.** Pilot & Hiring Process The initial engagement will begin with a **small paid trial** so both sides can determine whether the role is a good fit. Shortlisted candidates will be asked to: 1. Submit a brief voice recording 2. Participate in a short video interview 3. Complete a live appointment-setting role-play 4. Complete a small paid trial with real prospects If the pilot produces strong results and the working relationship is a good fit, we may extend the engagement. There is **no guarantee of ongoing work beyond the initial pilot**. To Apply Please include: * A brief description of your B2B appointment-setting experience * The types of businesses and decision-makers you have contacted * Your experience calling US-based prospects * Your typical daily call volume * Any appointment-setting results or metrics you can share * The CRM and calling systems you have used * Your availability during US business hours * A 60-second voice recording introducing yourself and explaining why you believe you would be a strong fit for this pilot We are looking for a **real conversationalist, not a script reader**. If you are curious, resilient, coachable, and genuinely enjoy talking with business owners, we'd like to hear from you.

The game has many different management screens, menus and systems, so we need an artist who can help build a consistent, reusable UI asset library that works properly inside a game engine. title: Senior Paid Media Strategist
description: Senior Paid Media Strategist Location: Remote, EST Hours Type: Full-Time, Independent Contractor Experience: 5+ years in paid media strategy, with enterprise budget ownership Pay Range: $25-$27 per hour, based on experience Reports to: Media Team Lead Start Date: ASAP About the Role We're looking for a Senior Paid Media Strategist to take full ownership of one of our largest and most complex accounts, a multi-location US home improvement brand running a seven-figure annual media program across Google Search, Performance Max, Meta, Bing and Local Services Ads, alongside a focused portfolio of established eCommerce and lead-gen clients. This is a senior, client-facing seat, not an execution seat. You'll run the weekly client sync and the monthly performance review yourself. You'll own the numbers, the change log, and the tracking behind both. We're not looking for someone to run a plan handed to them. We're looking for the person the client trusts to say what's working, what isn't, and what we're doing about it this week. One thing sets this role apart from most senior PPC jobs: you own measurement integrity. At this budget level, a broken conversion action or a mis-scoped tag isn't a reporting inconvenience. It silently misdirects bidding and burns real money before anyone notices. We need someone who treats GA4 and Google Tag Manager as core craft, not as someone else's job. You'll be supported by a Media Team Lead, a Performance Marketing Specialist, dedicated creative and email teams, and an internal AI stack we actively build on. What you won't have is someone checking your work for you. That's the level we're hiring at. What You'll Be Doing Account Ownership & Client Leadership Serve as the senior day-to-day owner for your accounts, including our high-ticket lead gen clients Lead weekly client syncs and monthly performance reviews independently: set the agenda, present the numbers, defend the recommendation Translate business goals (cost per appointment, cost per lead, revenue targets) into media plans, and translate results back into plain language Own budget pacing and reallocation across markets, products and platforms; flag over- and under-delivery before month-end, not after Maintain a clean, current change log so every performance movement can be traced to a decision Measurement & Tracking Integrity Own GA4 and Google Tag Manager configuration for your accounts: conversion actions, event definitions, triggers, consent and cross-domain setup Validate that platform-reported conversions reconcile with CRM and call-tracking reality, and investigate discrepancies before a client raises them Multi-Location & Multi-Market Paid Search Build and scale campaigns across multiple metro markets with distinct budgets, demand curves and seasonality Manage Local Services Ads alongside Search and Performance Max, and understand how they cannibalize and complement each other Structure geo, product and campaign naming and UTM conventions so reporting rolls up cleanly by market and product line Cross-Channel Strategy Plan across channels rather than platform by platform, and build a funnel view that accounts for audience differences, intent stages and creative fit Lead campaigns across Google (Search, Shopping, Performance Max), Bing, Meta, and where the client fits, YouTube, TikTok, LinkedIn and Reddit Steer platform AI intentionally (Performance Max, Advantage+, Demand Gen, AI Max) using guardrails, negatives, exclusions and asset control rather than accepting defaults AI-Assisted Execution Use our internal AI stack (Claude, Claude Code, and connected data tools) for analysis, QA, reporting and creative ideation Build lightweight automations that scale what you do: anomaly alerts, budget checks, feed monitoring, insight surfacing Contribute what you learn back to the team's shared workflows and documentation Quality Ownership Ship work QA'd. Peer review is a check, not your safety net. Nothing leaves your hands that you haven't verified yourself Apply our standard: don't send anything you wouldn't read yourself. That applies to reports, client emails, and change logs equally Escalate early and specifically. Surface risk while it's still cheap to fix Who You Are 5+ years managing paid media for US clients, with meaningful time in an agency or consulting environment You've personally held accounts at $100K+ per month in managed spend and can speak to how that changes decision-making Genuinely strong in GA4 and Google Tag Manager. You've built and debugged conversion tracking yourself, not briefed someone else to do it Expert-level in Google Ads (Search, Shopping, Performance Max) and confident across Meta and Bing A confident, proactive communicator in English, written and spoken, at a C1 level or above. You can hold a room with a client, simplify complexity, and deliver bad news well. All candidates complete an English and a DISC assessment as part of our process Comfortable owning the number and being accountable for it Detail-obsessed in a specific way: you check your own work before anyone asks You see problems coming. Pacing drift, a tracking gap, a rising cost per lead, a platform change that will hurt the account next month. The client hears it from you first, with a plan attached Curious about AI and automation, and already using it in your workflow Self-directed and reliable in a remote, globally distributed team Bonus if You Have High-ticket local lead-gen experience Multi-location or franchise paid search experience Server-side tracking, GA4 privacy configuration, or BigQuery / Looker Studio reporting Experience with product feed management (Google Merchant Center, Meta catalogs, DataFeedWatch, Channable) Experience with TV, direct mail or other offline media running alongside digital, and attributing across them Built automations or scripts with Google Ads scripts, Zapier, Supermetrics or similar Hours 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM US Eastern, Monday to Friday. We're a global team spread across five timezones and our clients are US-based, so overlapping the US day is what keeps us working as one team rather than five. There's flexibility within those hours, shaped mostly by client calls and internal meetings. We'll talk through what a typical week looks like at an interview. If working US Eastern hours doesn't fit your life, please don't apply. We'd rather both of us know now. Why ScaledOn? 100% remote with a global team Paid time off. Every contractor on our team gets it Flexible, performance-driven culture Direct access to innovative tools and early AI adoption Performance-based bonuses tied to KPIs Paid certifications and professional development We hire contractors intending to keep them. Several of our team have been with us for 8+ years About Us ScaledOn's mission is to support the dreams, aspirations, and growth of our clients through ecommerce marketing. We do this by delivering strong work as a collaborative team and helping businesses grow profitably. We take shared risks for shared rewards, keeping us closely aligned with our clients' goals. We are a 100% remote, work-from-home company offering location flexibility within a global, team-oriented environment. Compensation for this role is commensurate with experience. This is an independent contractor position. Our hiring process includes several assessments, including English and DISC assessments, followed by a paid 90 day trial period to ensure a strong mutual fit. We go into every contract expecting it to be a long-term one. As part of how we work, all tea ---------- mbers are required to track their working time using Hubstaff. Hubstaff is used for task-level time tracking and supports transparency, accurate billing, and fair workload management across the team. How to Apply Please complete the online application: ---------- The application includes two short items in addition to your background, one being a voice note just a heads up so you’re prepared when you start the application. 1. A written answer (5-10 sentences). Your largest account by monthly ad spend. Name the client or describe the business, the average monthly spend you were responsible for, and the exact months you managed it. Example: "US home services franchise, ~$120K/month across Google and Meta, March 2024 to February 2026 2. A voice note (60-90 seconds). Recorded on your phone, no video needed. Walk us through a month where an account you owned missed its target. What happened, what you told the client, and what you changed.

title: Project Manager/ Contract Administrator
description: PROJECT MANAGER / CONTRACT ADMINISTRATOR Full-Time | Remote – Philippines | Australian Construction & Landscaping About RYCOR RYCOR is a Melbourne-based landscape construction company specialising in high-quality residential and commercial landscape projects. We are looking for an experienced Project Manager / Contract Administrator based in the Philippines to join our team full-time. This is not simply an administration role. We are looking for someone who can take ownership of projects from quote acceptance through to project completion and handover, working closely with our Australian project managers, site teams, subcontractors and suppliers. Your objective will be simple: Help us deliver projects on time, on budget and as profitably and efficiently as possible. ⸻ THE ROLE You will become a key part of our construction and project management team. Once a project has been accepted, you will assist in managing and coordinating the project through the entire construction lifecycle. Your responsibilities will include: Project Setup & Pre-Construction * Review accepted quotations, plans, specifications and scopes of work. * Prepare project files and construction documentation. * Break projects into stages, activities and milestones. * Develop detailed project schedules and construction programs. * Identify long-lead-time materials and procurement requirements. * Prepare procurement schedules. * Identify required subcontractors and suppliers. * Obtain and compare supplier and subcontractor quotations. * Prepare and maintain project-specific scopes of work. * Assist with mark-ups and amendments to construction plans. * Ensure the construction team has the required information before works commence. Procurement & Materials Take ownership of procurement coordination, including: * Material take-offs and ordering. * Supplier quotation comparisons. * Purchase order preparation and tracking. * Delivery scheduling. * Monitoring lead times. * Confirming quantities and specifications. * Coordinating deliveries with site teams. * Identifying opportunities to reduce material costs. * Preventing unnecessary freight, double handling and wasted materials. You will be expected to continually look for opportunities to improve project margins through better procurement and planning. Subcontractor Management Assist with managing subcontractors throughout each project, including: * Issuing scopes of work. * Obtaining and comparing quotations. * Negotiating pricing where appropriate. * Scheduling subcontractors. * Confirming site dates. * Providing plans and project information. * Tracking subcontractor progress. * Reviewing invoices against quoted and completed works. * Identifying variations or discrepancies. * Following up outstanding work and documentation. You must be comfortable communicating directly with Australian subcontractors and suppliers. Project Scheduling Develop and maintain detailed construction programs showing: * Project stages. * Activities and tasks. * Dependencies. * Labour requirements. * Subcontractors. * Procurement deadlines. * Material delivery dates. * Key milestones. * Client decisions required. * Critical-path activities. * Target completion dates. We currently use Microsoft Teams and intend to increasingly use Microsoft Planner for project scheduling and management. You will be expected to help us develop and improve these systems. Project Financial Management A major part of this position is helping RYCOR deliver projects profitably. Responsibilities will include: * Maintaining project budgets. * Tracking committed costs. * Backcosting projects. * Comparing estimated versus actual costs. * Monitoring labour expenditure. * Monitoring material expenditure. * Monitoring subcontractor expenditure. * Identifying potential cost overruns early. * Tracking variations. * Assisting with progress claims and invoicing. * Forecasting project cost-to-complete. * Reporting projected final project margin. * Identifying opportunities to improve project profitability. We don’t want someone who simply reports that a project has gone over budget. We want someone who identifies potential problems early and helps the team prevent them from happening. Construction Administration You will also assist with: * Project documentation. * Filing and document control. * Scope-of-work preparation. * Plan mark-ups. * RFIs. * Variations. * Purchase orders. * Subcontractor documentation. * Meeting notes. * Project reports. * Progress claims. * Invoicing. * Backcosting. * Practical completion documentation. * Defect lists. * Project handover documentation. ⸻ SOFTWARE, SYSTEMS & AI RYCOR is focused on using technology, systems and AI to make our projects more efficient and profitable. Our current systems include: * Simpro – estimating, project/job management, purchasing and financial tracking. * Groundplan – construction take-offs, measurements and estimating. * Microsoft Teams – internal communication and collaboration. * Microsoft Planner – project planning, task management and scheduling. * Microsoft Excel – project budgets, reporting, analysis and financial tracking. * Microsoft Outlook and Word – communication and documentation. Previous experience with Simpro and/or Groundplan would be highly regarded, particularly within an Australian construction environment. AI Experience – Highly Regarded RYCOR is actively looking at ways to incorporate AI and automation into our construction and project management processes. Candidates with practical experience using AI tools will be highly regarded. We are particularly interested in people who can demonstrate how they have used AI to improve areas such as: * Project administration. * Construction scheduling. * Procurement. * Cost analysis. * Budget tracking. * Reporting. * Scope-of-work preparation. * Meeting summaries and action lists. * Document preparation. * Data analysis. * Subcontractor comparison. * Estimating and take-offs. * Process automation. We are not simply looking for someone who has used ChatGPT occasionally. We are particularly interested in candidates who can demonstrate how they have practically used AI or automation to save time, reduce administration, improve accuracy or increase project profitability. ⸻ WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR We are looking for someone with previous experience in: Construction Project Management and/or Contract Administration. Experience working remotely for an Australian construction company would be highly regarded. Experience in any of the following would also be beneficial: * Landscaping * Residential construction * Commercial construction * Civil construction * Quantity surveying * Estimating * Procurement * Contract administration You must have excellent spoken and written English. We intend to provide you with an Australian phone line, and you will regularly communicate directly with: * RYCOR employees * Project managers * Site supervisors * Subcontractors * Suppliers You therefore need to be confident, professional and comfortable having construction-related conversations over the phone. ⸻ WHAT WE WANT TO SEE FROM APPLICANTS We are particularly interested in evidence of what you have actually achieved. Please don’t just send us a résumé telling us that you have managed construction projects. Show us. As part of your application, please provide examples or a portfolio demonstrating how you have previously managed construction projects. We would particularly like to see examples of: 1. Project schedules or construction programs you have created. 2. Project budgets or cost trackers you have managed. 3. Procurement schedules you have developed. 4. Subcontractor management systems you have used. 5. Cost-to-complete or project forecasting reports. 6. Backcosting or estimated-vs-actual reporting. 7. Plan mark-ups or construction documentation you have prepared. 8. Examples where you identified a problem early and prevented a project from exceeding its budget or timeline. 9. Examples where you improved the profitability of a construction project. 10. Examples of systems or processes you introduced that made construction projects more efficient. 11. Examples of how you have used AI or automation in your previous roles. For at least one previous project, we would like you to explain: Original Contract Value: What was the project worth? Original Budget / Target Margin: What was the expected construction cost and profit? Your Role: What were you personally responsible for? Project Program: How did you plan and track the project? Challenges: What problems occurred during construction? Your Actions: What did you personally do to resolve them? Final Result: Was the project delivered on time? Financial Result: Was it delivered on budget, and what happened to the project margin? Lessons: What would you do differently next time? ⸻ THE PERSON WE WANT The successful candidate will be someone who: * Takes ownership. * Is highly organised. * Communicates confidently. * Thinks ahead rather than reacting to problems. * Understands construction sequencing. * Understands project financials. * Is commercially minded. * Is comfortable questioning costs. * Negotiates with suppliers and subcontractors. * Identifies risks early. * Follows people up without needing to be asked. * Enjoys building systems and improving processes. * Can manage multiple projects simultaneously. * Is confident adopting new technology. * Looks for opportunities to use AI and automation to improve the way they work. * Understands that project management is ultimately about time, cost, quality and communication. Most importantly, we want someone who treats the company’s money as though it were their own. If there is a better, faster or more profitable way to deliver something, we expect you to identify it and bring it to the team. ⸻ HOW SUCCESS WILL BE MEASURED Success in this position will be measured by: * Projects delivered to schedule. * Projects delivered within budget. * Gross profit maintained or improved against estimate. * Accurate procurement and purchasing. * Reduced project downtime. * Materials and subcontractors organised ahead of site requirements. * Accurate and timely project financial reporting. * Variations identified and processed promptly. * Accurate project documentation. * Effective communication with site teams, suppliers and subcontractors. * Problems identified before they affect project cost or program. * Increased use of systems, AI and automation to reduce unnecessary administration. * Continuous improvement of RYCOR’s project management systems. This is an opportunity to become an important long-term member of RYCOR’s construction team and have a genuine influence over how our projects are delivered.

job_title: YouTube Video Editor for a Hawaii Real Estate Team (Long-Term, Remote)
description: Aloha! We are a top-producing real estate team on Oahu, looking for a long-term video editor who can grow into a larger role over time. You will help us create useful, engaging YouTube videos for people making real estate decisions in Hawaii. See the video and thumbnail examples we like: ---------- WHAT YOU WILL EDIT - Long-form talking-head videos supported by property footage, local B-roll, maps, photos, and graphics for Hawaii buyers and sellers - Property tours, neighborhood and new-construction videos, and practical videos - One thoughtfully designed thumbnail for each long-form video, using our brand assets and reference examples - Roughly one separately paid Short per long-form video, ordered after the long-form receives final approval WHAT MATTERS MOST - Story instincts: find the strongest takes, build a clear opening, and keep the video moving naturally - Clean editing, including dialogue audio, music, color, captions, and pacing - Clear motion graphics such as maps, comparisons, text callouts, charts, or simple explainers - Thoughtful, effective thumbnail design that gives viewers a reason to click, works with the video's title, and matches our brand and reference examples - Good visual judgment: supporting footage should fit Hawaii, the subject, and the people being discussed - Timely, responsive communication: meet agreed deadlines, reply promptly, and raise questions or potential delays early - Resourcefulness and ownership: suggest practical solutions when something is missing or unclear, and keep the edit and files organized through final delivery Thumbnails are a core part of the role. We want a clear idea, strong composition, and readable text at phone size. Use our brand assets and examples as a starting point, and bring your judgment to each video's thumbnail. Use supplied property footage and local B-roll where relevant. When additional visuals are needed, source or create imagery that fits Hawaii, the subject, and the people being discussed. For a specific property, use its actual footage or photos and flag missing assets rather than substituting another home or inventing one. AI-assisted visuals and advanced motion graphics are welcome when they help, but are not required in every video. Check AI output carefully for geographic and factual accuracy, natural movement, and visual glitches. Only use results that look realistic and hold up during playback. TOOLS Use Adobe Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, or comparable professional editing software that supports an organized, editable project handoff. We use Google Drive for files and ---------- or an equivalent platform for timestamped review. Tell us which tools you work with; we can agree on the setup together. HOW WE WORK - Volume: Two to four long-form videos per month, with room to grow as our team and editor have capacity. - Footage and first draft: Expect new footage on Tuesdays. The video draft and thumbnail are due within 72 hours of receiving the complete footage and brief. - We provide: Footage, the video's goal, available outlines or scripts, brand assets, and visual references. - You lead the edit: Shape the story, choose the strongest takes, source or create appropriate supporting visuals, add graphics, refine sound and color, and design the thumbnail. Bring your creative judgment and flag gaps early. - Before review: Watch the full edit and check the thumbnail for pacing, spelling, audio, visual accuracy, and brand fit. - Feedback: We leave consolidated timestamped notes in ---------- or an equivalent platform. You carry those through to the final files. - Working hours: You manage your own working hours. Revision and Short deadlines are agreed separately and may extend beyond the initial draft window, including into a weekend by agreement. We work asynchronously with one agreed weekly check-in. PAY AND DELIVERABLES A few shortlisted applicants will be invited to a $50 USD paid test using our supplied footage: a 3 to 4 minute edit and one thumbnail. We will share the brief and confirm the 72-hour deadline before you begin. Each finalist is paid for completing the agreed test, whether or not they are hired. $100 USD per standard video package, normally an 8 to 12 minute finished video, including: 1. Within 72 hours: a complete long-form video draft with supporting visuals, graphics, audio, and color work in place, plus one fully designed thumbnail ready for review. 2. After feedback: the final video export and thumbnail, with one main revision and one final correction pass included. 3. At handoff: organized editable video and thumbnail files, relinkable media, and a short delivery note identifying any sourced or AI-assisted assets. Shorts are $20 each, ordered separately after the long-form video receives final approval. Expect roughly one Short per long-form video. Turn a strong moment into an engaging vertical video with a clear opening, natural pacing, readable captions, and supporting visuals or sound where they help. Deliver a finished vertical export and include its editable sequence in the project handoff. We agree on the number, length, and deadline before you begin. TO APPLY Please include all four items below. We’ll only review complete applications, including two relevant video samples and one thumbnail you designed. Please send direct links, not a general portfolio folder. Start your message with OAHU STORY, then include the following, using existing work for your samples: 1. Only your two most relevant video samples for this role, including at least one talking-head video with supporting B-roll or graphics. Use direct links to those videos rather than a full portfolio folder or a long list. Tell us what you handled and point to one timestamp showing your best work. 2. One thumbnail you designed, with a sentence about the idea behind it. 3. Your editing software, current availability, and when you could start. 4. A short answer: What would you do if the supplied footage did not include an important visual mentioned by the speaker? If you have polished AI-assisted video work, you may also share a timestamped example and briefly describe your input and cleanup. This is optional.

title: Editor
description: Role Overview We are looking for skilled editors who can generate an article from our brief using AI and then edit it into something a real reader would finish and a client would be proud to publish. You are not a writer and you will not be starting from a blank page. You own the piece from generation through to the version that goes to the client. You will work across client industries, currently weighted towards healthcare, with expansion into finance and other verticals. This is not proofreading. Grammar and spelling are the floor, not the job. The hard part is the human factor. AI will hand you something fluent, confident and completely generic, and your job is to turn that into something that reads like a person who knows the subject wrote it. The finished article has to answer what the reader actually searched for, say something the first three Google results do not, and carry none of the tells that make a reader stop trusting the page. Engagement Terms - Tasks are posted in a WhatsApp group on a first come, first served basis, the same group you are added to once you have applied with the subject line I'm your star editor and cleared the test. The first person to claim a task owns it. If it is not delivered by the stated deadline, it goes back to the group. - There is no minimum volume, but consistent editors get first sight of the bigger jobs. - You will be given the client's style guide, the SEO brief and the target keyword for each piece. Key Responsibilities Writing quality - Generate the first draft from our brief, target keyword and the SERP competitors using AI. Prompt it with the brief, the competitor pages and the client's existing copy rather than a one-line instruction. The raw output is your starting point, never your deliverable. - Strip the AI tells before anyone else sees it: uniform paragraph lengths, em dashes, empty openers, hedged claims, lists with nothing specific in them, and confident statements with no source behind them. - Ensure the text is free from grammar, spelling and punctuation errors. - Keep the language user-friendly and concise. Cut filler. - Match the client's house voice, including US or UK spelling as instructed per client. Reader experience - Logical: establish authority and credibility using supporting evidence such as statistics, academic publications, case studies, testimonials, Google reviews and relevant endorsements. Emotional: create a sense of assurance and connection. Use the PEEL structure (Point, Elaboration, Example, Link) and keep it authentic and relatable. - Highlight and sharpen the client's unique selling points so the piece does not read like every competitor's page. SEO checks - Confirm the draft answers the search intent behind the target keyword. If the ranking pages are comparisons and our draft is a sales page, flag it. - Target keyword present in the H1, the first 100 words, the meta title and two or three H2s, placed naturally and never stuffed. - Meta title and meta description within length, keyword front-loaded, appearing once, no filler calls to action. - Correct heading hierarchy with no skipped levels. - Internal links to the relevant service pages, with descriptive anchor text. - Flag missing or unsourced claims and any section that is too thin to stand. Business and compliance - Place calls to action strategically, for example after treatments, after benefits, and after the "why choose us" section, rather than one block at the end. - For healthcare clients, ensure the copy complies with the Healthcare Services (Advertisement) Regulations. Flag superlatives, guarantees, comparative claims and testimonials that cannot stand. Preferred Skills - Minimum 1 year of editing experience. Agency or content-marketing experience preferred. - Working knowledge of SEO. Deep technical SEO is a bonus, not a requirement. - Able to drive AI tools well (ChatGPT, Claude or similar), and more importantly able to tell when the output is generic and fix it. - Comfortable working from a brief and a style guide without hand-holding. - Excellent written English, native or near-native fluency. - Able to switch between US and UK spelling on instruction. - Bonus: healthcare or finance content experience. How to Apply - Please attach your CV and two published pieces you edited, and name one of them you are still proud of. - Only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

title: Video Editor — FPV Drone & Real Estate | DaVinci Resolve + After Effects
job_title: Video Editor — FPV Drone & Real Estate | DaVinci Resolve + After Effects
description: Video Editor — FPV Drone & Real Estate | DaVinci Resolve + After Effects | Long-Term Rate: $10–15 USD/hour, depending on experience Hours: 10–20 per week to start, growing toward full-time Schedule: Flexible. No fixed shift, no required US hours. Software: DaVinci Resolve + After Effects (required), Gyroflow (required) Type: Long-term. I am hiring one editor to grow with. Before you apply This is a specialist role, not a general editing role. I need a colorist and motion graphics editor who understands FPV drone footage, log color pipelines, and sound design at a professional level. If you cannot grade log footage in DaVinci Resolve and build motion-tracked graphics in After Effects, please do not apply. I would rather you save your time. If you can do those things, keep reading — the work is genuinely interesting and I pay every week, on time. About Vantage Studio I run a cinematography company in Northern California. I shoot FPV drone work, aerial cinematography, and real estate video for brokerages, commercial property owners, local businesses, and motorsports teams. I am FAA-certified with waivers to fly over people and over moving vehicles. That matters for you because it means the footage you will be cutting is not typical drone work. It is close, fast, and shot inside spaces most operators are not legally allowed to fly. Why I am hiring: I have been editing everything myself, and I no longer have the hours to do it properly at the volume my clients need. I am not looking for someone to replace my taste. I am looking for someone to execute at my standard, consistently, so I can stay behind the camera. Because I edit all of this myself, two things are true. I know exactly how long each task takes. And my feedback will be specific and technical — you will never get "make it better" from me. The standard I am chasing Below are reference examples of the caliber of work I am building toward — one for each type of work you would be doing. For each, I have noted exactly what I want you to look at. Commercial real estate — ---------- → [ what to notice, e.g. Use of FPV Drone shots and motion-tracked text, as well as a professional, constrained editing style while still being engaging ] Trending residential reel — ---------- → [ what to notice, e.g. the pacing, and how the tracked text sits in the scene, transitions, flow, sound design] FPV one-take — ---------- → [ what to notice, e.g. the sound design and where the hidden cuts are, smooth speed ramps and flow, motion treacked logo ] FPV one-take, second example — ---------- → [ what to notice, e.g. the sound design and flow of the speed ramps ] Aerial map/motion graphics — ---------- → [ what to notice, e.g. how the lot lines and street names stay locked to the ground, the level of detail in aerial and satellite maps ] If this is the level you already work at, we should talk. The work — four types 1. Residential real estate reels — 1 to 3 per week Short-form vertical listing videos with modern, trend-aware editing: Motion-tracked subtitles and text Masking and object isolation Smooth speed ramps AI-assisted effects and AI home renders / visualizations Clean grade from log footage 2. Commercial real estate videos — roughly 1 per week (not guaranteed every week) The same craft, executed more conservatively and more corporate: Polished, professional subtitle design FPV drone sequences with motion graphic text integrated into the shot Aerial map graphics built in After Effects, with motion-tracked overlays: street names, surrounding business callouts, lot lines and property boundaries, satellite map pulls Deliverables per property vary — long-form horizontal, vertical reels, short teasers 3. FPV one-take videos — the flagship work Single continuous drone takes for local businesses (gyms, restaurants, retail), motorsports (sprint car racing), and commercial property tours. These are the pieces that win me clients, and the edit is what makes or breaks them. Required: Gyroflow stabilization. Not optional. I need someone who has genuinely used it. Log color grading in Resolve, matched across the entire take Silky, invisible speed ramps Seamless hidden cuts — masked transitions as the drone passes behind an object Real sound design: whooshes tied to camera movement, ambience beds, actor dialogue, layered SFX, audio that fades naturally as the drone approaches and passes a subject, and comfort with EQ, compression, and other processing when a source needs fixing 4. Short-form social and paid ads Content for Vantage Studio itself — promotional videos, educational social content, and paid ad creative. This needs to be high-engagement and professional, with advanced motion graphics. If you have edited ads that performed well, tell me about it. Three things matter more than anything else: - Color grading. Everything I shoot is log. A clean, consistent, cinematic base is the foundation of all of it. - Sound design. Good audio is half of why an FPV one-take feels good. - Flow. Pacing, rhythm, how one shot hands off to the next. This is the part I cannot teach. Required — please do not apply unless all of these are true: - Fluent, natural spoken and written English. We will be on video calls together. This is not negotiable. - Extensive DaVinci Resolve experience, specifically grading log footage — node-based grading, color management, shot matching - Strong After Effects skills — motion graphics, motion tracking, masking - Gyroflow experience for FPV stabilization - Professional sound design ability. Not just adding a music track. - Prior US real estate video experience - Prior FPV or drone footage experience - Able to work from a written brief and hit deadlines without being chased - Reliable internet with solid upload speed, plus a backup connection Strongly preferred: - Real estate photo editing in an architectural or editorial style — HDR blending and luxury flambient work: natural warmth, sun flare on exteriors, sun rays through interior windows, sky replacement, twilight conversion - Graphic design on aerial stills — business callouts, street name overlays, lot line and property boundary overlays, satellite maps - Experience with motorsports, action, or automotive content What I provide: - Organized footage with selects marked, delivered by Google Drive or ---------- - A written brief for every project - Brand kit — LUTs, fonts, title and lower-third templates, music library - Fast, specific, technical feedback. Usually one or two rounds of notes per project. - Direction on brand and style, so you are never guessing what I want How pay works: - Paid every Friday, for the week just finished. No waiting on invoices. - I cover the transfer fees. The rate we agree on is exactly what lands in your account. - Hourly for the first month, then a flat weekly rate so your income is predictable. - Year-end bonus every December, 13th-month style, pro-rated for your first year. As a US client, I am not required to do this. I do it because I know it matters, and I budget for it from your first week. - Raises as you take on more, and a real path to full-time hours. I can pay through Wise, Payoneer, or OnlineJobs EasyPay — whichever is easiest for you. About the schedule: There is no fixed shift and you do not need to work US hours. I am in California, so I will usually send footage at the end of my day and review your work the next morning. I do need you reachable at some point during your own working day so questions do not sit for 24 hours. Otherwise, work when you work best. Philippine holidays: I do not set deadlines on your public holidays. Take them. Once you are on the flat weekly rate, a holiday week is paid the same as any other week. Just send me your dates in advance — and tell me early if a storm is likely to knock you offline, so I can plan around it instead of wondering where you went. How to apply — follow this exactly Applications that skip steps will not be read. That is intentional. Step 1. Start your message with the word VANTAGE. Step 2. Send links to your work. Please do not send a general agency showreel. I want to see three specific things: One FPV or drone piece you personally edited and graded — a one-take if you have one One example of motion-tracked graphics or an aerial map overlay One before/after of a log grade if you have it (ungraded log beside your final) For each link, tell me in one line what you personally did on it. Step 3. Answer these four questions. Short answers are completely fine. I am reading for whether you know the work, not for essay length. Walk me through your node structure when you grade a log clip in Resolve. How do you get to a neutral, correct base before you start building a creative look? What is your Gyroflow workflow? Tell me about a time the stabilization did not come out clean, and what you did about it. I want a lot line overlay and a street name that stay locked to the ground in a moving aerial shot. How do you build that in After Effects? A drone flies past a person who is talking. Describe what you are doing to the audio across those few seconds. Step 4. Tell me: Your rate expectation in USD per hour Your current availability in hours per week Who else you are currently working for, and how many hours you are committed to them Your internet upload speed The paid trial Shortlisted candidates do two short paid test edits using real footage from my projects — one FPV one-take, and one trending-style residential reel. They test different skills, so I need to see both. Each is a flat fee, paid on delivery. I never ask anyone to work for free. I read every application personally, and I reply to everyone who follows the steps above.
